column1: # HOTD2 function names — the committed source of truth for the Ghidra database.
# Addresses are virtual, lower-case hex, no 0x prefix.
# Regenerate from a live database with:   ./ghidra/run.sh export-annotations
# Replay onto a fresh import with:        ./ghidra/run.sh apply-annotations
# ApplyAnnotations only renames a symbol whose current name is still a Ghidra
# default (FUN_/SUB_/LAB_/DAT_/UNK_), so re-applying is idempotent and never
# clobbers a name a human chose in the GUI.
# Names recovered by Ghidra's own analysers (CRT, D3DX, Catch@/Unwind@) are
# deliberately NOT listed: auto-analysis recreates them on import.#
# **Rows are sorted by address, and every writer must keep them that way.**
# tools/annotate.py inserts in order; ExportAnnotations.java re-sorts on write.
# The file used to be append-only and grouped into topical sections, and both
# workstreams appending at the tail is where every TSV merge conflict came
# from -- two branches adding unrelated rows to the same last line. Sorted
# insertion puts them in different parts of the file instead. The sections
# went with it: each one spanned nearly the whole segment, so address order
# broke the twelve of them into 149 fragments.

column3: walks the region tables; the engine's only table-driven draw path
writes BAMS pitch/yaw; yaw = atan2(dx, dz)

Decompose the matrix stack's top rotation into a BAMS {pitch, yaw, roll} triple. Transforms (0,0,1) and hands it to VecToAngles for pitch and yaw; then transforms (1,0,0), cancels Rx(-pitch).Ry(-yaw) off it and takes fpatan of the result for roll. Read by RescueTargetHeldState (on the rescue) and by the stage-2 car rig FUN_00452320, whose wheels hang off a roll-limited copy of the body frame built from this triple.
matrix -> (rx, ry, rz) BAMS decomposition
atan2(|a x b|, a.b) for two vec3s, returned in BAMS. ComputeLookAtAngleError uses it to index the camera turn-rate curve, and TurnLookAtToward to size its slerp step.

dot(a,b)^2 / (|a|^2 * |b|^2), negated when the dot is negative -- the square of the cosine, never rooted. The camera hooks' `> 0.99999` convergence tests are against this value, so the threshold is about 0.18 degrees, not 0.26.
(num * b + den * a) / (num + den). CameraEaseBlockEyeToPathPose and CameraEaseEyeToPath call it with (1, 15) -- one sixteenth of the way from a to b per frame.

UpdateSceneViewAndLight() -- the per-frame scene update, run before anything draws. Three jobs.  1. For each of the two player camera blocks (base 0x009A6000, stride 0x69 dwords): build the view matrix from the block's position and its Y-then-X rotation, hand it to FUN_004A9BD0/FUN_004A8CA0, write the settled position back, then build the INVERSE (negated roll, X, Y, translation) into the block's second matrix slot. For the active player (g_current_player_view, DAT_009C6F00) it also transforms (0, DAT_009CA0E4, -1000) by that matrix and passes it to FUN_00403AC0.  2. MatrixStackSetTopFromArray(active view), then BuildSceneLightDirection(g_scene_light_pitch_bams, g_scene_light_yaw_bams, &g_scene_light_block0, &g_scene_light_dir_view) and SetRenderLightDirection(&g_scene_light_dir_view) -- note the VIEW-space vector is what reaches the device. FUN_0040E160 then rebuilds it again for the shadow/projection copy at 0x009A21E0.  3. **Latches the scene state**: g_scene_state_major_entered = g_scene_state_major and the same for minor. That is the pair IsPlayerAttackable reads, so 'entered' means 'as of the start of this frame's update', one frame behind a state change made during the frame. Finally bit 0 of DAT_009A5900 is set unless (major == 1 && DAT_009C8E98 != 5 && !(DAT_009A5900 & 0x30)).  The colour and ambient are NOT pushed here -- FUN_0040AD90 does that, with SetRenderLightColour/SetRenderAmbient, and SetLightingDefaultSingle turns them into the D3DLIGHT7.

EvtRunQueuedActions()  Drains the 16-slot ring of actions pushed by evt opcode 0x30 (queue_event). Each queued record is {?, selector, operand[...]}; the operands are copied to the scratch block at DAT_009A6184 (8 dwords) and the handler is fetched from a TWO-LEVEL table:      handler = table[selector >> 4][selector & 0xF]      /* table = 0x005776EC */  The high nibble is BOTH the group index and the operand count -- the instruction is `2 + (selector >> 4)` dwords -- so the groups are organised by arity. The index table has 7 slots, four of them null; the sub-tables are laid out immediately BEFORE it:      group 1 @ 0x005776C4  6 handlers  selectors 0x10 .. 0x15     group 2 @ 0x005776DC  2 handlers  selectors 0x20 .. 0x21     group 4 @ 0x005776E4  1 handler   selector  0x40     group 6 @ 0x005776E8  1 handler   selector  0x60  TEN handlers in total. An earlier note in the docs claimed "100+ scripted actions"; that was an overestimate and is wrong.      0x10  EvtActionSetPlayerFlag10      DAT_009A5EBC bit 0 = op0     0x11  EvtActionSceneState11         EvtEnterSceneState(cur_major, op0)     0x12  EvtActionSetUpdateRoutine12   DAT_009A5CE0 = PTR_FUN_00579E90[op0]     0x13  EvtActionSetContinuation13    per-player continuation = op0 ? .. : FUN_00420810     0x14  EvtActionSetGlobal14          DAT_009C6F00 = op0     0x15  EvtActionSetFlag15            DAT_009C6F33 = 1     0x20  EvtActionHoldCameraPreset20   op0 = frame countdown; each frame copy                                         6 dwords from 0x00576CF0 + op1*0x18                                         into the player's camera block     0x21  EvtActionFinishSequence21     EvtEnterSceneState(2, op0); DAT_009A5900 |= 1     0x40  EvtActionCamPlay40            PLAY A cam/ PATH -- see below     0x60  EvtActionStoreSixOperands60   copies 6 operands to DAT_009C6FD8..  Measured across stages 1-6: the only selectors that occur are exactly those ten (0x10 x3, 0x11 x4, 0x12 x2, 0x14 x2, 0x15 x6, 0x20 x1, 0x21 x418, 0x40 x751, 0x60 x13). 0x13 is defined but never used.  --- selector 0x40, the evt -> cam link -------------------------------------      queue_event 0x40, start_frame, end_frame, path_index, flags  EvtActionCamPlay40 -> CamStartPathPlayback -> CamAdvancePathFrame, which calls CamEvalPath7(DAT_009A2D78, (float)frame, &eye, &lookat, &roll, &_) once per frame and increments the frame counter until it passes end_frame.      start_frame == -1   resume from the current frame instead of seeking     flags & 2           defer: stash into DAT_009C70AC/B0 for a later 0x40     flags & 4           consume the stashed values instead of the operands  path_index is a GLOBAL index across every loaded cam/ file, not a per-file one. DAT_004C479C maps global index -> cam file id, and its run lengths are exactly the per-file path counts, cp_* first then op_*:      0..17 cp_demo(18)  18..28 cp_demo2(11)  29,30,31 (1 each)  32..54 cp_st1(23)     55..120 cp_st2(66) 121..162 cp_st3(42)  163..202 cp_st4(40)     203..216 cp_st5(14) 217..232 cp_st6(16) ... then the op_* files  VALIDATION: all 751 selector-0x40 instructions in stages 1-6 name a path inside their own stage's global range -- 751/751. A wrong operand order would scatter those indices across the whole 233-path space. See tools/verify_evt_cam.py.

The finish-sequence camera driver installed for scene state minors 4 and 6. Picks the camera mode into g_seq_camera_mode: mode 2 (return to path) only when the enemy count -- g_enemies_alive, or g_enemies_present when DAT_009C6F2E is 2 -- is zero AND no g_enemy_slots entry is claimed; otherwise 3 (track enemies). 6 when DAT_009CA094 is 1, and 7 when DAT_009C6F30 or DAT_009C6F32 is set. Clears g_camera_free and 0x009C6F2C on every frame the mode is not 2, and skips that clear in mode 2 so CameraTurnOntoPathTarget can latch the flag on convergence. Then dispatches through the camera-mode table at 0x00576CBC and writes g_cam_path_frame through __ftol.
Camera tick that eases the look-at onto the path's own target, then locks: once the dot product of desired and current exceeds 0.99999 it flips to evaluating the path straight into the camera block.

Camera mode 2's sub-handler 1. NOT what the old name CameraStartTurnOntoPathTarget claimed: the bytes at 0x00402867 are C6 05 2D 6F 9C 00 01, which writes g_camera_free = 1 -- the *path* branch -- along with 0x009C6F2C = 0. It abandons the turn after one damped step and hands the camera back to the path. It is also unreachable: its only reference is entry 1 of the sub-table at 0x00576CE0, selected by byte 0x009C6F2E, whose sole writer (0x0040322D) stores 0.

The gameplay camera. Calls SelectCameraLookAtTarget, eases the block's look-at onto the result with TurnLookAtToward, and takes the turn rate from ComputeLookAtAngleError while enemies are registered or a flat constant when none are.

The finish-sequence camera driver installed for scene state minor 7 (via DAT_00576B20[7] = FUN_00402DB0, which stores it into g_evt_action_handler). Two jobs: recompute g_camera_free from the four g_enemy_slots entries -- 1 unless one is claimed, and nothing else is tested -- then copy the six-dword deferred rail pose at 0x009C70C0 into g_camera_block_eye and the six at 0x009C70D8 into 0x009A60D8, and write g_cam_path_frame through __ftol. The strict mode selection lives in the sibling driver CameraDriverSelectMode, not here.
Eases the camera block's eye toward the path's eye channel at 1/16 per frame, leaving the look-at to the tracking code.

Eases g_camera_block_eye toward the deferred-rail pose eye at 0x009C70C0 by a sixteenth a frame while g_camera_ease_eye is set, and snaps straight to it otherwise. CameraTrackEnemiesTick opens with this.

Per frame: evaluates the active cam/ path's look-at into g_camera_lookat_target, then eases the camera block's current target (block+0xD8) toward it. The easing is why the pan is smooth rather than a snap.

Picks what the camera looks at. Walks g_enemy_slots; an enemy holding an attack permit (obj+0x121 != -1) is focused ALONE, otherwise the midpoint of two registered enemies is used, and with no enemies registered it falls back to the cam/ path's own target channel. This is the gameplay tracking camera.

One frame of a non-deferred cam_play, and the action handler EvtRunQueuedActions calls once per frame while the play is queued. Read from the instruction stream at 0x00403605..0x0040368D: cur = g_cam_path_cursor (+0x104); g_cam_path_frame (+0xD0) = cur; CamEvalPath7(g_active_cam_path, (float)cur, &g_camera_block_eye, &g_camera_block_target, &roll, &_); CamBlockSetAnglesFromLookAt(...); g_cam_path_frames_left = end - cur; if (cur >= end) { slot 0: g_queued_events_pending--, g_evt_action_advance = 1, cur++, return; else park the handler on NoOpStub } cur++.  **The publish, the curve evaluation and the block write all happen BEFORE the 'cur >= end' test that retires the action**, so the block holds the pose of the frame a shot ends on -- start..end inclusive, one frame each -- and only the frame AFTER the end is left unwritten. CameraPlayStashedPath (FUN_0040C8A0) and CameraStepRailTick (FUN_0040C790) are the deferred twins and increment first instead.
Installs CameraFollowPlayerMidpoint as the camera update hook, plus the per-player draw helper. One of eight installers that write g_camera_update_hook.
Installs CameraStepDeferredRailWithFrameExport as the camera update hook.

CamBlockSetAnglesFromLookAt(float *block_eye, float *block_target, float roll). Turns the camera block's eye/look-at pair into the block's own orientation words: VecToAngles(eye - target, &block[+0x8C], &block[+0x90]) then block[+0x94] = roll. Note the delta is eye MINUS target. CamAdvancePathFrame calls it immediately after CamEvalPath7 and before the end-of-path test, so the frame a shot ends on gets its angles written like any other.

Angle between the camera's current look direction and the desired one, clamped to 0x1FFF (45 deg) and used to index PTR_DAT_00576C04 -- the turn-rate curve, so a bigger swing turns at a different rate.

EvtEnterSceneState(int major, int minor)  The scene state machine. Records the state and immediately runs its installer:      DAT_009C6F14 = DAT_009C6F10 = minor;     DAT_009C6F0C = DAT_009C6F08 = major;     goto g_scene_state_table[major * 9 + minor];     /* 0x00576C14 */  The *9 is confirmed from the disassembly (LEA ECX,[ECX+EAX*8]; ADD EAX,ECX), not from the decompiler. FUN_00403BB0 is the same without the DAT_009C6F08/10 backup copies.  A cell does not do work -- it INSTALLS the hooks for that phase:      _DAT_009C7080              camera update, run each frame by CameraUpdateTick     _DAT_009A5CDC/_DAT_009A5E0C   per-player update  (P1 / P2, 0x130 apart)     _DAT_009A5CE0/_DAT_009A5E10   per-player sub-routine                                (also writable from script: queue_event 0x12)  6 rows x 9 columns. Unused cells point at SceneStateInvalidHang (0x00402710), which is `while(1);` -- an invalid transition DELIBERATELY LOCKS UP, so the live cells below are an exact statement of which states exist.       min:   0        1        2        3        4        5        6      7    8  maj 0 |  none      -        -        -        -        -        -      -    -  maj 1 |   -     follow    none+B   viewang     -        -        -      -    -  maj 2 |   -        -        -        -      snap     shake   stash+f stash  -  maj 3 |   -        -        -        -        -        -        -      -    -  maj 4 | nop x6 ..............................          -        -      -  0x402720  maj 5 | 402890     -      NULL    420810    402A40     -      402740 402860 402740  Camera hooks installed by rows 0-2, all writing the same six globals -- DAT_009C71E0/E4/E8 eye xyz, DAT_009C71EC/F0/F4 pitch/yaw/roll (BAMS):    (0,0) 0x00403970  no camera hook (the do-nothing stub)   (1,1) 0x00403980  CameraFollowPlayerMidpoint  -- midpoint of the two players,                     or player DAT_009C7000 alone when DAT_009C8E80 == 1   (1,2) 0x004039A0  no camera hook, but installs the player-B sub-routine   (1,3) 0x004039D0  CameraFromViewAngles -- builds the pose from the view                     struct by RotateY(yaw-0x8000)/RotateX(-pitch)/roll and a                     (0,-15,0) translate   (2,4) 0x00403A00  CameraSnapToPathEye -- snap to the cam/ path eye, then                     re-install itself as 0x0040C470 for following frames   (2,5) 0x00403A30  CameraPathWithImpulseShake -- path pose plus a 30-frame                     decaying impulse, gated on _DAT_009C9028 & 0x20000   (2,6) 0x00403A60  CameraPlayStashedPathPublishFrame   (2,7) 0x00403A90  CameraPlayStashedPath  (2,6) and (2,7) both call CamEvalPath7(g_active_cam_path, frame, ...) directly, stepping DAT_009C70AC toward DAT_009C70B0 -- and those are exactly the globals that EvtActionCamPlay40's `flags & 2` branch (FUN_00403490) stashes. So `queue_event 0x40` with bit 1 set defers a path, and camera state (2,6)/(2,7) is what plays it. They differ only by `<` vs `<=` on the end frame and whether the current frame is published to _DAT_009C709C.  Three of the camera hooks share this, which fixes two script opcodes:      if (DAT_009C70F4 == 1) eye.y = DAT_009C8E58;      /* fixed height   */     else                   eye.y = path.y - 15.0f;    /* path-relative  */  DAT_009C8E58 is written by evt opcode 0x1A and DAT_009C70F4 by opcode 0x36, so 0x1A sets a fixed camera eye height and 0x36 selects it.  VALIDATION [measured]: every state transition in the shipped scripts lands on a live cell. `queue_event` selector 0x21 (finish_sequence) always passes major = 2, and its 444 operands across all stages are only 4, 6 and 7 -- inside row 2's live set {4,5,6,7}. Selector 0x11 passes the current major with operands 1 and 3, inside row 1's live set {1,2,3}. A wrong row width would put these on the hang loop.
Rotates a look-at point toward a desired one by num/(num+rate) of the angle between them and re-emits it at a fixed 100-unit radius from the eye. Rate 0 snaps; larger is slower.
Loads the stashed path id and frame for the current branch variable and evaluates it into the camera block.

Bind one loaded cam/ file's paths into the global 0..417 path-slot space.  Walks the file's offset table and the EXE slot list in lockstep, so path k of a file is global slot slot_list[k]:      slot = *psVar3++;                                   // s16[] at 0x004C470C     *(int *)(&DAT_0059C9F8 + slot * 8) = *piVar4++ + DAT_0059C9EC;     (&DAT_0059C9FC)[slot * 4] = 2;  i.e. descriptor_ptr = file_base + offset_table[k]. Count comes from the u16 table at 0x004C476C. The 0x10-byte per-file record at 0x0059D708 gets its state word (+8) set to 2; its +0 is the raw allocation and its +4 the curve base, both filled by the loader at 0x00403F75/0x00403F9E as file_base + 4 + path_count*4.  NOTE FOR THE FORMAT: this performs NO fixup, relocation or decode of the curve payload. The file arrives by a plain CreateFileA / GetFileSize / ReadFile / CloseHandle into a 32-byte-aligned buffer, and CamEvalHermiteCurve then reads those bytes as floats. So the bytes on disk are the bytes the game evaluates -- which is what establishes that the smashed 0xFF bytes in cp_st1/cp_demo/cp_title/cp_st3 are a data defect and not a misparse. See docs/re/anomalies.md.  CamEvalPath7 takes the descriptor pointer from this table but the curve base from SLOT_TO_CAM (0x004C479C) instead; the two tables agree for all 418 slots.

Evaluate one cam/ Hermite curve at time param_2.  param_1 is the curve header as a ushort*: [0] = key_count (always a power of two), [1] = search_steps (its log2). Keys follow at byte +4, 16 bytes each.  The indexing pins the layout beyond doubt. *(float *)(param_1 + i*8 + 2) is byte i*16 + 4 -- key i's first field -- and it is what the binary search compares against, so field 0 is TIME. With pfVar1 = &key[i].field0:      pfVar1[ 1]  key[i].value           -> weight  3s^2/h^2 - 2s^3/h^3     pfVar1[-3]  key[i-1].value         -> weight  2s^3/h^3 - 3s^2/h^2 + 1     pfVar1[ 3]  key[i].tangent_in      -> weight  s^3/h^2 - s^2/h     pfVar1[-2]  key[i-1].tangent_out   -> weight  s^3/h^2 - 2s^2/h + s     pfVar1[-4]  key[i-1].time  so the key is {time, value, tangent_out, tangent_in} at a 16-byte stride, and tangents are in value-per-unit-time. Textbook cubic Hermite.  There is no masking, no sentinel test and no integer path: whatever bytes are in the file are read as floats. Combined with the loader doing a plain ReadFile and CamBindPathSlots doing no payload fixup, that is what proves the smashed 0xFF bytes in cp_st1/cp_demo/cp_title/cp_st3 are evaluated by the shipped game too. See docs/re/anomalies.md.  The search cannot leave the key array, so times outside the curve extrapolate along the end segments rather than clamping.
writes {float x,y,z; int rx,ry,rz}; Ghidra types all six as float and is wrong
consumes the shot-test list, per player

The first test every registered object gets, and for most classes the ONLY one. RayTestSphere(player, obj+0x70, obj+0x74, obj+0x78, obj+0x124) against the point RegisterForShotTest published and the radius at obj+0x124; on a hit it forks: if obj+0x34 bit 0x80 is set AND g_character_skeletons[obj+0x1F4] has nodes AND bit 0x8000 is clear it hands over to ShotTestSkeleton and the shot is resolved bone by bone, and otherwise THE WHOLE ACTOR IS ONE CANDIDATE -- its +0x70/74/78 and its flags go into the candidate list at 0x0059F4DC and the nearest wins. So a class with no skeleton is hit as a single sphere and needs no bones at all, which is what makes class 0x52's mouse shootable: MouseInit sets obj+0x124 = 2.0 and nothing else. ProcessPlayerShots picks this arm when obj+0x34 bit 0x10 is clear and ShotTestMesh when it is set.
walks g_pCharacterSkeletons[char_type] -- the SAME tree the renderer draws through
per bone: sphere, or mesh when record+0x88 != -1; recurses into children
ray vs the bone's hit sphere from g_pBoneHitSpheres, appended to g_coli_candidates
precise test against the bone's own collision mesh in its local space
origin -> origin + direction * 1000
the miss: ColiSegmentVsMesh against the full and ray-only collision sets
sets obj+0x34 |= 8 and the shooter bit

Appends the actor to the per-frame list at 0x0059D8E8: {obj, obj+0x34, obj+0x12C, +0x130, +0x134}, stride 5 dwords. Skipped when obj+0x34 bit 0x8000 is set, and taken only when bit 0x10 is set or obj+0x78 <= 0 -- and obj+0x78 is the VIEW-SPACE z, so that half is a behind-the-camera cull. ActorDespawn (FUN_00409CC0) sets obj+0x34 |= 0x80018000, so an object that despawned earlier in the same frame still reaches its own call and the append silently does not happen; three of the class 0x41 routines are written exactly that way. It feeds two consumers, not one: the gunshot hit test, and -- after ColiPublishDynamicList copies it to 0x005A30A0 -- ColiTestSphereAgainstActors, the actor-versus-actor push. So a class that never calls this takes no part in separating a crowd. The bit 0x10 also picks WHICH shot test ProcessPlayerShots runs: clear goes to ShotTestSphere and set to ShotTestMesh.
A shot that hit the world: takes the surface material from the collision hit record (+0x30) and spawns the matching sprite and sound.

Copies the registration list at 0x0059D8E8 to the dynamic list at 0x005A30A0 that ColiTestSphereAgainstActors walks, five dwords per entry. The two-buffer split is what lets the push test a snapshot of the frame's spheres rather than a list being appended to while it reads.

The actor-versus-actor sphere test. Walks the per-frame dynamic list at 0x005A30A0 (stride 5 dwords, {ptr, ?, x, y, z}), skipping the caller and anything carrying obj+0x34 bits 0x80008000 or 0x10, and lazily filling obj+0x128 from obj+0x124 for an actor whose class never set a body radius. Overlap is centre-to-centre against the SUM of the radii and the nearest candidate wins. It does not move the actor it finds: it writes the OPPOSITE push onto it -- obj+0x138 = me, obj+0x13C = depth, obj+0x140..0x148 = -normal -- and that actor applies it on its own next frame, so one test per actor separates a whole crowd.
unprojects the crosshair with g_projection_distance_px (640.21) and writes the per-player shot record at g_ShotRecords
rotates the centre into the shot frame with the precomputed sin/cos and compares the perpendicular distance to the radius

The task SpawnBoneHitSprite starts: draws asset slot 0x3A + cel at the posed position of bone task+0x48 of actor task+0x34 (the bone record's +0x274/+0x278/+0x27C/+0x284), scaled by depth -- 1.0 beyond -20 units, otherwise 0.25 - z*0.0375 -- and then by 0.15 with g_wCaptionMode 1 or 0.3 without. Steps the cel and kills itself past 0x18, so it is 25 frames long. What the 25 slots from 0x3A are is [open].

ActorAlloc(BoneHitSpriteDrawAndTick, 0x50) with the actor at task+0x34, the bone index at task+0x48 and the cel counter at task+0x44 = 0. Called once per hit bone by OneHitTargetUpdate. Renderer-only.
The blood flipbook: AssetDrawSlot(frame + 0x3A) for 25 frames at the hit bone, in view space, scaled (-view_z*0.0375 + 0.25) * 0.3 * severity.
Spawn the blood flipbook at a bone. Arg 3 is the severity scale ActorShotFeedback picks: 0.5 damaged, 0.75 damaged and swapped, 1.0 severed.
billboarded sprite-animation effect by kind

SpawnSpriteEffectFromParams(params) -- allocate one sprite-effect actor and start it.  The body behind SpawnSpriteEffect (FUN_00407340), which has 37 callers and does nothing but marshal a position/facing pair plus a kind into the 12-float parameter block, passing -1.0 at params[6] for "no scale override". FUN_004073A0 is a bare pass-through with 5 more callers.  Algorithm: ActorAlloc(LAB_00407A70, 0x68); position from params[0..2]; facing from params[3..4], recomputed toward g_camera_block_eye when params[10] != 0; kind byte params[9] stored at +0x5C; a switch on the kind fills the texture range [+0x60, +0x64] and the base scale +0x50. Kinds 1/2/3/5/6 are the collision materials (sand, metal, other, water, wood); 0x53 also seeds +0x4C from rand(); 0x5A recurses twice to spawn kinds 0x5B and 0x5C. Then a distance-based scale law (kind 'S' out to -35, everything but 'c' out to -15) and PlayImpactSoundForMaterial(kind).  Parameters: params -- 12 floats, built by the caller. Returns: nothing.  Named SpriteEffectSlotRange in ghidra/annotations until 2026-09-03, which described only the switch; docs/formats/combat.md called this address SpawnImpactSprite, which described only the material cases and collided with the wrapper's own name. It spawns, and impact is one of its kinds.
Collision material -> ricochet sound. The filenames it resolves to are what name the materials: 1 sand, 2 metal, 3 other, 5 water, 6 wood.

The per-frame body of the object SpawnSpriteEffectFromParams allocates, and the whole of what a sprite effect is. Draws AssetDrawSlot(+0x60) under translate(+0x38..+0x40) * RotY(+0x48) * RotX(+0x44) * RotZ(+0x4C) * scale(+0x50/+0x54/+0x58) in draw layer 0xE, then +0x60 += 1 and dies once it passes the last slot at +0x64 -- so the flipbook is one asset slot per frame at 60 Hz and its length is last - first + 1. Kind 'P' (0x50) draws under light colour (1.0, 0.3, 0.0) and kind 'S' (0x53) under (0.85, 0.85, 0.75) at three quarters scale until its cursor reaches 0x129.

On DAT_009C8E98 == 6 only, spawns a 120-frame flat ground ring at the actor's shadow anchor obj+0x100/+0x108 and the ground height plus 0.05. Draws asset slot 0x1A38 scaled in X and Z only, expanding from 0 to 4x over its life through cos at 136.5333 BAMS a frame.
obj+0x1390 is a PARENT ACTOR here, not a descriptor tail

Event opcodes 0x01-0x04: run the spawn only in a one-player game.    if (g_max_attackers == 1) jmp g_evt_spawn_gated_handlers[g_evt_opcode];   else                      skip the -1-terminated operand list;  g_evt_spawn_gated_handlers (0x00577650) is indexed by the *opcode*, so 0x01 -> EvtOpSpawnPlaced09, 0x02 -> EvtOpSpawnSimple0A, 0x03 -> EvtOpSpawnObj0B,    0x04 -> EvtOpSpawnObjC0C. The descriptor list is therefore identical to the ungated opcode it forwards to; only the gate is new. EvtOpSpawnIfTwoPlayers (0x00408860) is the same routine testing 2.  g_max_attackers is the count of players currently in play (raised in FUN_00414770 for a player state flagged 0x20, lowered in FUN_00414280), so "mode" here means the live player count, not a difficulty or game mode.  Only 0x03/0x04 and 0x07/0x08 are ever encoded by a shipped script.

Event opcodes 0x05-0x08: run the spawn only in a two-player game.  Identical to EvtOpSpawnIfOnePlayer (0x00408820) but testing g_max_attackers == 2. The forward table g_evt_spawn_gated_handlers repeats the same four entries at indices 5-8, so 0x05 -> EvtOpSpawnPlaced09, 0x06 -> EvtOpSpawnSimple0A, 0x07 -> EvtOpSpawnObj0B, 0x08 -> EvtOpSpawnObjC0C.  Stage 1 block 0 step 2 pairs them: 0x07 lists three class-0x30 zombies and 0x03 lists the last two of the same three, so the second player adds one zombie to the stage's opening encounter.
alloc 0x13F4; reads desc+0x24/+0x25 inline; does NOT set obj+0x1390

obj+0x34 = the spawn record's flags word | 1, and obj+0x38 = 0. Run by SpawnFromDescriptor BEFORE the class's own Init, which then ORs its bits on top. This is where the descriptor's flags become the actor's: bit 15 takes it out of the shot test and the crowd push, bit 17 skips the per-frame ground snap in ZombiePushOutOfWorldAndActors so a spawn placed on a ledge stays on it (95 spawns), bit 18 tells EnemyZombieInit not to compute the aim angles, bit 27 picks between row[2] and row[3] (155 spawns), and bit 14 freezes the pose. Bits 1 and 2 are consumed rather than kept: EnemyZombieInitByCharType (0045300B, 00453045) clears each and raises obj+0x38 bit 0x10 or 0x20 in its place, which it has to, because bits 1 and 2 of obj+0x34 are what MarkActorShot writes to name the player who fired. Bit 1 is the stationary thrower's do-not-walk-away and EXACTLY TWO shipped records set it, stage 3 block 2's two axe men (evt 0x3078 and 0x30BC, 0x20002); bit 2 is set by three stage-2 class-0x30 records. Bit 23 (0x800000) is a read-only spawn bit: NOTHING in .text writes it -- an exhaustive scan of every encoding that can set bit 23 of the dword at +0x34 finds no site -- and its five readers all ask the same question, skip the NoCameraTrack raise and the g_enemy_slots clear when this actor is the last enemy. Six shipped spawns carry it, all class 0x30 initial state 18: three in stage 1 (char type 7) and three in stage 3 (char type 11, 0x8800000). Bit 3 (0x8) is class 0x30's ride-the-carrier bit: EnemyZombieInitByCharType (0045301D) reads it and re-reads the descriptor's position and yaw as an offset on g_carrier_object, see ZombieAttachToCarrier. EXACTLY FOUR shipped records set it, all class 0x30, all st5evtbl block 2 step 2 op 38 (0x1D44, 0x1D74, 0x1DA4, 0x1DD4; init_flags 0x20008 and 0x60008). Unlike bits 1 and 2 it is NOT cleared, so it stays readable on obj+0x34.

Event opcode 0x0A, and its operands are NOT the 0x24-byte placement descriptor the other spawn opcodes use: each points at a two-word record {class, hp}. The object is allocated from g_class_handlers[class] at 0x13F4 bytes, initialised by FUN_00408970, and both obj+0x11C and obj+0x11E take the second word as a SIGNED 16-BIT store, so the shipped 0xFFFF0000 is a zero. Nothing writes a position, so this is the opcode for objects that place themselves. All four records the shipped scripts name live in comevtbl.bin -- classes 0x60 (chapter card), 0x61 (result card), 0x62 (its tally) and 0x63 (the subtitle gate) -- which is why every stage names the same four addresses 0x00977234/3C/44/4C; stage 6 adds three stage-local records. Ported: script/ops/spawn.ts places them and game/class60/, game/class61/ run the two that raise a script flag.

opcodes 0x0B/0x0D; alloc 0x13F4; obj+0x1390 = descriptor + 0x24. Also copies the u16 at descriptor+0x20 into obj+0x1316 (MOV word ptr [ESI + 0x1316], AX -- 66898616130000 at 0x00408A77), which EnemyThrowerInit and EnemyZombieInit both read as their class's second flag word. tools/hod2lib/evt.py calls that word 'unused in every shipped file'; it is not -- 23 of 51 class-0x31 and 76 of 345 class-0x30 spawn descriptors set it, including five stage-6 class-0x31 spawns that carry surface bits 0x40/0x80/0x100.
opcode 0x0C; alloc 0x1314; obj+0x130C = descriptor + 0x24
Clears g_enemy_slots, the 16-entry {u8 occupied; void *actor} table the tracking camera reads.
Rebuilds g_enemy_slots each frame from the radix-sorted candidate list: enemies holding an attack permit take slots 0 and 1, everyone else fills from slot 2.
Takes the first free general slot, 2..13; slots 0 and 1 are reserved for enemies holding an attack permit. The slot index is kept in obj+0x120.

Adds an actor to the camera candidate list unless obj+0x34 bit 0x10000 is set -- which ZombieStateApproach sets while walking and clears when the actor wins an attack permit, so only committed enemies are ever tracked. Key is (int)(|actor - camera eye| * 10.0). ITS XREF LIST IS INCOMPLETE IN GHIDRA AND THE MISSING CALLER IS THE IMPORTANT ONE: get_xrefs_to 0x00408ec0 returns eleven sites and not one of them is an enemy class, which reads as proof that class 0x30 and 0x31 are never camera candidates. They are. ActorRegisterCameraPoint (FUN_00409B70) ends PUSH ESI / CALL 0x00408ec0 at 0x00409bec..0x00409c03, AFTER the JMP to MatrixStackPop that Ghidra has marked no-return -- so the function body, the decompilation and the xref all stop at the tail call, and disassemble_bytes past 0x00409bec is what finds it. EnemyZombieUpdate (FUN_004533F0) makes that call every frame with a 4.0 lift.
LSD radix sort, two 8-bit passes, over the {distance key, actor} candidate list -- nearest first.
Adds a live, not-yet-dead actor to the distance-ranked enemy list, at most 14.

Once a frame: sorts the registration list by distance to the camera and writes **two** different ranks. Pass one: obj+0x131D gets the raw distance rank, nearest first, and obj+0x131E is set to 0xE. Then entries that are not live, or that carry obj+0x34 bit 0x20000000 -- which ZombieStateBackOff sets while it retreats -- are dropped, and pass two numbers the survivors 0, 1, 2 into obj+0x131E. So the compacted rank is the queue with the retreating actors taken out, and it is what the '< 3' cap tests, while the ring allowance tests the raw one. The list holds fourteen; a fifteenth enemy is never ranked and keeps 0xFF, which reads as -1 and passes every test.

A radix sort over the distance-rank registration list: two 8-bit passes on the u16 key at DAT_005A4D58, moving the {key, actor} pairs through the scratch at DAT_005A4E38 and back. Called by RankEnemiesByDistance and nothing else; it only orders, it does not move anyone.
14-slot table at g_hit_slots; sets obj+0x38 |= 0x40
Frees this actor's camera slot: g_enemy_slots[obj+0x120] = 0, obj+0x120 = 0xFF.

The one and only caller of ResolveHit (FUN_00409430) in the image -- one xref -- and the gate on it. ChooseHitPlayerOrder first, then for each player in g_hit_player_order whose bit is up in obj+0x34: g_hit_bone[p] = (s8)obj+0x190+p, and ResolveHit runs ONLY if obj+0x34 bit 0x100 is clear (00409336 8b4834 MOV ECX,[EAX+0x34] / 00409339 f6c501 TEST CH,0x1 / 0040933c 750e JNZ 0040934c, which lands past the CALL at 0040933f). So an actor the class has made shot-immune -- a thrower down or getting up, a zombie emerging or frozen on a cue -- takes NO damage at all: not reduced damage, and not a hit resolved and then discarded. The shot still marks the actor and still gets feedback, which is where ThrowerShotFeedback's forced g_hit_result = 5 comes from. It then clears bit 3 of the bone record's +0x280 and both the per-player bit and obj+0x34 bit 3.
picks which players resolve, randomising the order in two-player

body-part and damage tables indexed by actor type. Reads g_app_state (0x009C8E98) TWICE, and both reads are about being out of play. At 0x00409495, when g_app_state != 6 it raises obj+0x34 |= 0xE00 on the actor being hit (a1988e9c00 / 83f806 / 7409 / 8b4734 / 80cc0e / 894734) -- three bits with three readers: 0x200 makes ActorSwapDamagedPart return before it does anything (f6c502 at 0x00409916), 0x400 skips both the sever arm (f6c604 at 0x004095BD) and the torso death-wound arm (f6c404 at 0x004096C0), and 0x800 forces g_hit_result to 0 (f6c508 at 0x004096F9). At 0x00409741 the 1-in-4 head pop on the killing shot is gated on g_app_state == 6 (833d988e9c0006 / 756c), so the head only comes off in play. Neither read fires during ordinary play; both hold in the attract demo, which is g_app_state 5.
per-bone, per-difficulty addend from g_pBoneDamageByRank
decrements obj+0x11C only

writes the effect slot into record[0] -- the slot the bone DRAWS -- so a hit replaces that body part. Refuses outright when g_cur_actor's obj+0x34 bit 0x200 is set: 00409913 8b4834 MOV ECX,[EAX+0x34] / 00409916 f6c502 TEST CH,0x2 / 00409919 757f JNZ (the epilogue), which skips the swap, the obj+0x78 clear and the obj+0x1318 zone bit. Only ResolveHit's out-of-play OR of 0xE00 raises 0x200; no shipped spawn record carries it.
gives the swapped part its own hit sphere from the TAIL of g_pBoneHitSpheres, past bone_count-1 entries, terminated by slot == -1
Search g_character_skeletons[char_type] for the node whose bone index (+0x14) is the argument. Starts at the root's children, so the root itself is never returned.
Recursive half of FindSkeletonNodeForBone. Node layout: +0x14 u16 bone, +0x16 u16 child count, +0x18 child pointers.

Run when a bone reaches its sever step (effect-table next == 1, or a torso hit that kills). Calls RemoveBoneSubtree on every CHILD of that bone -- the bone itself keeps the stump model ActorSwapDamagedPart just gave it, and everything below it disappears.

Sets the destroyed-zone bit in obj+0x1318, zeroes the bone's draw slot (rec+0x00) and rec+0x78, then recurses into its children. A zero draw slot is both invisible and unshootable: ShotTestBoneTree tests `if (rec[0] != 0)`.

Transforms obj+0x100 into view space for the shot test, runs RegisterForShotTest, then **raises obj+0x104 by its float argument** -- 4.0 for a class-0x30 zombie, 0 for a class-0x31 thrower -- and registers the actor for camera tracking. So the point the camera follows is the tracked bone lifted by four.

Projects the actor's tracked view-space point at obj+0x70/74/78 by g_projection_distance_px and asks whether it lands inside the frame -- half-width g_projection_distance_px * 0.5, half-height a literal 240. TryClaimAttackSlot calls it before handing out a permit, so an enemy off the side of the screen cannot start an attack, nor sit on the one permit while it is out of shot.

Writes one byte -- 0 or 1, and nothing else is accepted -- into every part of a skinned-model record: model+0x3C parts, the byte at model+0x40 + i*8 - 7. The blinking corpse states are what call it, once per frame, with the parity of their own countdown.

Traces a vertical segment from (x, y-1000, z) up to (x, y, z) and returns g_coli_hit_surface -- the surface-type id, 0 for a miss. The sibling of QueryGroundHeightAt, which returns the height. Callers test 0x35, 0x37, 5 and 0x5A.

May an enemy commit an attack on this player? Three clauses, in order: g_scene_state_major_entered (0x009C6F08) must be 2 -- the cam/ path camera row, so no attack lands during the follow camera or a scripted view-angle turn; then g_app_state == 5 returns TRUE unconditionally, which is the ATTRACT-MODE override (the demo has no real player, so its g_player_state is never 5 and the demo would otherwise never be attacked); otherwise g_player_state[player * 0x98] must be 5. It does NOT test g_player_invuln_frames: the 90-frame window after a hit stops the damage and nothing else, so enemies keep taking their turns through it. Called with -1 by TryClaimAttackSlot and the scripted attackers, which in the engine reads g_player_state - 0x130 bytes and relies on that not being 5.

Step an angle toward another by at most *rate* BAMS per frame -- a rate limit, not an ease. ZombieStateHoldAtRange and ZombieStateWaitTurn pass 0x40 and ZombieStateBackOff -0x40, which is a third of a degree a frame: slow enough that a retreating actor cannot whip round when it passes the point it is turning relative to.
TurnActorTowardCamera without the 1.5-unit forward offset: eases the actor's yaw toward the camera eye itself.
Eases the actor's yaw (obj+0x68) toward a point 1.5 units in front of the camera.
Eases the actor's yaw toward the direction (actor - point), the mirror of TurnActorTowardCamera. ZombieStateBackOff passes the position the strike started from.

TurnActorAwayFromPoint that also reports arrival: steps obj+0x68 at most the step argument in BAMS toward the heading atan2(obj - point), then returns FUN_0040A040(new yaw, target, tolerance) -- 1 when the yaw is now within the tolerance of the target. Ghidra types it void; the value falls through EAX. ThrowerStateStandAndDecide calls it with step and tolerance both 0x200 and uses both senses: non-zero advances the sub-state, and later not-1 resets it.

Sets up a ballistic arc from a per-frame downward ACCELERATION rather than a duration: counts the frames out by stepping v -= a, y += v until the height has passed the destination's, then writes obj+0x5C = -a, zeroes obj+0x58 and obj+0x60, and sets the flat x and z speeds to the distance over that count and the initial y speed to (n*n*a + 2*dy) / 2n. ZombieStateDelayedLeap is the caller; the frame count lands in obj+0x1330.

Spawns the flying head the 1-in-4 headshot burst throws. NOT a blood spray, which is what docs/formats/combat.md called it until 2026-09-04 -- it is ActorAlloc(SeveredHeadUpdate, 0x1A8), an independent object with its own per-frame routine. Seeds +0x40..0x48 from the actor's obj+0x394 head point transformed through the camera block's matrix, +0x64/+0x68 from obj+0x330/+0x334 (the initial pitch and yaw), and +0x1A4 = the head asset slot the caller passes from obj+0x32C. Draw scale +0x118 is 1.0, or 2.0 in Original Mode with the big-head item (DAT_009C88A8) unless the character type is 0xE, which takes 1.8.

The flying head's per-frame routine, three sub-states at +0x194. Launch (0): gravity +0x5C = -0.0204166, up speed +0x50 = (rand()%20 + 1)*0.01 + 0.3, and a horizontal push of 0.2 along the camera's own yaw -- MatrixRotateY(g_camera_block+0xD0) applied to (0, 0, -0.2) -- so the head always flies AWAY from the viewer. Two spin rates, +0x19C yaw with a random sign and +0x1A0 pitch, both rand()%0x800 + 0x800 BAMS a frame. Falling (1): QueryGroundHeightAt each frame; on contact y snaps to the ground, the vertical speed is negated and scaled by 0.25 -- a bounce -- FUN_00408370 marks the ground at 0.25, and the sound is 0x1116A9 for head slots 0x2015/0x1DC1, else 0x4416A9 on a wet surface (g_coli_hit_surface 0x37 or 5) and 0x2616A9 otherwise. Once |vy| <= 0.15 it settles: velocities zeroed, FUN_00408370 at 0.5, and 0x78 frames on the clock. Settled (2): sinks 0.04 a frame while both spins decay by a tenth, then frees itself. Draws AssetDrawSlot(+0x1A4) under translate, rotateY(yaw), rotateX(pitch) and the +0x118 scale.

Picks the ground-shadow ellipse size by character type -- 50x30 for types 0x44 and 0x47, 11x10 for everything else -- and calls ActorDrawGroundShadow. Skipped when obj+0x34 bit 0x80000 is set or obj+0x1F8 bit 0 is clear.

Draws asset slot 0x10D0 as a flattened ellipse on the ground under the actor. The height comes from QueryGroundHeightAt(x, y+3, z) when obj+0x1F8 bit 2 is set, from obj+0x44 otherwise, and from g_camera_fixed_eye_y while g_app_state is 0x0D.

Two sounds per event: a flesh impact from g_hit_voice_table[0..4] and a voice from one of two sets, chosen by character type. Kind 0 hurt, 1 killed, 2 headshot kill -- AND kind 3, which is the ATTACK CRY and is neither: it plays a single sound, coin-flipped within its set's own pair, and no impact. The set split is the switch at 0x0040A6F5 over obj+0x1F4: types 0, 2, 5, 6, 9, 0x0E, 0x0F, 0x10 and 0x11 take set A, every other type set B. TWENTY-THREE CALL SITES, AND THE CENSUS IS COMPLETE: kind 0 at 0045402D, 00449D11, 00452608, 00451A03; kind 1 at 0045264E, 00449A8B, 00451AF0; kind 2 at 00449A7E; 00453F7A is 2 when the hit result is 2 and 1 otherwise; and thirteen kind-3 sites -- 00454136 (ActorShotFeedback, gated on bone 2's draw slot being 0x1DC2, the head prop it then swaps for 0x1DC1), 0045EA4F, 004592B0, 00449C19, 0044B709, 0044EC02, 0044F157, 0045AE84, 0045E496, 0044C21D, 00455B8A, 0045AFF0, 00450C30, 0045843C. NOTHING PASSES 4. Kind 4's two ids live at g_actor_voice_kind4 (0x005A4EA8), both zero in the image and written by nothing, so kind 4 reaches PlaySoundId(0) and that early-outs: the arm is dead code and porting it is porting silence. None of the five kinds is an idle noise -- all five fire on an event. The standing groan is ZombieStateHoldAtRange's PlaySoundId(0x1917A9) at 004558D6 and the held-weapon loop is EnemyZombieInitByCharType's at 0045314F, neither of them this routine.
Returns g_damage_rank, the 0..15 adaptive rank DamageRankModifier indexes. NOT g_difficulty.
adds the difficulty delta to obj+0x11E, clamps [1,300], copies to obj+0x11C
fills the 112-slot array from the {class,handler} pairs

LZSS decompressor. Returns the number of bytes written to dst.  Called by every pol/ and tex/ asset loader. On disk a compressed file is a u32 uncompressed-size header followed by the bitstream; callers read that header themselves and pass src = file + 4.  Format ------ Flag bits are read LSB-first from the same byte stream that carries the literal and match payload bytes, so a payload byte may be fetched while a flag byte is still partly consumed. A fresh flag byte is loaded only when its 8-bit budget is exhausted.    while flag bit == 1:        emit one literal byte   flag bit == 0, a match follows:       next bit == 1  -> long form           u16 w           w == 0                -> END OF STREAM           offset = (w >> 3) - 8192      (13-bit, always negative)           n      = w & 7           length = n + 2                if n != 0           length = u8 + 1               if n == 0       next bit == 0  -> short form           two bits, MSB first   -> n           offset = u8 - 256             (8-bit, always negative)           length = n + 2  Window is 8192 bytes. Matches are copied one byte at a time from dst+offset, so overlapping copies are intentional and an offset of -1 is a legal run fill.  Verified: reimplemented in tools/hod2lib/lz.py and run against all 793 compressed assets. Every one produces exactly the byte count its header declares. Spec in docs/formats/lz.md.

PushSceneLightStateToDevice() -- the object entry point FUN_0040AE60 installs with ActorAlloc(FUN_0040AD90, 0x34), so it runs once a frame. It pushes the whole scene light state to the device: the nine per-channel setters FUN_0040B0A0..FUN_0040B390 for light block 0 and again for block 1, then PushSceneFogFromLightBlock(&DAT_009A357C, &DAT_009A357A, g_scene_fog_near, g_scene_fog_far), SetRenderLightColour(g_scene_light_colour_r/g/b) and SetRenderAmbient(g_scene_light_ambient). This and SetupSceneProjection (through FUN_0040C2E0) are the only two callers of the fog push, and neither transforms the near/far -- they are eye-space depths and the view matrix that draws a triangle is what they are relative to.
evt opcode 0x20's dispatch entry: ApplyLightChannelOperand(0), i.e. the every-frame light block. Opcode 0x24 is the block-1 twin and 0x21/0x23 (and 0x25/0x27) are the rate and time tween forms.

ApplyLightChannelOperand(block) -- the body of evt opcodes 0x20/0x24 (set a light-block channel). **This switch is the authoritative channel map**, and it is dword offsets into the block, not inference from a seeding function:  case 0 -> block[0x0C] = g_scene_fog_near        (+0x30)  case 1 -> block[0x0D] = g_scene_fog_far         (+0x34)  case 2 -> block[0x09] = g_scene_fog_r           (+0x24)  case 3 -> block[0x0A] = g_scene_fog_g           (+0x28)  case 4 -> block[0x0B] = g_scene_fog_b           (+0x2C)  case 5 -> writes [9] and [10] then FALLS THROUGH into case 4, so it is the  all-three-fog-components alias  case 6 -> block[0x90] = g_scene_light_colour_r  (+0x240)  case 7 -> block[0x91] = g_scene_light_colour_g  (+0x244)  case 8 -> block[0x92] = g_scene_light_colour_b  (+0x248)  case 9 -> writes [0x90], [0x91], [0x92]: the all-three-light-colour alias  case 10 -> block[0x93] = g_scene_light_ambient  (+0x24C)  Each case also writes the parallel tween block (g_light_tween_block0/1) at indices 1,5,9,0xD,0x11,0x15,0x19,0x1D,0x21 -- stride 0x10 with the value at +4, but only NINE slots for eleven channel numbers, because the aliases 5 and 9 have none. So the tween block index is a COMPACTED index (0,1,2,3,4,6,7,8,10 -> 0..8) and coincides with the channel number only for 0..4. Reading the channel map off that array instead of off this switch gets channels 6+ wrong by one slot.  block == 0 selects g_scene_light_block0 (the one pushed every frame); 1 selects g_scene_light_block1, which nothing reads. Operands for the float channels are POINTERS resolved through FUN_0045EBB0; the fog RGB channels take their value inline.

PushSceneFogFromLightBlock(a, b, near, far) -- SetFogRange(near, far), and nothing else. **The first two arguments are dead**: both callers pass them and this routine forwards only param_3 and param_4, so the scene fog range reaches D3DRENDERSTATE_FOGSTART/FOGEND untouched. Two callers, and that is the whole of the fog-range path in the binary: PushSceneLightStateToDevice (0x0040AD90) once a frame with g_scene_fog_near/far, and FUN_0040C2E0 from SetupSceneProjection with the scene light block's +0x30/+0x34 -- the same two words. No camera position, eye or transform appears anywhere on either path, which is what makes FOGSTART/FOGEND eye-space depths measured from whatever view matrix draws the frame.

Steady-state body of CameraSnapToPathEye, reached by that function re-pointing g_camera_update_hook at itself+N. Writes only the eye, never the angles -- which is how the camera holds position while SelectCameraLookAtTarget swings the look-at.

Steady-state body of CameraStepDeferredRailWithFrameExport. Advances the stashed path frame, evaluates eye and target as independent channels, takes yaw from (eye - target) and forces pitch and roll to zero.

The camera hook scene state (2,7) installs -- the second of the two that play a range EvtActionCamPlay40's `flags & 2` branch (FUN_00403490) stashed into g_stashed_path_frame/g_stashed_path_end_frame. It re-points g_camera_update_hook at itself, so it is both the installer and the steady body. **It increments before it evaluates**: `if (end < cur) goto tail; cur += 1; DAT_009C70BC = (float)cur; CamEvalPath7(...)`, and only then `g_cam_path_frames_left = end - cur` at the tail. So a stashed 581..660 draws 582..660 -- the start frame is stepped past and the end frame IS reached -- where CamAdvancePathFrame (FUN_004035E0), which drives the ordinary non-deferred play, publishes the cursor and increments after. CameraStepRailTick (FUN_0040C790) is the (2,6) twin and differs only in using <= where this uses <, so this one runs one frame past the end and that one stops on it. The browser port had modelled both as CamAdvancePathFrame and so lost the last frame of every deferred shot; stage 2 block 16's captor cue (path 75 frame 660) and its civilian's killed-script cue (frame 650) are both timed to that tail and neither could fire.

PushSceneFogColour() -- packs the scene light block's fog colour and pushes it to the device, every frame, from FUN_0040E730 (the scene draw):  SetFogColour((g_scene_fog_r << 8 | g_scene_fog_g) << 8 | g_scene_fog_b).  So the three components are ints 0..255 packed with alpha 0. They are the integer form of light-block channels 2, 3 and 4 -- the ones evt opcodes 0x20-0x27 write as floats 0..255. FUN_00460250 seeds them 255/0/0 alongside the mirrored float channel array at 0x009C89E4 + channel*0x10 (0=near, 1=far, 2/3/4=fog RGB as 255.0/0.0/0.0, 6/7/8=light RGB), which is what proves the channel numbering.

The per-frame transform of one effect node: MatrixTranslate from EffectFrameTranslations, then RotZ/RotY/RotX from EffectFrameRotations, indexed by the node's bone - 1. g_effect_interp_mode[effect] selects the rate: 0 is one key per frame, otherwise the animation runs at half rate and odd frames blend the two neighbouring keys (mode 2 slerping through matrices when any axis differs by more than 0x3000).

Draws an animated effect through EffectDrawTree with AssetDrawSlot. The argument is a 4-int state block {effect id, motion id, frame, prev frame} living inside the owning object -- obj+0x324 for a class-0x41 prop.

Wraps the frame counter (to 0 at g_motion_play_length[motion]-1, and to the end when it goes negative) and then walks g_effect_trees[effect id]'s children with EffectDrawNode. The descriptor IS a node: same {u32 slot; s16 bone; u16 children; u32 child[]} struct, with slot 0 and bone 0 so the root itself never draws.

One effect node: push, EffectPoseNode, AssetDrawSlot(node->slot), recurse into the children, pop. A node with bone < 1 is a pure transform and draws nothing. Slot 0x10CE gets a random 0.27-0.37 scale each frame, which is how the smoke puffs vary.
As EffectDrawUnlit but routes each part through SubmitSlotWithSceneLightArray instead of AssetDrawSlot. KindedPropUpdate picks this one for item set 4 and for scene 3.

EffectDrawUnlit with two extras, and the entry point both class 0x44 selector 0 and FUN_00474120 use. EffectDrawWithCapture(state, capture_bone, slot_override): DAT_007C1789 = capture_bone + 1, so EffectDrawNode copies the matrix of the node whose bone equals capture_bone into state+0x14 (obj+0x338); DAT_007C178C = slot_override, and a value >= 0 makes every node draw THAT slot instead of its own. EffectDrawUnlit passes 0xFF and -1 for the two, which is why it captures nothing. DAT_007C1788 = 0 either way, so the parts are unlit.

Address of one frame's translation array inside the motion buffer: g_motion_slots[motion].base + 4 + frame * align4(bones * 0x12 - 0xF), then bone * 0xC for three floats. The effect's animation is an ordinary motion; only the node tree is its own.
Address of one frame's rotation array, the same stride as EffectFrameTranslations offset past the translations; bone * 6 for three BAMS shorts in X, Y, Z order.

BuildSceneLightDirection(pitch_bams, yaw_bams, world_out, view_out)  Turns the scene light block's +0x18 / +0x1C angle pair into a direction vector, in both world and view space:      v = (0, 0, 1)     MatrixStackPush; MatrixLoadIdentity();     MatrixRotateY(yaw); MatrixRotateX(pitch);     TransformVector(v) -> world_out            ; block +0x00     MultiplyByViewMatrix(g_view[player]);     TransformVector(v) -> view_out             ; block +0x0C     MatrixStackPop  MatrixRotateY/X PRE-multiply (M <- R x M) and the vector transform is D3D's row-vector form, so pitch is applied first and yaw second. Working it through with the matrices as those rotators actually store them:      dir = ( cos(pitch) * sin(yaw), -sin(pitch), cos(pitch) * cos(yaw) )  The caller (UpdateSceneViewAndLight, 0x00401F40) passes **view_out** to SetRenderLightDirection, which negates it into g_render_light_dir_*. So the D3DLIGHT7 direction -- the direction light travels -- is -dir, and `dir` itself is the direction the light comes FROM.  Both angles are BAMS: MatrixRotateX/Y multiply by 9.58738e-05 = 2*pi/65536.  Written by evt opcodes 0x18 (set) and 0x17 (slerp over N frames).
g_app_state_pending = -1. Drops a pending state change without committing it. Called by ResetGameOnStart's teardown path (FUN_0040A920 -> 0x0040E840).

g_app_state_pending = the argument. Does not change g_app_state; CommitAppState applies it at the end of the frame. Fourteen call sites, requesting 3, 4, 6, 7, 0x0C and 0x0F. Start-with-a-credit (FUN_00414FC0) requests 6, which is what makes 6 the in-play state.

The only writer of g_app_state, run at the end of the per-frame tick FUN_0040E730. Does nothing while g_app_state_pending is negative. Otherwise it tears the old screen down (AssetDrainAllJobs when the pending state is 0x0E, three other teardowns otherwise), sets DAT_009C71C4 = (pending == 5) -- the attract flag -- clears the per-player counters, then g_app_state = pending and g_app_state_pending = -1. The line that fixes what 6 and 7 mean: if (pending < 6 || pending > 7) g_player_state = 9 for both players, so 6 and 7 are the ONLY states that leave a live player alone.

RequestAppState(g_app_state_next_table[g_wCaptionMode][g_app_state]) -- the scripted advance out of a screen that has finished. Callers: RunAttractDemo when the demo scene runs out while g_app_state is 5, and the name-entry screen FUN_00481400 when g_GameMode is not 3.

Builds the skeletal model record embedded at obj+0x194. Writes model+0x116C (the character size, and the factor SkeletonApplyRootMotion scales its root delta by) from the CHARACTER TYPE alone -- MOVSX EAX,[ESI+0x60]; ADD EAX,-0x1e; CMP EAX,0x1a; JA to the 1.0 arm, then the index byte table at 0x00410568 selecting 0x3f19999a / 0x3f333333 / 0x3f666666. And writes model+0x64 = 3 unconditionally at 0x004104C5 -- MOV dword ptr [ESI + 0x64], 0x3, bytes c7466403000000 -- so bit 1, the one and only gate SkeletonApplyRootMotion tests before it moves the actor, is SET on every skeletal actor in the game. Classes 0x30 and 0x31 never change it; class 0x10's script does, per block. [proved]
reads the motion frame, sets the object root pose, then walks the node tree

per node: writes the bone's DRAW RECORD at obj+0x20C + bone*0x90 and then Translate(bone offset); RotZ; RotY; RotX from frame+0x0C+bone*6, recursing into the children. The record fields it writes each frame are +0x00 the asset slot, +0x74 = 0x21, +0x78 the HIT-SPHERE RADIUS and +0x7C..+0x84 its centre, from PTR_DAT_004D032C[char_type][bone-1] with the radius scaled by obj+0x1300 -- but ONLY when that table entry's own slot equals the slot just written. Otherwise all four go to zero. So a bone whose drawn model has been swapped away from the one the table names -- a gore variant, or a hand that has thrown its weapon -- loses its hit sphere and cannot be shot, without anything else asking for it. ZombieThrowHandWeapon (0045A2B2/0045A2DB) and SpawnThrownWeapon (00450540) write that same +0x78 to zero outright as the weapon leaves, which is the same statement made immediately.
Per-frame root pose: reads the current motion frame, or blends two of them by DAT_007C1C24 when the cross-fade flag is set (obj+0x37 & 0x21), and applies the root translation and rotation.

Converts the frame-to-frame delta of the motion root into world movement when obj+0x64 bit 1 is set, rotating it by the actor's own orientation, then calls the per-frame pose hook at motion block +0x115C.
draws record[bone].slot; record base obj+0x20C, stride 0x90
internally push/pop balanced

The body of DrawSkinnedModelAndShadow: parks the track and bone records in g_motion_track/g_motion_bone_records, walks g_character_skeletons[type] emitting each node, then runs the actor's attachment list. The part loop at the end is the DRAW GATE: for i in 0..model+0x3C, it emits part i only when the byte at model+0x40 + i*8 + 1 is non-zero -- the same byte ActorSetPartVisibility (FUN_00409D10) writes for every part at once, and the one ZombieStateAwaitCivilianOrder (FUN_0045BAD0) clears for part 0 alone to hold a captor off screen. The byte at +0 of the same record is a lazily-filled 'this part has a model' cache: zero asks FUN_00419520 and, if that answers, latches 1.

The motion sampler's clock arm. model[2] = model[0] % (g_motion_play_length[model[8]] + 1) -- the play cursor, which WRAPS at play_length + 1 and so takes every value from 0 to the play length inclusive; model[6] = model[2] / 2 is the authored frame, and an odd cursor blends the two neighbours on tracks 1 and 2, which is the 60 Hz over 30 Hz interpolation. Sets model+0x5D when the cursor has reached the play length and model+0x5E when it has reached play_length - 1. Nothing here advances model[0]: the owning class does, and a class holds a clip on its last frame by simply not incrementing it.

Emits one node of the skeleton and, when its bone index matches the tracked one, records that node's **world position** into obj+0x100/104/108 -- which is what SelectCameraLookAtTarget aims the camera at, never obj+0x40. The bone is 1 for an ordinary humanoid (character types 0..0x14), 2 when obj+0x136C bit 0x10000000 is set, and 9 for body condition 5 or the g_camera_block_target case; obj+0x10C..114 gets the same point in the other space. A further -3.5 is applied to the height in the two-player attacker case. Recurses into the node's children.

Start a clip at frame zero with **no cross-fade**: writes the motion id to track+0x20, zeroes the frame counter (track+0x00), the play cursor (track+0x08), track+0x10 and track+0x18, and clears the two fade bytes at +0x36/+0x37, so nothing of the outgoing clip is left to blend from. ActorSetMotionBlended (FUN_004119A0) is the fading half of the pair; this one is for the scripted cues that are meant to cut, and ZombieStateMotionCue21 is one of them.

Start a motion on the track with a **cross-fade**: the fourth argument is the fade length in frames, stored at track+0x30 as length+1, alongside the start frame at +0x08 and its half at +0x18. Every class-0x30 state passes one -- 5 for ZombieStateApproach's walk and ZombieStateStrike's swing, 10 for the attack run, the hold's idle, ZombieStateBackOff's retreat, the lunge and ZombieStateWaitTurn. ActorSetMotion (FUN_00411930) is the one that does not fade, and it is used for the scripted cues that are meant to cut.
Start a motion on one of the actor's two motion tracks; the track index is the last argument (0 the looping motion, 1 the one-shot the hit reaction uses).
MotionCrossFadeTo with a different flag pair (block+0x38 |= 9); used by the alternate hit reaction indexed by the last-hit zone.
Start a motion on track 1 cross-fading from what is playing. block+0x33 = fade + 1 -- ActorPlayHitReaction passes 20 when the hit severed something and 10 otherwise.

Per-node veto, consulted by SkeletonEmitNode before it calls the node draw hook at obj+0x1158. Read from the disassembly rather than the decompiler's switch: for character type 0x17 it is CMP word[node+0x14],0x10 / SETGE, so every bone from 16 up is suppressed -- exactly the eight BuildCharacterPartSubparts replaces. Otherwise it suppresses BONE 9 alone, and only when the slot bone 9 is CURRENTLY DRAWING -- g_motion_bone_records[9].slot, so a swap would change the answer -- is one of ten literals: 0xE3C 0xE4D 0xEA2 0xEB6 0xEC6 0xED6 0xEF6 0xF06 0xF83 0x15B0, enumerated out of the jump table at 0x00412360 and its byte map at 0x00412368. Those ten are exactly the ten character types whose g_pCharacterExtraParts part 1 draws that same slot, 1:1 with no strays either way: 0x21 0x22 0x26 0x28 0x29 0x2A 0x2C 0x2D 0x35 0x3B. The rule is: when a part is drawn soft, do not also draw it rigid. It never ADDS a draw.

Bind the attachment list at obj+0x1170: for every id in the s16[] up to the terminating negative, look up g_actor_attachment_table[id] = {s32 bone; s32 slot}. An id BELOW 0x24 overwrites bone_records[bone].slot -- the bone draws that model instead of the one its skeleton node names, which is how a civilian gets one of the 60 interchangeable hito_kao_* faces. An id of 0x12 or above also asks the asset system to load the slot. Ids of 0x24 and above are drawn as extra models by ActorDrawAttachedParts and are not bound here. CivilianInit calls this straight after writing the list pointer from the spawn tail's +0x08.
The undo of ActorBindPartList's loads: walks the same s16[] and releases every slot whose id is 0x12 or above. It does not put the overwritten bone slots back -- the object is being torn down.

Draw the actor's attachment list: the s16[] at obj+0x1170, terminated by a negative. SkeletonDrawWalk calls this last, through the hook at obj+0x1174, so attachments are drawn after every skeleton node. Ids above 0x23 index g_actor_attachment_table; the record is {s32 bone; s32 slot} and the draw is MatrixStackSetTopFromArray(bone_records[bone].matrix at +0x28) then AssetDrawSlot(slot) -- an EXTRA model on a bone, not a replacement. In Original Mode (g_GameMode == 1) with DAT_009C88AC set, bone 2 is scaled 1.5x in X and Z and bones 5/8/12/15 by 2.0x. Ids 0x23 and below are handled by ActorBindPartList at build time instead, which overwrites the bone's own drawn slot. Every class-0x10 civilian's hair, hat, bag and shoes come through here: 52 of the 65 class-0x10 spawns in the shipped evts carry a list.

ActorDrawAttachedParts submitting through the scene light array instead of AssetDrawSlot. CivilianInit installs it at obj+0x1174 in place of the plain one when g_scene_light_array (0x009A2BB4) is non-null, and raises obj+0x38 bit 8 at the same time. Same list, same records, same 1.5x/2.0x Original Mode scales.
motion job sub-step 0: builds "mot\%s", CreateFileA, allocates size+0x20
sub-step 1: one ReadFile of the whole bank -- mot/ is NOT compressed
sub-step 2: the entire parse -- one int32 offset per motion id in the bank
asset job kind 8; dispatches the sub-step at job+0x0C
asset job kind 9
asset job kind 10
((bones*6+15)&~3)*frame + 4 + slot.base; bones from the CHARACTER type

DrawBackdropDome -- the game's sky.  Ghidra had left this block undefined, so it appeared in no xref listing by name. Selected by evt opcode 0x1B (preset, DAT_009A2C34) and gated by 0x1C (mode, DAT_009CA090: 0 off, 2 drawn but frozen, else drawn and animating).  Preset table at g_backdrop_preset_table (0x00579968), 12 x 16 bytes:      +0x00  s16  slot_a   the dome that is drawn     +0x02  s16  slot_b   a second slot, used by the 8/10/11 variant paths     +0x04  f32  dy       Y offset from the camera, 0 .. -3000     +0x08  s32  spin     BAMS added to the angle every frame     +0x0C  s32  angle0   BAMS the angle resets to when the preset changes  Main path:      esi = &g_camera_pose[g_camera_player];     /* 0x009A60C0 + player*0x69 */     if (preset != DAT_007C2118) {              /* preset changed */         state->angle = table[preset].angle0;     }     if (backdrop_mode == 0) return;      MatrixStackPush(0);     MatrixTranslate(esi->x, esi->y + table[preset].dy, esi->z);     if (backdrop_mode != 2) state->angle += table[preset].spin;     if (preset == 5) { MatrixRotateZ(0x8000); MatrixRotateY(-angle); }     else               MatrixRotateY(angle);     MatrixScale(1.2f, 1.2f, -1.2f);     AssetDrawSlot(table[preset].slot_a);  TWO DETAILS THAT MATTER:    * It follows the camera in ALL THREE AXES, not just horizontally, so the     dome can never be approached.   * The Z SCALE IS NEGATIVE. The dome is turned inside out -- it is modelled     to be seen from within.  Presets 8, 10 and 11 branch to separate paths at 0x004133FB / 0x004133F3 / 0x00413441; those also call FUN_00413560, which scrolls texture V by -0.005/frame and wraps at -2.995.  The call at 0x004133D3 is to FUN_0041EBB0, the empty stub -- a dead call.  Every dome lives in st1_1, etc_1 or st5_01b regardless of which stage uses it; the sky is shared geometry. No region draws these slots, so the script pulls them in with opcode 0x50 like any other prop.  See docs/formats/evt.md.

DrawRainParticles -- evt opcode 0x1D's effect, gated on DAT_009C8E50 == 1.      SetDrawLayerNibble(0xE);     for (p = g_rain_particles; p < 0x007C2114; p += 3 floats) {         p.y -= 2.0;         if (p.y <= -7.0) {                    /* respawn */             p.x = rand() % 0x14 - 10.0;       /* [-10,  9] */             p.y = rand() % 0x32 - 25.0;       /* [-25, 24] */             p.z = rand() % 0x19 - 35.0;       /* [-35,-11] */         }         world = RotY(g_camera_pose[player].yaw) * p               + g_camera_pose[player].eye;         yaw = angle_of(world - eye, with dy passed as a LITERAL 0);         Translate(world); RotateY(yaw); RotateZ(0x100);         Scale(1.5, 3.5, 1.0);         AssetDrawSlotAlpha(0x53, 0.5);     }     SetDrawLayerNibble(8);                    /* back to the default layer */  THE COUNT IS NOT STORED. The particle array runs 0x007C1EB8 .. 0x007C2114 at 12 bytes each, which is 50. The loop bound is the end of the array.  Three details that are not what a from-scratch particle system would do:    * The volume is rotated by the camera's YAW ONLY before the eye is added,     so it follows where the camera looks horizontally while staying     world-vertical. Rain never tilts when the camera pitches.   * The spawn box is 20 x 50 x 25 sitting IN FRONT of the camera (z from -35     to -11), so drops are only ever created ahead of the view.   * The per-drop yaw is computed with the vertical component passed as a     literal 0, so a drop's facing does not change as it falls.  RotZ(0x100) is 1.40625 degrees -- the streaks are very slightly off vertical.  Asset slot 0x53 is stage1.bin[0]. No region draws it and no asset opcode loads it: the routine names the slot as a literal, so anything reconstructing the scene must pull it in explicitly or the effect has no model.  The call at 0x00413704 is FUN_0041EBB0, the empty stub -- a dead call, the same one DrawBackdropDome makes.  [measured] Only stage 1 ever turns rain on: 18 `enable_rain 1` in st1evtbl, and every other stage's uses are all 0.  See docs/formats/evt.md.

Draw the HUD letterbox shutter and drive the firing gate. evt opcode 0x1F selects the state in DAT_009CA0F4.  Geometry: the bars are asset 0x93E, which is common.bin model 129 -- a single four-vertex quad spanning x -0.515..0.515, y -0.05..0.05. MatrixTranslate positions its ORIGIN, so a bar placed at y = 0.35 occupies 0.30..0.40. At the game's 41.100 degree vertical FOV the frustum half-height at |z| = 1 is tan(20.55 deg) = 0.37477, so a closed shutter's inner edge sits at 80 % of the half-height: a 10 % band top and bottom. The quad's 0.515 half-width just covers the 0.4997 half-width of a 4:3 frustum, i.e. the artwork is cut for a 4:3 screen exactly.  States (DAT_009CA0F4):   0  draw closed at +/-0.35, -> 4, gate ON   1  opening: counter 0 -> 0x28, y = 0.35 + counter*0.0025, -> 2, gate ON   2  nothing drawn -- fully open (y = 0.45 clears the frame at counter 30)   3  closing: counter 0x28 -> 0; at 0 draw closed, -> 4, gate OFF   4  draw closed unless (DAT_009A5900 & 0x30)   5  draw closed, -> 4, gate OFF   6  gate ON, -> 2   7  restore the previous state (DAT_009C8E9C)   8  one bar at (0,0,-1) scaled (1,8,1) -- half-height 0.4, a full blackout  The gate is g_nFiringGate (0x009C8E00). It is not "the shutter is open": states 0 and 5 both draw a closed shutter and set it 1 and 0 respectively. It is also what gates the Start poll for a cutscene skip -- see g_nEvtSkippableRegion.

One player's whole per-frame update while a stage is running. Ghidra had not made a function here at all -- the region 0x00413DDF..0x00413FAF is orphaned instructions after FUN_00413DB0, which is one of four sibling handlers that hand the player task to the next state through FUN_00414770(obj, n). Body, in order: stash the per-player word at 0x009A5CD8 into DAT_009A26A0 and call the per-player hook at 0x009A5CE0 + player*0x130; FUN_00415100; force g_player_lives to 1 while g_app_state is 5 (the attract demo), then clamp it at 0; with lives left, run the trigger -- FUN_00414B90 in g_GameMode 1 (Original), PlayerFireAndReloadUpdate otherwise; draw the crosshair HudDrawCrosshair; FUN_00416B00 unless g_GameMode is 2 with DAT_009C72F2 set; then, outside app states 9 and 5, either the dead branch (arcade sets DAT_009A2234, otherwise g_players_in_play-- and FUN_00415080(4,1,obj)) or the HUD branch -- `if (g_nFiringGate != 0) HudDrawAmmoAndReloadPrompt(obj)`, then FUN_004174A0 and a copy of lives into +0x08 of the per-player block. Ends with FUN_00417300, FUN_00414600 when FUN_00413280 says gameplay is live, and FUN_00413FB0. The g_nFiringGate test at 0x00413F63 is the proof that the ammo readout is hidden while the shutter's gate is down, the way HudDrawCrosshair's own test hides the crosshair.

One player's trigger, per frame; PlayerUpdateInPlay calls it in every g_GameMode but 1, which takes FUN_00414B90 instead. With ammo left and the firing gate open it decrements g_player_ammo, raises g_nPlayerFired, counts g_player_shot_count, builds the shot ray from the crosshair through BuildShotRay, calls PlayerShotEffectSpawn and plays g_gunshot_sound_ids[player]. With the magazine empty, or on the reload button, it calls PlayerRefillMagazine. The magazine it compares against is the literal 6 in arcade and g_player_magazine_size in Original Mode.  THE SHAPE OF THE GATE, because it decides what a blocked trigger does: the body is  if (trigger_latch) { if (no ammo) { auto-refill } else if (g_nFiringGate != 0) { the fire block } }  so a trigger pulled while g_nFiringGate is 0 does NOTHING -- it returns before the ammo decrement, before the shot counter, before BuildShotRay and before PlayerShotEffectSpawn, so no muzzle flash, no tracer and no gunshot are spawned either. The reload paths are outside the gate and still run; only PlayerRefillMagazine's sound is gated. The ammo decrement has three further exemptions inside the gate: DAT_009C8E98 == 5 (the attract demo), DAT_009C9FD9[player*0x7c] set, and an Original Mode magazine size of -1 (unlimited); the shot still fires in all three. The tail is the other half of the gate: while g_nFiringGate is 0 and g_nEvtSkippableRegion is set, the same button sets g_nSkipRequested instead (0x00414AE2).
Refill: g_player_ammo = 6, or g_player_magazine_size when g_GameMode is 1 and that byte is not -1. Clears the empty latch at 0x009A5C7E and plays 0x3E16A9 while the firing gate is open.

The g_GameMode == 1 twin of PlayerFireAndReloadUpdate; 0x00413EE5 reads g_GameMode, decrements it and calls this one on zero, the arcade one otherwise. Same trigger shape -- decrement g_player_ammo, count the shot, BuildShotRay, PlayerShotEffectSpawn -- plus two things the arcade arm has not: an auto-fire latch driven by the per-player bytes at 0x009A2251/0x009A2252/0x009A2253 out of the 8-byte rows at 0x00579EDC, and a recoil spread that offsets the crosshair by rand()%%0x40 across and rand()%%0x30 down before the ray is built, taken only while +0x07 of the Original Mode block is 1 and the burst counter is not 2. The gunshot is g_original_weapon_gunshot_ids[g_original_weapon_sound_kind] when that entry is non-zero and g_gunshot_sound_ids[player] when it is zero. Reloading goes to PlayerReloadOriginalModeWeapon, not PlayerRefillMagazine.

Original Mode's reload, called by PlayerFireOriginalModeWeapon in place of PlayerRefillMagazine. Refuses while +0x07 of the Original Mode block is 2 unless the weapon's own +0x1E is 1; otherwise calls FUN_00416420, sets the magazine to g_player_magazine_size and plays g_original_weapon_reload_ids[g_original_weapon_sound_kind], falling back to 0x3E16A9 COMMON\RELOAD1_44.WAV when that entry is zero -- both gated on g_nFiringGate, as PlayerRefillMagazine's own play is.

Computes g_active_player from g_players_in_play: a count of 0 gives -1, nobody; 1 gives player 1 when the per-player state word at 0x009A5C62 is neither 5 nor 7 and player 0 otherwise; 2 gives 2, both, and also raises DAT_007C211C. TryClaimAttackSlot reads the answer when g_max_attackers is 1, and class 0x31 state 22 uses it to force a target after a failed claim.

One life, -100 points, 0x5A frames of invulnerability, and _DAT_009A3794 -= 2, which UpdateDamageRank consumes -- being hit lowers the adaptive rank and makes the game easier. There is no variable damage against the player.
Rejects a player index that is not 0 or 1, and rejects a hit while the player entity is in a state other than 1 or 4..5 during app state 6.
PlayerTakeDamage with an explicit invulnerability duration and an override that ignores the current one.
+1 to g_player_lives, or 300 points instead when the player is already at the cap -- g_max_lives, or the per-player Boss Mode cap at 0x009A2245 + p*0x14.

The crosshair sprite, one player, once a frame, from PlayerUpdateInPlay. Four conditions, all required: g_app_state == 6 (in play); the player is either holding a live gun (DAT_009A5D85[p*0x130] != 1 and DAT_009C8FD0[p*0x14] != 0) or in input mode 5 or 6 as FUN_0041E260 reports it; g_player_lives > 0; and g_nFiringGate != 0 (the read at 0x00416A65). So the crosshair is HIDDEN whenever the shutter's firing gate is down -- the same flag that makes the trigger do nothing. Position: modes 5/6 take it from FUN_0041E280, everything else from (g_crosshair_x + 320, 240 - g_crosshair_y), i.e. the 640x480 screen with the origin at the centre and y up. The sprite id is a s16 from the table at 0x00579F58 indexed by (DAT_009C9F60[p*0x7c] + player*4); the record at 0x009A5D44 + player*0x130 is handed to FUN_0041C630.

Draws and steps the three 6-record rings one player's shots leave, in draw layer 0xC. The muzzle flash (g_shot_flash_ring) runs 9 frames from g_muzzle_flash_slots[player] at scale 0.1 with a second draw from g_muzzle_smoke_slots[player] at 0.75 for weapon kind 4 and 0.5 otherwise, and is skipped entirely for kind 3. The tracer (g_shot_tracer_ring) advances by its velocity, billboards through MatrixClearRotation, spins +0x1000 BAMS a frame and draws g_muzzle_smoke_slots[player] + 2; it lives 60 frames, or dies on its second frame when g_shot_hit_something says the shot landed. The third ring is Original Mode weapon kind 4 only: 24 frames from slot 0xA6F at scale 0.05. Every record's frame counter steps whether or not it is live.

Fills one slot of all three per-player effect rings, once per trigger pull, hit or miss. The muzzle point is the crosshair at camera-space z = -1: (g_crosshair_x / g_projection_distance_px, g_crosshair_y / g_projection_distance_px, -1.0), with the flash angles from FUN_004016B0 and then yaw += 0x8000 and pitch negated. The tracer takes that point through the camera matrix into world space and flies normalize(point - eye) * 20.0, or * 10.0 for Original Mode weapon kind 5, which also routes its draw down the object-path arm. The ring cursor g_shot_effect_cursor advances after the flash and the tracer are written and BEFORE the Original Mode third record, so that one lands in the NEXT slot.

The ammo readout and the RELOAD prompt, one player. Called from PlayerUpdateInPlay only while g_nFiringGate is non-zero. Draws nothing unless g_bHudShutterState is 2 (fully open, full size) or 1 (opening, scaled by (40 - counter)*0.0125 + 1 from the per-player float at 0x007C2120); any other shutter state zeroes that counter and skips the readout. Arcade draws one bullet sprite per round left, stepping (spacing + 24) px from x=24 for player 1 and back from x=592 for player 2, at y = 364 + the per-weapon dy. Original Mode draws the same sprite once plus a two-digit count when g_player_ammo >= 7, and 'oo' (sprites 0x65, 99) when g_player_magazine_size is -1, i.e. unlimited; the sprite and the two offsets come from the 12-byte rows at 0x004ECA20 indexed by the weapon at DAT_009A2247. Then the RELOAD prompt, which needs the empty latch DAT_009A5C7E set AND g_nFiringGate again (0x00418001): sprite 0xA27 blinks on the low 45 of every 60 frames of the counter at 0x009A5C80, joined after 120 frames by 0xA28 or 0xA29, and the same counter plays a nag sound while the trigger is held. The counter counts up and re-arms at 120 rather than overflowing.

Loads the shared pol/common.bin and tex/common.bin asset banks.  The clearest example of the asset load path in the binary; every other loader is a variation on it.    wsprintfA(path, "pol\%s", "common.bin")   CreateFileA / GetFileSize / ReadFile into the staging buffer at 009c8e54   size = *staging                     <- u32 uncompressed size header   LzDecompress(staging + 1, dst)      <- src skips the header  The pol bank decompresses to a fixed .data buffer at 00811720. The tex bank is allocated at run time: alloc(size + 0x20), then aligned up to 32 before use.  The registration loop that follows walks 0x175 (373) entries of a table at 004e3110, using the sign bit of each container word as a present/absent flag.
