ModelFlipStripCullingParity(model)  Walks a loaded NL1 model's mesh chain and XORs bit 0 of every *strip* control word, flipping culling 2 <-> 3 (backface <-> frontface) and 0 <-> 1 (both "no cull", so a no-op there).  Applied ONLY to the four asset slots listed at g_ModelFixupSlotList (0x0057A280) -- it is a per-asset content patch, not a general load step. Paired with ModelForceFogControlNone, called immediately before it.  This is the canonical statement of the NL1 chain walk. Three rules, nothing else -- no parameter_control bit, no shading mode, no 16-bit-UV flag:    chain word bit 31 set  -> mesh header, 0x50 bytes, skip geometry with                             (mesh_data_size & ~3)   chain word bit 31 clear-> strip header {flags, count}, 8 bytes;                             count is a TRIANGLE count when flags & 8   vertex record          -> 8 bytes when bit 0 of its first dword is clear                             (a back-reference), 32 bytes when set  Verified against all 9,112 models: the walk lands exactly on every declared mesh end, zero desyncs (tools/verify_walk.py).

ModelForceFogControlNone(model)  Walks a loaded NL1 model's mesh headers and rewrites each mesh's tsp_instruction:      tsp = (tsp & 0xFFBFFFFF) | 0x00800000;  Bits 22-23 are PowerVR2 fog control (0 LUT, 1 per-vertex, 2 none, 3 LUT mode 2). Clearing 22 and setting 23 forces fog control to 2 = NONE, so these meshes never take the fog path in TranslatePvr2StateToD3D.  Only reached for the four slots in g_ModelFixupSlotList. Mesh stride here is (mesh_data_size & ~3) + 0x50 -- the size field is masked down to a 4-byte boundary, as it is in WalkMeshChainAndDraw.  Note the walk assumes every chain word at this level has bit 31 set; if one does not it falls into an infinite loop, which is a second confirmation that a top-level chain word is always either a mesh header or the zero terminator.

Build the runtime record for one of g_pCharacterExtraParts' parts, lazily, the first time SkeletonDrawWalk wants to draw it. Refuses while the part's asset slot is not resident. The 0x54-byte record holds four {count, source verts, index list, bone matrix} groups plus the drawn slot at +0x44 and the matrix the draw happens in at +0x50; the five bone indices come from g_character_part_bones[part], with per-character-type overrides for 0x0E, 0x1F/0x46/0x4E, 0x41, 0x4C and 0x53. Character type 0x17's part 1 goes to FUN_00419EB0 instead, which builds eight sub-parts. The vertices are a private copy of the loaded model's, so the deform writes into geometry only this actor draws.
Part drawer: deform all four groups -- which=1 for k in 0,1 then which=0 for k in 0,1 -- then draw. Every part 1 in the game takes it, and so does type 0x4C's whole 18-part list.

The part's 0x54-byte runtime record, or 0 if it has none yet. Rebuilds it through BuildCharacterPart when the asset slot has moved -- it compares rec+0x48 against the slot's current base -- and drops the old vertex map with FreeCharacterPartVertexMap.

The deform, and it is a HARD PARTITION rather than a blend. One call per vertex group: it composes inverse(draw bone matrix) * (group bone matrix), then walks the part's rows -- one signed byte per row in the group's assign array -- and for every row the byte claims (>= 0) transforms that group's source point and normal, at rec+0x04/+0x24 with stride 0x18, into the draw bone's space and writes them over every copy of that vertex in the loaded model. A negative byte means the row belongs to another group. Measured across three parts: 0 rows claimed by two groups and 0 claimed by none, so every vertex has exactly one bone and weight 1. The source arrays are in the GROUP BONE's local space, so the net effect after the draw re-applies the draw bone's matrix is simply world = group_bone_matrix * source_vertex.

Draw the deformed part: set the matrix from rec+0x50, the FIFTH bone of the part's g_character_part_bones row, and AssetDrawSlot(rec+0x44). Skipped when the part's visibility byte at model+0x40 + part*8 + 1 is clear. The character-type switch chooses between AssetDrawSlot, SubmitSlotWithSceneLightArray and the two-argument lit variants, and type 0x4C's parts 0-5 draw a second slot from DAT_004EDA50 as well.
Part drawer: deform group 2 only, then draw. g_character_part_drawers gives it to types 0x1F/0x46/0x4E parts 1 and 2.
DeformCharacterPartGroup for one group, then DrawCharacterPartSlot. The which argument picks the pair of group slots: 1 is groups 0 and 1, 0 is groups 2 and 3.

Part drawer: deform group 0 only, then draw -- the commonest by far, and every humanoid's part 0 (the waist). The part's other groups are left holding what the loaded model stores, which is correct because a group whose bone IS the draw bone deforms to the identity: measured, the exe's source vertices for such a group equal the pol model's stored ones to within the low mantissa bit that WriteCharacterPartVertexPos sets.
Byte-for-byte the same as DrawCharacterPartGroup0 -- push 1, call DeformAndDrawCharacterPart -- as a second copy. g_character_part_drawers gives this one to character type 0x17's part 0.

Character type 0x17's part 1 alone, and a different mechanism: instead of one slot with four vertex groups it builds EIGHT sub-parts from g_class17_subpart_records, each with its own bone, asset slot and vertex map, into a 0xD0 record. Gated on DAT_009C7A78 == 4. Its eight bones are 16 and above, which is exactly the range SkeletonNodeDrawSuppressed vetoes for this type.
The drawer for character type 0x17's eight sub-parts. Unread beyond its shape.

Dispatch one of the character's non-skeleton parts: g_character_part_drawers[char_type][part](part). Every humanoid's part 0 is FUN_00419E90, which deforms one vertex group; the types with two parts draw part 1 through FUN_004198B0, which deforms all four. SkeletonDrawWalk's tail loop is what calls it, once per part that has a model and is not hidden.

Per part, the map from a logical vertex to every copy of it in the loaded model. Copies two blobs out of the mesh-info block in .rdata and relocates the second by adding the loaded model's base. The result is a 0x1C record: +0x04 the row count, +0x08 the head size in bytes, +0x10 the row stride, +0x18 the rows. A row is {s16 head[n]; u32 vertex_record_pointers[m]} with the pointer list terminated by -1, and a row is one logical vertex: measured, hito_gal's waist has 20 rows and 24 pointers onto 24 distinct vertex records, its skirt 24 rows and 28 pointers onto 28. The head is read by nothing in this build.
Frees the two blobs BuildCharacterPartVertexMap copied and then the record.

Write one deformed position over every copy of a logical vertex. It ORs bit 0 into the x coordinate's bits first, which is the PowerVR2 vertex control word: bit 0 of a record's first dword is what tells the chain walker this is a 32-byte vertex and not an 8-byte back-reference, so the write must not clear it. That costs the low mantissa bit of x, about 6e-4 at these magnitudes.
The normal half of WriteCharacterPartVertexPos, at +0x0C of the vertex record. It ORs bit 0 into the normal's z for the same reason the position half does it to x.
WriteCharacterPartVertexPos, writing the same position a second time 0x82C0 bytes further on. Used only for character type 0x4C's parts 0-5, whose model has a twin at that fixed offset.
WriteCharacterPartVertexNormal writing a second copy 0x82C0 bytes on, NEGATED -- the twin is mirrored, so its normals point the other way. Character type 0x4C only.

Terminated by id == 0xFFFF.               id 0 early-outs -- that is how a script says "no sound".               0x000100A0 is a special case: SS_SND_ALL_SOUND_OFF.               0x21A9 / 0x121A9 take a distinct FUN_004AC020 arg set.   1  BGM      (id & 0xFFF) indexes a table of char* filenames, prefixed with               the string at DAT_00588B58. TWO tables, chosen by:                   if (DAT_009C8E98 == 6 && g_GameMode == 0) plain else AR               0x00580354  char*[41]  "_AR" mix   (PTR_s_ST2_AR_WAV_00580354)               0x005803F8  char*[20]  plain mix   (PTR_s_ST2_WAV_005803F8)               The tables are CONTIGUOUS -- 0x580354 + 41*4 == 0x5803F8 --               which is what fixes their lengths; neither is terminated.               Index 0 is ST2, 1 is ST1; indices 2, 4 and 7 are null in both.               ids 0x10000009 / 0x10000014 / 0x10000025 pass 0 rather than 1               for FUN_004AC020's second arg (loop flag). Name at +2, prefixed "Sound\Voice\".   8  control  0x80000000 stops playback (FUN_0041D3E0) and clears               DAT_009C8FB8.  Reached from evt opcode 0x5F via BgmStopThenPlay (0x0041D450), which is literally PlaySoundId(0x80000000) then PlaySoundId(operand[2]) -- the instruction consumes four operands and uses only the third. Also the SE path for evt opcodes 0x38/0x3A.  Stage BGM is NOT started from the event script: every bgm_entry_play in the six stage scripts names a boss or transition track (indices 5, 14, 15, 16, 18, 19). Whatever starts ST1_AR..ST6_AR at stage entry has not been traced.  See docs/formats/sound.md.  THE SE PATH HAS A LOOP BRANCH THAT WAS NOT WRITTEN DOWN HERE, and it is the whole of the game's looping ambience: before playing, and unless the id is 0x21A9 or 0x121A9, it walks g_looping_se_ids (0x005887FC) and g_looping_se_stop_ids (0x005888B0) in step -- an id found in the first sets the loop flag it hands SoundPlayOnFreeChannel, an id found in the second makes it call SoundStopAllLoopingSe() first and play unlooped. That is how one PlaySoundId call starts a chainsaw and another stops it, with no handle in between.

The default per-frame pose hook: does nothing. Every skeletal actor installed by FUN_00410440 gets this one.

Signed BAMS heading error from a transform block's own orientation (+0x24 pitch, +0x28 yaw, +0x2C roll) to an x/z offset: builds the inverse rotation, transforms {dx, 0, dz} into the block's space and returns the angle. [likely] -- the return is past the MatrixStackPop Ghidra ends the body at; the reading comes from ActorTurnTowardXZ, which adds the result straight to the yaw and clamps it, and from Class14StateHunt, which refuses an attack while |result| > 0x1FFF.
Steps a transform block's yaw at +0x28 toward an x/z offset by at most one BAMS step, using ActorHeadingErrorTo. Class 0x14 passes 0x200 everywhere.

Writes the player this actor works against into obj+0x121. One player: the active player at 0x009C7000. Two: whichever forced-target flag is set, else a rand() pick weighted by the difference of the two life counts at 0x009A5C66 + player*0x98, so the player who is behind is chosen more often.

The attract-mode demo playlist. Walks g_attract_demo_playlist (0x00589828), 0x14 bytes an entry, indexed by DAT_009A3400 and terminated by a scene of -1: each entry names a g_scene_index at +0, a g_evt_block_index at +2, and a BGM track at +8 with its parameter at +0xC. Class 0x53's Init -- the cat: g_character_skeletons maps its character type 0x1A to eighteen nodes that all land in cat.bin. Reads two s16s off the descriptor tail: the first is an animation set that indexes 0x00589A64 (stride 10) for the motion, the second the subtype. Class 0x53 subtype >= 2: a shootable route-branch trigger. While its sub-state is 0 it counts frames, and at 200 it plays motion 0x2FA. If obj+0x34 bit 3 is set (shot) AND g_script_branch_var is still 0 AND g_evt_block_index == 8, it writes g_script_branch_var = 2, plays motion 0x2FD and latches sub-state 1 -- so this trigger answers the branch only in block 8, and only if nothing else has answered it already. That gate is load-bearing: of the four shipped spawns only block 8's route record has a slot 2 to go to, and tools/verify_branches.py fails if the gate is dropped. The update ScriptedSceneryDispatch33 installs for class 0x33 selector 1 -- obj+0x11C is the sub-type selector, not hit points (L3), so the evt's hp field picks it. This is the object g_carrier_object (0x009A5C34) points at: 004331e1 MOV [0x009a5c34],EBP writes it every frame, so the global is live for as long as one of these exists. It raises TWO bits on its OWN obj+0x34, and they are different ends of the ride. 0x10000000 at 00433203, when g_script_flags[tail+0x20] == 1 or (s32)tail+0x18 == obj+0x1370 -- that is what ZombieStateRideCarrier (class 0x30 state 29) leaves on. 0x40000000 at 00433280, once tail+0x14 is not -1.0f and obj+0x1370 has passed it, together with obj+0x1334 = 0 and an effect spawned from the six dwords at tail+0x24 -- and THAT is the bit ZombieStateDelayedStrikeInPlace reads at 0045eafe to give up to state 10 after 0x14 frames. Twenty frames after raising it the routine also sets obj+0x34 bit 0x200000, plays 0x723A9 and swaps the drawn slot to 0x1AAB..0x1AD2. Stage 5 block 2 step 2 op 37 spawns one (evt 7396, hp 1).

Class 0x33 selector 1's mover. One caller, ScriptedCarrierUpdate33 at 004333EC, and only on the frames that routine does not despawn or detonate. obj+0x1312 is its own two-step cursor. 0 seats the object from the descriptor tail: obj+0x13F0 = tail+0x00 (draw slot); tail+0x04 == -1 ORs 0x80000001 into obj+0x34 and copies tail+0x08 into BOTH obj+0x124 and obj+0x128 (the shot sphere), otherwise it ORs 0x80000051 -- bit 0x10 is the mesh shot volume -- and puts tail+0x04 in obj+0x14C; obj+0x1350 = tail+0x0C (the op_ path slot); obj+0x1374 = tail+0x10 (the last frame); obj+0x1354/0x1358/0x135C = 0x24A/0x260/0 (the sprite cursors the draw tail cycles). obj+0x1370 starts at (float)(g_cam_path_frame - 1) via FILD, so the path cursor is seeded from the CAMERA's frame at the spawn instruction and is its own counter thereafter. Cursor 1 runs; 2 and up return at 00433881, which is what freezes obj+0x1370 for good. Every running frame adds 1.0 (0x004C4380) to obj+0x1370; if obj+0x1374 <= it the cursor goes to 2, otherwise CamEvalObjectPath6(obj+0x1350, obj+0x1370) writes obj+0x40/0x44/0x48 and obj+0x64/0x68/0x6C -- the three rotations MASKED to 16 bits -- and obj+0x118 = 1.0. Draw slot 0x1A35 and 0x1A36 override the scale to 2.5, 0x1A36 also adds 0x4000 BAMS to obj+0x68, and 0x1B0E subtracts 5.0 (0x0055D2B4) from obj+0x40. Slot 0x1B0E also plays 0x423A9 on the seating frame. Three shipped spawns: st2evtbl 20432 (0x1A36, path 336) and 75152 (0x1A35, path 338), st5evtbl 7396 (0x1B0E, path 382).

Class 0x33 sub-handler 4, off ScriptedSceneryDispatch33's obj+0x11C switch. A piece of scenery an actor shoves out of its way. Reads the descriptor tail at obj+0x1390: +0x00 the draw slot (stage 1's two are 4196 = komono_7.bin part 0, a chair); +0x04 a shot mesh, and when it is -1 obj+0x124 = obj+0x128 = the f32 at +0x08 (3.5) so the object gets a body sphere instead; +0x0C a script flag that CLEARS obj+0x34 bit 0x8000; +0x0D a script flag that calls ActorDespawn. Bit 0x8000 is the freeze and it is the same bit ColiTestSphereAgainstActors skips on (0x80008000), so a frozen one is not a push target either: the two chairs spawn with descriptor flags 0x8000 set and stage 1 block 1 step 3's set_script_flag 32 is what arms them. While the bit is clear it runs ScriptedPushableApplyPush33, then draws AssetDrawSlot(obj+0x13F0) at obj+0x40..0x48 / obj+0x64..0x6C. L35: Ghidra ends the body at 0x00433C5C, on the MatrixStackPop call, and the real tail runs to 0x00433CD3 -- a second matrix push that writes the transformed origin to obj+0x70..0x78 and then PUSH ESI / CALL 0x00405160 at 0x00433CC6, RegisterForShotTest, which is what puts the object in the per-frame dynamic list a zombie's push can find. The decompilation shows neither, and the xref list of RegisterForShotTest does not name this function.

The move half of ScriptedPushableUpdate33 (class 0x33 selector 4), and it is class 0x30's push arithmetic on a scenery object. If obj+0x138 is non-zero -- the pusher ColiTestSphereAgainstActors recorded there -- it steps obj+0x40/0x44/0x48 by obj+0x13C * 0.1 along obj+0x140..0x148, times 1.8 when the PUSHER's obj+0x34 carries either airborne bit (0x18000000), clears obj+0x138, and re-resolves against the actors. Then it always resolves against the full collision set at the full hit depth. ScriptedPushableSyncSphere33 re-seats the collision sphere after every one of the three moves. Same fraction (0.1) and same airborne multiplier as ZombiePushOutOfWorldAndActors, so an enemy walking into one of these shoves it aside at exactly the speed it would shove another enemy.

Three stores: obj+0x12C = obj+0x40, obj+0x134 = obj+0x48, obj+0x130 = obj+0x44 + obj+0x128 -- the collision-sphere centre from the position, with y raised by the body radius. Called only by ScriptedPushableApplyPush33, once before the push and once after every move it makes, which is why a shoved object's sphere never lags its model. The class-0x33 selector-4 counterpart of ActorUpdateBoundingSphere (FUN_00454AC0) and ThrowerPlaceCollisionSphere (FUN_00449E80).

g_class_handler_pairs class 0x60, and the actor every stage's block 0 step 1 places with spawn_simple just before its wait_script_flag 0xF8. An installer first: if g_GameMode == 3 (boss rush) it calls FUN_00434920 and writes it into obj+0x00; else if g_app_state == 0x0B it calls FUN_00434DA0 and installs that; otherwise it runs the chapter card inline. The card is a two-sub machine on obj+0x1312. Sub 0 (0x00434360) ORs 0x20 into DAT_009A5900, seats the scene light block through FUN_0040E140 with g_scene_index's entry of DAT_009A60CC/D0, calls FUN_0040C2C0(0.3f), runs a per-scene setup arm from the jump table at 0x004348D8 (each fills the eight u16 text slots at 0x007DCBA0..AE), then at 0x004345A4 INCs the sub to 1 and sets obj+0x11C = 0xB4 -- 180 frames -- and falls straight into the sub-1 body. Sub 1 draws the card per scene from the table at 0x004348F0 and every arm falls into the countdown at 0x00434802: a pad skip (g_pad 0x009C9028 bit 2, only once obj+0x11C < 0xA0, or bit 0x20000 unconditionally) forces obj+0x11C = 1; then DEC obj+0x11C, and while it is above 0 the routine returns. At zero it plays the per-scene exit sound (0x18C/0x18D/0x18E through FUN_0041D710), calls FUN_0041D970, sets g_script_flags[0xF8] = 1 at 0x004348C1, clears DAT_009A5900 bit 0x20 and ActorKills itself. That flag write is the whole reason wait_script_flag 0xF8 opens.

g_class_handler_pairs class 0x61 -- the stage-clear card, placed by spawn_simple 0x0097723C in the last step of every result block and gated by the wait_script_flag 0xFE two instructions later. Reads g_civilians_rescued_by_scene[g_scene_index] and the per-scene tables at 0x0055DF50 / 0x0055E044 / 0x0055E04B, then dispatches on obj+0x1312: sub 0 at 0x00434FB1 calls FUN_0041D3A0(0,0,-1) and FUN_0041CFD0(0x10000003), zeroes g_nFiringGate, ORs 0x10 into DAT_009A5900 and sets obj+0x11C = 0x1A4 -- 420 frames, seven seconds; sub 1 at 0x00435107 advances the sub once obj+0x11C has fallen to 0x78 or below, which is when the score tally at 0x00434F4D starts adding up; every sub then falls into the common tail at 0x00435118, which draws the rescue list and ends DEC obj+0x11C / JG return. At zero it sets g_script_flags[0xFE] = 1 at 0x0043567C, clears DAT_009A5900 bit 0x10 and ActorKills itself. Nothing else in the image writes 0x009C72FE -- a whole-image byte search for the address finds exactly this instruction -- so this actor is the only thing that can open a 0xFE gate.

g_class_handler_pairs class 0x62 -- the result card's companion, placed by spawn_simple 0x00977244 immediately before class 0x61 in the same step. Loads texbank 0x16A (FUN_0041D6D0) and sound 0x7C (FUN_0041D650), then reads g_civilians_rescued_by_scene[g_scene_index] and walks the per-scene rescue list at 0x0055DF50 until a 0xFFFF terminator. Writes no script flag: a whole-image sweep of g_script_flags puts every writer outside 0x00435930..0x00435F20.

Per-frame task started by evt opcode 0x2D (play_dialogue). Draws the subtitle line the countdown is currently on.  Task fields: +0x34 variant id, +0x36 frames remaining, +0x38 line index.      frames -= 1;     if (frames == 0 || g_nEvtSkipFlag || DAT_009A2230) { task_end(); return; }     if (DAT_009C911E != 1) {         id = lines[variant * 4 + line];              // u16[] at 0x005919A8         if (frames < line_rec[id].end_frame) line++;         DrawTextCentred(line_rec[id].x_offset, 384.0, line_rec[id].text);         return;     }     FUN_0041C6D0(rec.sprite, rec.x, rec.y, 1,1,1, 0, 7);  THE SPRITE BRANCH IS DEAD. The game always draws text, which makes the script's dialogue recoverable: "We're meeting G over there.", "Get him!" and so on.  Lines advance on a countdown, not a timer: end_frame (line record +0x3E) is "frames still remaining when this line gives way", so the last line of a variant stores 0 and holds to the end.  Line record, 0x40 bytes at 0x0058BC68:     +0x00  f32   x_offset    added to the centred position     +0x04  char  text[0x3A]  NUL-terminated ASCII     +0x3E  u16   end_frame  The early return on g_nEvtSkipFlag means a skipped cutscene drops its subtitles -- a third live consumer of the skip flag beyond 0x40/0x41/0x42 and 0x2E.

g_class_handler_pairs class 0x63, and the commonest spawn_simple record (0x0097724C), placed at the top of most steps in every stage -- installs CheckCutsceneSkipRequest from the task table at 0x005934E4. Detail: clears DAT_009A1A18 and installs FUN_00435F40 into obj+0x00; that update ActorKills the object outright while DAT_009A2D7C is zero, otherwise once DAT_009A1A18 is raised it copies DAT_009A6144 into DAT_009A6148, sets DAT_009A2D74 and DAT_009A2230 to 1, calls FUN_0041D970 and installs FUN_00435FA0, which clears DAT_009A2230 and ActorKills. Writes no script flag.

The standing task that turns a Start press into a cutscene skip. THIS IS THE LINK that makes the whole skip feature work.      if (g_nEvtSkippableRegion == 0) { task_end(); return; }     if (g_nSkipRequested) {         if (cam_end != cam_frame) cam_end = cam_frame;   // end the move here         g_nSkipRequested = 0;         g_nEvtSkipFlag   = 1;         DAT_009A2230     = 1;         AssetDrainAllJobs();         *task = FinishCutsceneSkip;                      // clears 2230, ends     }  Note what the camera line is NOT: DAT_009A6148 is the end frame and DAT_009A6144 the current one (see CamAdvancePathFrame), so this ends the current camera move where it stands rather than fast-forwarding it to the end of the path. That retires the queued event, which is what lets wait_queued_events_done fall through.  AssetDrainAllJobs is there because the waits that would have covered the streaming are about to be skipped past.  Installed from the task table at 0x005934E4 via InitCutsceneSkipWatcher, so nothing calls it directly. That is why Ghidra had not disassembled this block and why an xref search on g_nEvtSkipFlag appeared to show only writers storing 0 -- which led an earlier revision of these notes to the wrong conclusion that the feature was one assignment short of working. It is not; it ships working.
clears DAT_009A2230 one frame later and ends the task
score -> rank 0..7; picks the ending track

Draw one line of dialogue text, centred, as a run of glyph sprites.      void DrawTextCentred(float x_offset, float baseline_y, char *text)  Measures the string, then starts at x = 320.0 - len * 5.6 + x_offset and advances 11.2 px per character across the game's 640x480 screen. Callers pass 384.0 as the baseline, i.e. subtitles sit near the bottom.  Lowercase letters get a per-glyph baseline nudge for descenders and x-height:      g          +4     p q y      +5     b i l      +1     f j t      +2     d h k      +0     everything else in a-z  +3  Characters map to sprite ids through the u16 table at 0x0055E054, indexed by character code; '~' is a literal 0x62D. Each glyph is drawn by FUN_0041C6D0 with colour (1.0, 0.8, 0.8).  Sole caller is DrawDialogueSubtitleTask, the per-frame task evt opcode 0x2D starts.

Allocate the boss-name banner: a task running BossIntroBannerUpdate with a 0xE0-byte block at obj+0x1310 and the caller's record at obj+0x130C. Class 0x19's entrance calls it with g_boss4_intro_banners.

The boss-name banner, and the reason class 0x19's g_script_flags[31] is not immediate. Waits on g_script_flags[record+0x00] (30 for both of class 0x19's records), then counts a frame at +0x04 from 1: eight sprites slide in over frames 1..0x50 along camera path record+0x02, hold and fade until frame record+0x04 (300), and on that frame it restores the camera block, frees slots 0x7ED/0x7EE, sets g_bHudShutterState = 1 at 0x00437F1E and kills itself. That write is the only one in the image that puts the shutter into state 1 from inside a stage, and class 0x19's entrance is waiting for it.

Class 0x51's handler -- THE FISH, settled by asset name: its draw slots 0x1156..0x1169 are fish.bin entries 3 to 22 and the death slots 0xB6F/0xB70/0xB71 are entries 0, 1 and 2. Reads the descriptor tail at obj+0x130C. tail+0x0E == 6 means the record is NOT a fish: it is a GROUP HEADER, which clears the four g_water_attack_slots, copies tail+0x00 into g_water_level and ActorKills itself -- seven of the twenty-eight shipped descriptors are these, and they sit at the world origin. Otherwise: obj+0x124 = 2.1, an 0x84-byte ActorAllocSub at obj+0x1310 holding the whole class, both enemy counters up, sub+0x76 = -1, obj+0x120/0x121 = -1, RegisterEnemySlot, sub+0x1C/0x24 = tail+0x00/+0x04 (the per-axis closing speed), FishBeginRise, then tail+0x0C as the entry mode (0 raises sub+0x6A bit 2 and draws solid, 1 zeroes the alpha to fade in), tail+0x0E the sub-type, tail+0x10 the rise frames, tail+0x12 the bob cycles, tail+0x14 the lunge frames and tail+0x08 the bob amplitude. Installs FishUpdate.

Allocates one class-0x51 FISH at a point -- ActorAlloc(FishUpdate, 0x1314) plus an 0x84-byte sub-block -- with a lifetime at sub+0x7E (0 means 0x50) and a sub-type at sub+0x6C, incrementing both enemy counters. REFUSES while ANY of the four dwords at g_water_attack_slots is non-zero, which is what paces a summoning round to one fish at a time. Writes g_water_level = -24.9 itself. Skips FishBeginRise entirely and calls FishClaimSlotAndLunge, so a summoned fish has no rise and no bob. Class 0x14's two summoning rounds are its only callers.

Class 0x51's per-frame routine: g_cur_actor = obj, then FishCheckShot, FishRunState, FishDraw, FishProjectToScreen and FishRegisterForCameraTracking. The shot is checked BEFORE the state runs, so the frame a fish is hit is the first frame of its death state.

What a PLACED class-0x51 fish starts from. Puts the actor back on sub+0x00..0x08, turns sub+0x1C/0x24 (the tail's per-axis speeds) into a velocity toward g_camera_block_eye by scaling them with the UNIT direction, faces it that way (atan(dx/dz) in BAMS), and zeroes the rest of the block into state 0 with a full alpha and the strip at 0x1156..0x1169. Its sub+0x78 = 1 is a default FishInit overwrites one line later.

The class-0x51 leap begins, or it does not. Claims one of the four g_water_attack_slots -- a random index first, then the lowest free one, -1 if all four are taken -- and the index decides the attack permit: slots 0/1 are player 0 and 2/3 player 1 in a two-player game, and in one player it is (g_active_player == 0) ? 0 : 1. The slot is ALSO where the fish leaps to: a point in the camera's own space at x = +/-1.5, z = -6.0, y = 0 (or 1.0 for sub-type 2) less 2.0 again for the odd slots. dx is forced to 1.0 when it is exactly zero. Writes the whole displacement to sub+0x28/0x2C/0x30, the yaw atan(dx/dz) to sub+0x50 and the pitch atan(dz/dy) to sub+0x58, draws sub-type 2's +/-2 sideways swing into sub+0x80, divides the displacement by sub+0x7E into sub+0x1C/0x20/0x24, records the origin at sub+0x10/0x14/0x18, resets the strip and enters state 2.

Class 0x51's whole damage model, and it has no hit points: it fires only in states 0 to 3 with obj+0x34 bit 3 set, so a fish is only ever shot once. 80 points to whichever of bits 1/2 is set, or to rand() & 1 when both are, and g_player_hit_count only for sub-type 0. PlaySoundId(0x716A9) = COMMON\\BLOOD07_16.WAV. Then the fork on sub+0x6A bit 0: NOT submerged goes to state 4 with a 0.4 kick, a velocity directly away from the camera at half the distance and a tumble drawn on both axes; submerged surfaces to g_water_level + 0.04, splashes, drops g_enemies_present and goes to state 5. Both arms end with the hit bit cleared, SpawnFishBloodCloud, obj+0x34 |= 0x10000, one off g_enemies_alive and the enemy slot, and the permit and attack slot released.
Class 0x51's six-arm switch on sub+0x62. State 2 is the only arm with two calls -- FishStateLunge then FishLungeTestBite, in that order, so a fish that arrives this frame bites this frame.

Class 0x51 state 0. Closes on the camera at sub+0x1C/0x24, keeps sub+0x6A bit 0 in step with g_water_level every frame, winds the alpha up by 0.02 toward 1.0, advances the strip, and hands to state 1 once the timer reaches sub+0x7C.

Class 0x51 state 1, the surface ride: y = sin(sub+0x68) * sub+0x44 + sub+0x04, floored at the home height, with the phase stepped 0x333 a frame and reset every 0x50 frames -- each reset counting a cycle into sub+0x7A. The splash is fired on the CROSSING, not on the state: 0.3 coming out of the water, 0.5 going in, only when the bit is about to change. The pitch snaps to 0xE000 on the first frame of each cycle and winds up 0xCC a frame to a 0xFFFF stop. When sub+0x7A reaches sub+0x78 it calls FishClaimSlotAndLunge; on -1 it retires from both counters, releases everything and FishBeginSwimAway(0x3C).

Class 0x51 state 2. The arc is a sine of the STEP over the duration, not of a clock: sub+0x74 is clamped at sub+0x7E - 1 while the timer runs on to twice that, so a fish that has not connected hangs at the top of its leap for a second duration before FishEndLunge takes it. Sub-type 0 rides its velocity in x and z and takes y from one sine; sub-type 1 adds a second sine at twice the rate and six units of amplitude; sub-type 2 leaves x to the sines -- sub+0x28 plus the +/-2 at sub+0x80 -- and steps y and z linearly. Splashes once, at timer 2.

Ends a class-0x51 leap: state 3 with the timer restarted, the camera slot cleared and the attack permit released -- but NOT the attack slot, which FishStateFallBack holds for another 0x20 frames so the next fish cannot leap through the one still coming down.

Class 0x51 state 3. Thirty-two frames of nothing, then the g_water_attack_slots entry goes back; from 0x20 to 0x3F it falls 0.4 a frame at half its lateral speed; past 0x3F it takes one off each enemy counter, clears its g_hit_slots entry and the permit, and ActorDespawns.

Class 0x51 state 4 -- shot above the water. A ballistic arc at 0.03266 a frame with a tumble on sub+0x50/0x58. SUB-TYPE 1 IS THE ONLY ARM THAT ASKS THE WORLD FOR A FLOOR (QueryGroundHeightAt ten units above itself), and g_coli_hit_surface == 0 means the trace found nothing, so that sub-branch is the WATER case and the other is solid ground, which plays COMMON\\ENE_WALK3_16.WAV and pins the corpse. Every other sub-type waits to fall back through g_water_level, or gives up at 0x1900 frames. All routes drop g_enemies_present and enter state 5.

Class 0x51 state 5 -- dead on the water, or on a floor. y = sin(sub+0x40) * sub+0x2C + sub+0x0C with the centre sinking 0.005 a frame, for 300 frames, then ActorDespawn. sub+0x40 is a FLOAT BAMS phase accumulating sub+0x3C and converted by __ftol masked to 16 bits; the decompiler drops that argument. A corpse that landed on solid ground has a rate of zero, so it lies still and still sinks. Fires two surface rings at timer 1 unless sub+0x6A bit 1 says it is on the ground.

Runs beside class 0x51 state 2 every frame. One distance to g_camera_block_eye, three answers: under 8.0 it calls PlayerTakeDamage(obj+0x121, 1, 9) if it holds a permit and ends the lunge either way; over 200.0 it ends the lunge without a bite; between the two, nothing.

Class 0x51's draw. States 2 and 3 and the default share an arm that, when sub+0x6A bit 2 is set and the fish is below g_water_level, draws a FLATTENED SILHOUETTE at the surface instead -- scale (0.4, 0.01, 0.4) at g_water_level + 0.07 -- and otherwise translates, yaws by sub+0x50 and pitches by the lunge progress or by sub+0x58. Bit 2 also picks AssetDrawSlot over AssetDrawSlotWithAlpha(slot, sub+0x48). State 5 half-turns before pitching.

Writes obj+0x70/0x74/0x78 for a class-0x51 fish in states 0, 1, 2 and 3 by transforming its position through the camera matrix at g_camera_blocks + player * 0x1A4. FishDraw writes the same three fields for the other states from the matrix stack.

The way out for a class-0x51 fish that wanted to leap and found all four attack slots taken. Zeroes the timer, puts a frame count in sub+0x7C, sets sub+0x28 = 0.4 as the silhouette scale and installs FishSwimAwayTick. NOTHING EVER REMOVES THE OBJECT: the frame count is never read and the installed update has no despawn.

The update FishBeginSwimAway installs. Holds the fish at sub+0x04, drifts it along sub+0x1C/0x24 and draws -- the surface silhouette at sub+0x28 scale when sub+0x6A bit 2 is set, the model otherwise. No despawn and no state test; see FishBeginSwimAway.
Offers a class-0x51 fish to the camera in states 0, 1 and 2 only: copies its position to obj+0x100 and calls RegisterForCameraTracking.

Allocates a 0x68-byte task drawing asset slot 0x3A upward at the dying fish's camera-space point, in g_app_state 6 only. NOT SpawnBloodSpray despite the shared first slot: this one draws with an identity matrix at obj+0x70/0x74/0x78 and its update has no last frame.
SpawnFishBloodCloud's update. Loads identity, translates to the stored camera-space point, scales by 0.1 (0.05 with g_wCaptionMode) and draws slot +0x54, then increments it. No termination.

Allocates a 0x68-byte flipbook task at (fish.x, g_water_level - 0.4, fish.z) starting at asset slot 0x1339, with the caller's scale at +0x58 and kind at +0x64. Kind 0 plays COMMON\\SIBUKI3_16.WAV and anything else COMMON\\SIBUKI2_16.WAV -- shibuki, a splash. Called on the surface crossing in state 1 (0.3 out, 0.5 in), at lunge frame 2 (0.6), and on both deaths that meet water (0.8, kind 1).
FishSpawnWaterSplash's update: translate, scale by +0x58, yaw to the camera, draw slot +0x54 and increment it. No termination.

Allocates a 0x68-byte task at (fish.x, g_water_level - 0.2, fish.z) drawing asset slot 0xB71 -- fish.bin entry 2 -- with the caller's scale and a full alpha. Silent. Fired twice on the first frame of state 5 unless the corpse is on solid ground, and once by each of the two deaths that meet water.
FishSpawnSurfaceRing's update: translate, scale (+0x58, 0.2, +0x58) and AssetDrawSlotWithAlpha(+0x54, +0x60). Neither the slot nor the alpha is stepped, and there is no termination.

g_class_handler_pairs class 0x11, and the only creature in the game built on frog.bin. Spawned by evt opcode 0x0C, so the descriptor tail arrives at obj+0x130C and there is no obj+0x1390. Seeds three file-scope globals that every routine in the class uses instead of an argument -- 0x009A26A0 = obj, 0x007DCBC4 = obj+0x194 (the skinned model), 0x007DCBCC = obj+0x40 (position/velocity), 0x007DCBC8 = the 0x38-byte sub-block it allocates through ActorAllocSub and parks at obj+0x1310 -- which means only one class-0x11 object can be mid-update at a time. Reads the tail through FrogArmScriptFromDescriptorTail, snaps y to g_ground_plane_y, writes gravity -0.0272222 to obj+0x5C, takes the CHARACTER TYPE from tail+0x00 (0x1B = frog.bin, 15 bones) into obj+0x1F4 and the motion id from tail+0x02 (0x141 in all four shipped spawns) into obj+0x1B4, builds the skeleton with ActorBuildSkinnedModel, sets obj+0x124 = g_actor_radius_by_char[0x1B] = 10.0 and obj+0x128 = 3.0, raises g_enemies_present and g_enemies_alive, sets obj+0x121 = 0xFF and installs 0x0043A1E0. Four spawns exist in the whole game, all st1evtbl block 3 step 1.

Class 0x11's per-frame body; Ghidra had no function here. Re-seeds the four class globals, writes the 2-D camera distance to sub+0x14, stashes the model root's transformed position in 0x007DCBB8..C0, then runs FrogAwardKillAndEnterDeath, FrogReadNextScriptCommand, g_class11_states[sub+0x04] (the ten-entry table at 0x00592660), FrogIntegrateVelocityAndGravity, FrogDrawAndCycleBone2Slot, ActorRegisterCameraPoint(1.0f) -- 1.0, against 4.0 for a class-0x30 zombie -- and FrogPushOutOfActorCollision. The shot flag is consumed before the state runs and the actor-vs-actor push happens after the draw.

The class-0x11 shot path, and there is no hit-point arithmetic in it: obj+0x11C is stored 0 as a u16 and never compared, so the first shot that raises obj+0x34 bit 3 kills. Latches obj+0x34 bit 0x4000000, sets sub+0x04 = 8 and sub+0x05 = 0, ORs obj+0x34 0x8000, calls ChooseHitPlayerOrder, swaps bone 1's draw slot to 0xB91 (frog.bin 3) and blanks bones 2 and 3, spawns a bone hit sprite on bone 2, picks the shooter from obj+0x34 & 6 (2 -> player 0, 4 -> player 1, else a coin flip), ScoreAddForPlayer(p, 0x50) -- 80 points -- increments g_player_hit_count at 0x009A5C86 + p*0x130, and plays 0x716A9 = COMMON\BLOOD07_16.WAV.

Class 0x11's integrator. Adds obj+0x4C/0x54/0x50 to obj+0x40/0x48/0x44 in that order, then adds obj+0x5C (-0.0272222) to the y velocity only while the actor is above g_ground_plane_y AND sub+0x00 bit 3 is clear. Bit 3 is raised on the frame FrogStateLeapAtPlayer connects and cleared again when the leap's recovery ends, which is what holds the frog in the air on the player's face.

Class 0x11's draw, plus the thirty-model cycle on bone 2. While sub+0x00 bit 1 is set it steps sub+0x0A and derives a triangle wave sub+0x08 = ping-pong over 0..29 with period 59, raising bit 2 on the wrap; the draw is SetSceneLight / DrawSkinnedModelAndShadow(part, obj+0x40, part+0x78) / RestoreSceneLight; then, unless obj+0x34 bit 0x4000000 is set, bone 2's draw slot at part+0x198 = 0xB94 + sub+0x08, which is exactly frog.bin entries 6..35 and ends where bone 3's default slot 0xBB2 begins. Finally it advances the motion cursor at part+0x00 unless obj+0x34 bit 0x4000 -- the freeze the death state sets on the penultimate frame of clip 0x13F.

Class 0x11's actor-vs-actor separation, run last in the frame and skipped entirely while sub+0x04 == 6 (the leap). Transforms part+0x130 through the camera block matrix, takes the translation, and ColiTestSphereAgainstActors it with radius obj+0x128 = 3.0. On a hit it scales g_coli_hit_depth by the distance the actor moved this frame -- 0.05 below 0.1 of travel, by the travel itself up to 0.6, flat above -- times 0.3, and adds that along g_coli_hit_normal_x/z to obj+0x40 and obj+0x48. Writes the point to obj+0x12C..0x134 either way.

Reads class 0x11's descriptor tail (obj+0x130C) into the sub-block: state 0, sub+0x18 = tail+0x04 (trigger camera path), sub+0x1C = tail+0x06 (trigger frame), sub+0x20 = 0x141, sub+0x0C = tail+0x0A (the command cursor). sub+0x10 is the half-width of the wedge in front of the camera the frog may hop into: tail+0x08 when nonzero, else the horizontal half-FOV minus 0x200, computed as -0x200 - ftol(atan2(320.0, g_projection_distance_px) * -10430.378). One caller, FrogInit.

Class 0x11's command reader and, once the list ends, its whole AI. Runs every frame but returns unless sub+0x00 bit 0 is set. While *(s16*)sub+0x0C != -1 it takes the opcode's LOW BYTE as the new state and consumes operands: op 0 takes three s16 (camera path, frame, motion id), op 3 takes one s16 and stores it minus obj+0x68 sign-extended as a relative turn, everything else takes none. At the 0xFFFF terminator the cursor stops for good and the autonomous half takes over: inside 50.0 of the camera it goes to state 6 and CLAIMS g_attack_permits[obj+0x121] -- picking the player from g_players_in_play, g_active_player and which permits are free, and falling back to state 7 if the permit is already held -- and outside 50.0 it rolls a new wander state through the eight-entry jump table at 0x0043A970 (states 0/4/7 -> 1; states 1/3 -> rand()%6 giving 7, 4 or 1; states 2/5/6 unchanged), then downgrades state 1 to 5 inside 53.0 and to 2 inside 76.0.

Two instructions: FLD float ptr [0x009C8E58] / RET. It takes three float arguments -- callers push the actor's x, y and z -- and IGNORES all of them, so it is g_ground_plane_y and not a terrain query, whatever the decompiler's signature says (L1). Four callers, all class 0x11: FrogInit, FrogIntegrateVelocityAndGravity, FrogStateLeapAtPlayer and FrogStateDieTumbleAndSink.

g_class11_states[0]. Substate 0 starts the motion in sub+0x20 (0x141 by default, or op 0's third operand) and falls straight through into substate 1's test: g_active_cam_path == sub+0x18 && g_cam_path_frame >= sub+0x1C raises sub+0x00 bit 0 and the reader takes the next command. Note this reads camera block 0's frame at 0x009A6110, while FrogStateHopWithinScreenWedge's aim reads camera block 2's yaw.

g_class11_states[1], [2] and [3] -- the travelling hop, on clip 0x140 with 0x142/0x143 as the 45-degrees-per-pass turns. GHIDRA DROPS 687 BYTES of this function at 0x0043AAC8-0x0043AD76 and 42 more at 0x0043AF04-0x0043AF2D (L37); the five-arm jump table is at 0x0043B0CC. Substate 0: state 3 uses the absolute turn op 3 already stored, states 1 and 2 compute atan2 to the camera in the actor's frame, offset it by 0x1800 depending on which side of the screen the shot sphere obj+0x70/0x78 sits, and then CLAMP the result into the on-screen wedge -- two screen-edge rays built from sub+0x10 and camera block 2's yaw at 0x009A6418, each backed off by asin(perpendicular distance / 26.0) whenever the frog is within 26 units of that ray -- before drawing a heading out of the surviving window with rand() and clamping to +-0x2000. Substate 1 turns 0x2000 per clip and hands to clip 0x140 once the remaining turn is within 0x2000. Substate 2 launches on motion frame 0x12 at speed -1.0 for state 3, -(10 - rand()%5)*0.1 for state 1, and for state 2 a speed that falls linearly to zero as the camera distance reaches 40.0 so the frog stops 26 units short. Substate 3 halves the residual turn each frame and zeroes the velocity on frame 0x2C; substate 4 asks for the next command when the clip ends.

g_class11_states[4] and [5] -- clip 0x144, no velocity, so the frog does not translate. 37 bytes are dropped by the decompiler at 0x0043B212-0x0043B236 (L37): state 5's substate 0 sets sub+0x18 = atan2 to the camera so it turns to face the player, and JUMPS PAST the sub+0x18 = 0 that state 4 executes. Substate 1 turns 0x40 a frame toward sub+0x18 and raises sub+0x00 bit 0 when the clip ends.

g_class11_states[6] -- class 0x11's attack, reached only from FrogReadNextScriptCommand's autonomous half and only with an attack permit in hand; no shipped command list names it. GHIDRA DROPS 288 BYTES at 0x0043B3F2-0x0043B50E and 75 at 0x0043B62D-0x0043B677, which makes substate 0 look like it can never advance (L37); the six-arm jump table is at 0x0043B85C. Substate 0 picks a landing point 12.5 units in front of the camera, offset sideways by (player*2-1)*3.0 unless g_max_attackers is 1, and (rand()%3-1)*3.0-3.0 in y, nudges it 3.0 further along the intended heading, and picks clip 0x142/0x143 to turn or 0x13E to leap. Substate 1 turns 0x2000 per clip and hands to 0x13E within 0x1000. Substate 2 launches on motion frame 0x1E with a 30-frame ballistic solution -- horizontal (target-pos)/30 and vertical (target-pos)/30 minus gravity*14.5 -- and starts the bone-2 cycle. Substate 3 calls PlayerTakeDamage(obj+0x121, 1, 9) on motion frame 0x3C UNCONDITIONALLY: the hit is timed, not tested. Substate 4 waits for the bone-2 cycle to wrap, then plays 0x13E with a 61-frame fade and turns gravity back on. Substate 5 releases the attack permit, drops BOTH enemy counters and ActorDespawns once the frog is back on the ground -- so a frog that lands its attack leaves the level without ever dying or scoring.

g_class11_states[7]. Substate 0 plays clip 0x141 and arms two counters, sub+0x18 = rand()%0x1A + 0x40 (64..89 frames) and sub+0x1C = sub+0x18 - rand()%0x1A. On the frame the countdown reaches sub+0x1C it raises sub+0x00 bit 1, which starts FrogDrawAndCycleBone2Slot's thirty-model cycle on bone 2, and plays PlaySoundId(0x3716A9) = COMMON\KAERU4_22.WAV -- kaeru, and the decisive evidence with frog.bin that class 0x11 is a frog. The cycle's wrap (bit 2) clears bits 1 and 2 again. At zero it raises bit 0 and the reader picks the next state.

g_class11_states[8], entered only from FrogAwardKillAndEnterDeath; 39 bytes are dropped at 0x0043BB68-0x0043BB8E (L37) and they are the ones that zero the flag word and RELEASE the attack permit. Substate 0 plays clip 0x13F, clears obj+0x34 bit 0x4000, sets bit 0x10000 unless obj+0x34 bit 0x800000 is set and this is the last enemy alive, drops g_enemies_alive, and throws the corpse at 0.5 units a frame along the camera basis's -Z by rotating (0,0,-0.5) through rows 0..2 of the camera block matrix. Substate 1 bounces it on g_ground_plane_y -- y velocity times -0.3 and xz times 0.6 on a live bounce, xz times 0.8 once flat, each axis snapping to zero below 0.05 -- and when everything is zero on the clip's last frame it calls SpawnGroundRingEffect, sets y velocity -0.035 and arms sub+0x18 = 0xB4; it also freezes the clip through obj+0x34 bit 0x4000 on the penultimate frame. Substate 2 counts those 180 frames down, then drops g_enemies_present, clears g_hit_slots[obj+0x3C] and ActorDespawns.

Class 0x40. Allocates N HordeMemberInit objects of 0x13F4 into g_horde_members (0x007DCC20, 10 slots), each carrying its index at +0x131B and the placer's position, selector and count, then ActorKills itself. Selector obj+0x130C: 0 -> one member; 1 -> 8, or 10 in a two-player game, 6 in evt blocks 0x0E/0x12 (8 with two players) and 4 in block 0x19; 2 -> not a spawner at all, it calls FUN_0043DC30 and dies. Nine spawns, all selector 1.

One horde member's constructor, installed by PlaceHorde. Allocates a 0x504 side struct at obj+0x1390, fixes the character type at 0x1D (mol.bin, a six-segment chain) and picks the variant in side+0x68 from g_evt_block_index -- 3->0, 8->1, 0x0E->3, 0x12->4, 0x19->2. Seeds the member's place in the entry formation from g_horde_formation (0x0055E200) and its wander box from 0x0055E568/0x0055E574, increments both enemy counters unless the variant is 2, then installs HordeMemberUpdate.

The horde member's seven-state machine and draw. States: 0 hold, 1 fly the six-segment entry spline from g_horde_formation, 2 wind up, 3 dive at the camera, 4 pull out, 5 wander the box with neighbour avoidance inside 6.0 units, 6 dead. Dies to one shot for 80 points, playing STAGE1_SE or STAGE2_SE PDMG_MORR1/2_44.wav by g_scene_index; draws a ground shadow at slot 0x10D0 on g_camera_fixed_eye_y. Returns immediately while g_active_cam_path is 0x47.

Releases the creature ZombieStateReleaseBodyCreature carries. ActorAlloc(BodyCreatureInit, 0x13F4), then parks the HOST in DAT_007DCBD8 indexed by the host's own object slot obj+0x3C and gives the new actor that index at +0x1350 -- so the creature finds its host through the slot table rather than a pointer. Copies the host's camera-space point obj+0x100..0x108, sets obj+0x120 to 0xFF, and calls FUN_00408E80. Its only caller is that state.

The creature's init, installed by SpawnBodyCreature and replaced at its end by BodyCreatureUpdate. Allocates a 0x504-byte tail into obj+0x1390, seeds obj+0x34 = 1, obj+0x11C = 1, obj+0x134C = 0.3, obj+0x124 = 0.8, obj+0x133C = 1 and state 0, and -- the part that matters to a room gate -- RAISES BOTH g_enemies_present AND g_enemies_alive, so it is a countable enemy the player has to deal with. Its start position is the host's camera-space point transformed back to world.

The creature's per-frame entry; it has no class id, like the thrown weapon, and is reached only through the allocation in SpawnBodyCreature. State 0 rides the HOST's bone matrix at host+0x2C4. State 3 is the flight: it interpolates obj+0x1344 from 0 toward 1 along the tail's start/end pair with a sine arc in y, easing by obj+0x1348 which decays 0.925 a frame down to a floor of 0.005, and spins about X. TWO WAYS OUT. Shot (obj+0x34 bit 8): PlaySoundId(0x3B16A9) COMMON MEET02_22.WAV, 0x50 to the player who fired -- split by a coin flip when both are flagged -- an effect through FUN_00430C50, and state 6. Not shot: past 0.9 it latches and 0x1E frames later FUN_00415300(player, 1, 9) DAMAGES THE PLAYER and it goes to state 4. States 4 and 6 both fall at 0.010888 a frame with the spin clamped to -0x4000 or +0x4000, and below y = -3.0 it drops both enemy counters and despawns. It draws AssetDrawSlot(obj+0x1330 % 0x28 + 0x1D31) -- a FORTY-SLOT sprite loop at 0x1D31.

Class 0x52's handler -- the MOUSE. g_asset_slots maps its draw slots 0x1385..0x138E to mouse.bin entries 0..9, which is one of the binary's two name tables and settles a species docs/formats/spawns.md had as [open]. Sets obj+0x3C = -1 and obj+0x124 = 2.0 (the shot-test radius), allocates a 0x28-byte sub-block at obj+0x1310 and seeds it: +0x26 the subtype from the descriptor tail, +0x0C the 0.4 unit-per-frame speed, +0x00/+0x08 the velocity from the spawn yaw, +0x24 = 0x1385 and +0x22 = 0x138E the first and last frames of the ten-frame strip, +0x20 = 0x1385 + rand()%10 the frame it starts on. Then FUN_00409270 claims a slot in the 14-entry table at 0x009C88C0. Subtype 0 and 1 go to MouseWanderUpdate; subtype 2, 3 and 4 go to MouseBranchTriggerUpdate with the velocity zeroed and the frame pinned to 0x1385 -- but ONLY while g_GameMode == 1, and in arcade the actor despawns on its first frame. Ten spawns: stage 1 block 1 (four of subtype 0), stage 2 block 18 (subtypes 1 and 2), stage 4 block 7 (two of subtype 1) and block 10 (subtypes 3 and 4).

Class 0x52 subtypes 0 and 1: the mouse running about. Sub-state 0 moves by the sub-block's velocity, advances the ten-frame strip at sub+0x20 and wraps it from sub+0x22 back to sub+0x24, and every hundredth frame of its life counter takes a 40 percent chance (rand()%10 < 4) to enter sub-state 1. Sub-state 1 holds for 60 frames, then turns by (rand() & 0xFFF) - (rand() & 0xFFF) BAMS and rebuilds the velocity from the new yaw at the 0.4 speed. Subtype 1 draws through SubmitSlotWithSceneLightArray and subtype 0 through AssetDrawSlot -- the same model, lit or not. The life counter at sub+0x1C despawns it past 600 frames, so a wanderer leaves on its own after ten seconds and writes no route.

Class 0x52 subtypes 2-4: a shootable route-branch trigger that runs away. Sub-state 0 stands on frame 0x1385 and waits for obj+0x34 bit 3; on a hit, and only when the s16 at 0x00564444 + subtype*2 is non-zero (18, 10, 10 for subtypes 2, 3, 4 -- what those numbers are is [open]), it writes g_script_branch_var = the SIGNED BYTE at 0x00564442 + subtype: subtype 2 -> 2, subtype 3 -> 1, subtype 4 -> 2. The hit bit is cleared whether or not the gate passed. Sub-state 1 rebuilds the velocity from the spawn yaw and picks the per-subtype sub-state 2, 3 or 4, each of which runs the strip and moves until it passes its own bound -- z < -1940.8 for subtype 2, x > -87.0 for 3, x < -184.0 for 4 -- and then sub-state 10, which despawns. The two tables at 0x00564442/0x00564444 overlap a double and a float and are only valid for indices 2..4: the adjacent-array shape, indexed from a base chosen so the used entries land.
Class 0x15. Spawns N copies of a prop spaced by a delta vector; each samples the wave field for its height.
Reads {amplitude, wavelength, speed} from the descriptor tail on its first tick, installs WaveEvalTravelling, then advances the source's phase by speed every frame.

One travelling source's contribution. phase = (|cos yaw| > 0.5 ? cos(yaw)*p.z : sin(yaw)*p.x) + src.phase; height = cos(2*pi*phase/wavelength) * amplitude. The 65536 scale and the BAMS cosine make it a plain sinusoid truncated to BAMS resolution. FPU args are dropped by the decompiler -- read from the disassembly.
Same setup with WaveEvalCircular, then walks the source itself along its BAMS yaw at speed -- x += sin(yaw)*speed, z += cos(yaw)*speed.
One circular source's contribution. r = hypot(p.x-src.x, p.z-src.z); height = cos(2*pi*r/wavelength) * amplitude * max(0, 1 - r*0.01), so a ripple dies at 100 units.

Class 0x16. Allocates the 0x2C-byte wave-field manager and records the water plane Y from the spawn descriptor's y -- the descriptor's x and z are ignored, so the field is a global plane height, not a placed object.
Class 0x17. Claims one of eight source slots, copies the spawn position and its three orientation words into it, and picks travelling or circular from g_wave_source_kinds by obj+0x11C.
Sums every active source's contribution at a point. This is a height QUERY for floating objects -- the water surface itself is static level geometry and is never displaced by it.

Class 0x43's handler and a PLACER, not the actor: it allocates a 0x2A0-byte object running OwlUpdateAndResolveShot and then ActorKills itself. The species is settled twice over -- OwlDrawBodyChain's sixteen AssetDrawSlot ids all resolve to owl.bin, and the death sound is COMMON2\FUKUROU1/2_22.wav, fukurou being Japanese for owl. In a one-player game it keeps only member 0 of subtype 0 and members 0-1 of every other subtype, killing the rest outright. obj+0x228 = descriptor+0x22 - 1 is the member index 0..3 and obj+0x224 = descriptor+0x25 the subtype 0..3; the fourteen shipped spawns are all opcode 0x09 so there is no obj+0x1390 tail. obj+0x1F0 is bams(atan2(camEyeX - x, camEyeZ - z)) frozen at spawn -- the decompiler drops the whole FPU sequence at 0x00445EB3. Subtype 0 starts in state 4, subtype 2 in state 3, subtypes 1 and 3 in state 0. It stamps four words it owns alone: 0x007DCC64 = 0.03 (read by nothing), 0x007DCC68 = 0.06 (the approach-spline rate), 0x007DCC50 and 0x007DCC54 = 0.

Class 0x43's per-frame entry. obj+0x34 bit 3 is the WHOLE damage model -- the class calls no ResolveHit, no DispatchHit and no ActorApplyDamage, and nothing decrements obj+0x11C -- so one bullet kills. A subtype-0 owl is invulnerable until g_cam_path_frame reaches 682.0 (FILD/FCOMP at 0x004460EA), which applies to no other subtype. Death pays 80 to the player named by bits 1/2 (a coin flip when both are set), gives back g_enemies_alive, g_enemies_present and the enemy slot, releases g_class43_attack_token if the owl was in state 4, launches the corpse along the camera yaw and swaps obj[0] for OwlCorpseFallAndSettle. Then it dispatches g_class43_states[obj+0x220] (0x00592944, 7 entries used), steers obj+0x68 toward either the velocity heading or the camera depending on the state, draws, and publishes obj+0x70/74/78 for ShotTestSphere against a radius of 1.5 at obj+0x124. It never writes obj+0x12C, so its actor-versus-actor push entry is degenerate.

g_class43_states[0]. The staggered launch: g_class43_launch_delay (0x00592940, s8[4] = {0,1,2,3}, the four bytes immediately before the state table) times 20 frames per member. Member 0 has no delay and goes straight to state 3 as soon as g_class43_attack_token is -1, g_scene_state_major_entered is 2 and a player is in play; members 1-3 play COMMON2\HABATAKI6_16.wav and go to state 2 toward a HARD-CODED holding circle -- (-640, spawnY+10, -950) radius 6.28 dwell 55 for subtype 1, (-415, 140, -2750) radius 6.28 dwell 88 for everything else. obj+0x240 winds BACKWARDS from 44 while waiting and the member-0 exit does not reset it, so a long wait would underflow the wing-beat slot; in the shipped data the gate opens on the first frame.

g_class43_states[1]. Circles obj+0x1DC/1E0/1E4 at radius obj+0x290 (6.28), obj+0x1F4 stepping +0x3E0 for subtype 1 and -0x3E0 otherwise -- 992 BAMS a frame, a lap in about 66. Steering gain 0.014, pitch eased toward 0x1000 at 5% and obj+0x218 toward 0 at 20%. Leaves for state 3 once obj+0x24C passes obj+0x248 (55 or 88) AND g_class43_attack_token is -1 -- that token is what makes the flock attack one at a time.

g_class43_states[3]. Rides a uniform quadratic B-spline through g_class43_approach_curves (0x00564550, s16[4 subtype][4 member][4 point][3], 384 bytes ending exactly where the float pool begins), advancing obj+0x29C by 0x007DCC68 = 0.06 only while inside 4.0 of the current point and stepping the segment at 0.99. Speed capped at 1.5, steering gain ramping 0.003 a frame to 0.15 (subtype 2) or 0.2. At the end of segment 1 subtypes 0/1/3 take g_class43_attack_token and enter state 4 with obj+0x244 = 1, the arm that homes on the camera eye; SUBTYPE 2 INSTEAD COASTS through obj+0x24C and enters with obj+0x244 = 2, so a stage-2 block-14 owl never homes in on its first pass.

g_class43_states[2]. A straight lerp from obj+0x1C4/1C8/1CC to the holding point obj+0x1B8/1BC/1C0 with obj+0x270 climbing 0.0175 a frame to 1.0, plus a 30-frame vertical bob of 0.15. Pitch eases toward 0x3000 when obj+0x3C is set and 0x1000 when it is not, and NOTHING IN THIS CLASS EVER WRITES obj+0x3C, so the target is always 0x1000. Within 5.0 of the holding point it goes to state 1 if obj+0x230 is set (which state 0 always sets on this path) and to state 3 otherwise.

g_class43_states[4], and the strike. GHIDRA'S FUNCTION BODY SKIPS 395 BYTES: the listing jumps 0x004470EC -> 0x0044727C past a MatrixStackPop it has marked no-return, and those bytes are the entire obj+0x244 != 1 trajectory -- a lerp onto the camera with a lateral sway of sin(obj+0x1FC) * obj+0x294 rotated by obj+0x1F0, a 0.2 bob and a bank eased toward sin(obj+0x1FC + 0x4000) * 4096. Read it with disassemble_bytes. The obj+0x244 == 1 arm is a plain lerp onto the camera eye whose rate obj+0x274 accelerates by 0.005 a frame. Inside 5.0 units of the camera eye it calls PlayerTakeDamage(obj+0x121, 1, 9) if that player is in state 5 -- one life, no clip frame, no attack permit but the token -- then picks an escape direction, builds a retreat circle from a four-arm jump table at 0x00447678, sheds 8 feathers, releases the token and goes to state 5.

g_class43_states[5]. Half an orbit of the retreat circle built by state 4, radius 5/7/6/8 by subtype from a jump table at 0x00447C04, obj+0x1F4 stepping obj+0x234 * 0x1F0. Pitches toward the climb angle by an eighth each frame and floors it at 0. Past 0x8800 (or below 0x7800 going the other way) it coasts, damping 0.9, and on the frame obj+0x240 hits 18 it plays COMMON2\HABATAKI6_16.wav, retakes g_class43_attack_token and re-enters state 4 with obj+0x244 = 2. THE LOOP IS 4 -> 5 -> 4 FOR EVER: an owl only leaves through being shot.

Class 0x43's whole renderer -- a hand-built matrix chain, no skeleton and no character type. GHIDRA'S BODY ENDS AT 0x00447D40 on a no-return MatrixStackPop and the routine really runs to 0x00447FA4, so three of its four limb chains are in no decompilation. Sixteen AssetDrawSlot ids, all owl.bin: 0xBBF/0xBC0 the body alive/dead on obj+0x34 bit 0x1000000, 0xBC1 + obj+0x240 the 30-frame beat, 0xBF8 + a 16-frame ping-pong of the global frame counter for the head (frozen at 0 in state 6), 0xBF1/0xBF4/0xBF2 an inner chain, and 0xBF6/0xBBE/0xC08+n and 0xBF5/0xBBD/0xC18+n for the mirrored outer pair whose 15-frame strip is stepped by obj+0x21C during the dive only. 15 pushes against 15 pops on both the live and the dead path.

Class 0x43's target selection, called on every dive launch. Two players: a rand() coin, and an aim offset obj+0x1E8/1EC of obj+0x204/60 units placed 0xC000 or 0x4000 off the camera yaw so the two owls come in on opposite sides. One player: obj+0x121 follows g_active_player when that is 0 or 1 and is LEFT ALONE when it is -1 or 2, and the offsets stay zero.

Evaluates g_class43_approach_curves at (obj+0x298, obj+0x29C) into the steering target obj+0x1AC/1B0/1B4. The control-point index is obj+0x298 + (obj+0x228 + obj+0x224*4)*4, so four points per (subtype, member) and two spline segments; the weights come from FUN_0042DFD0, the uniform quadratic B-spline basis ((1-t)^2/2, (1-t)t + 1/2, t^2/2) shared with class 0x40. Every row's first control point is its descriptor's spawn position, which is what says the indexing is not adrift.

Class 0x43's corpse -- installed into obj[0] by OwlUpdateAndResolveShot, so it replaces the update rather than being a state. Gravity -0.020415, a tumble on obj+0x64 driven by obj+0x1F8, a per-subtype landing, then 121 frames of drawing under a second light block (FUN_0041DC70/FUN_0041DCC0) before ActorDespawn. Subtype 0 falls down a stairwell: two five-point polylines at 0x005928C8 (f32[2][5][3], 0x78 bytes ending exactly at g_class43_launch_delay) reflect its z velocity, a wall at x = -739 stops it, and a thirteen-step floor from y=45 to y=33 bounces it with COMMON\DAMAGE5_22.WAV. Subtype 1 settles against a plane through OwlTestPositionBelowPlane; subtype 2 bounces once inside a box and settles at y = -35.98; subtype 3 splashes into water at y = -25 with COMMON\SIBUKI8_16.WAV.
Allocates the 0x80-byte splash the subtype-3 corpse makes when it reaches y = -25, seeded with the corpse's x and z and a fixed y of -25.0.

The splash's update: AssetDrawSlot(0x1339 + n) -- common.bin 307..336 -- one frame per tick, ActorKill past frame 29. Its tail is past a no-return MatrixStackPop and is invisible in the decompilation.
Returns 1 when a*x + b*y + c*z + d <= 0 for the actor's obj+0x40/44/48. Its one caller is the subtype-1 corpse landing, which tests the plane (0, 0.97903, 0.20372, 140.1687).

The one steering primitive every class-0x43 flight state uses: velocity += ((target - position) - velocity) * gain, componentwise, on obj+0x1A0/1A4/1A8 against obj+0x1AC/1B0/1B4. The gain is the whole difference between the states -- 0.003 gliding to the holding point, 0.014 circling, a ramp to 0.15/0.2 on the spline, obj+0x270 * 0.03 in the dive.

Scatters N 0x80-byte feather objects running OwlFeatherDriftAndDraw in a +-0.5 box around the owl, each with a random drift target within +-3, a fall rate of -0.0215..-0.0185, a spin and a tumble. 40 on death, 8 on each strike.

One shed feather: eases toward its drift target, re-rolls the target every half turn of its phase and ActorKills after eight of them. Draws AssetDrawSlot(0xBF0) -- owl.bin 51 -- at scale 0.15 under translate, RotZ, RotY and a fixed RotX(0x4000).

Allocates the 0x13F4-byte decal the corpse leaves where it settles, with a 120-frame life at obj+0x1330 and the caller's scale at obj+0x1340. Plays STAGE1_SE\BOBBLE1_22.wav when g_scene_index is 0 and STAGE2_SE\BOBBLE1_22.wav otherwise.

The decal's first phase: counts obj+0x1330 down from 120 and draws AssetDrawSlot(0x1A38) -- common.bin 371 -- with its x and z scaled by cos(obj+0x1320) * obj+0x1340 * 3. At zero it hands over to OwlGroundImpactRingFadeOut.
The decal's second phase: 40 more frames of AssetDrawSlotWithAlpha(0x1A38, (40 - n) * 0.025) at a fixed scale, then ActorKill.

Class 0x20's handler, and an Init. Everything comes from the parameter tail at obj+0x1390: tail+0x00 (s8) the character type into obj+0x1F4, tail+0x01 (s8) a SUB-TYPE into obj+0x130C, tail+0x02/+0x04 (s16) the removal trigger (g_active_cam_path == tail+0x02 and g_cam_path_frame >= tail+0x04), tail+0x06 (s16) the motion into obj+0x1B4 -- and ZERO there means pick one of g_class20_idle_motions (0x005647A4) with rand() & 3. Sub-type 2 also reads four floats at tail+0x08..+0x14 as an x/z BOX. Then ActorBuildSkinnedModel, obj+0x1F8 |= 2, obj+0x194 = rand() (a random phase), obj+0x12EC = OneHitTargetBoneDrawHook, obj+0x120 = 0xFF (no camera slot), obj+0x3C = -1 (no hit slot), and obj+0x124 = g_actor_radius_by_char[type]. In g_app_state 10 it raises obj+0x34 bit 0x8000 INSTEAD of setting the radius, which takes the actor out of the shot test entirely. Installs OneHitTargetUpdate, or OneHitTargetHoldDrawn when g_GameMode == 2 and g_evt_block_index == 0xD.

Class 0x20's per-frame routine, and the whole of what the class is: a skinned actor that DIES TO ANY ONE HIT. It has no hit points -- nothing subtracts from obj+0x11C anywhere in the class -- so the branch on obj+0x34 bit 3 (MarkActorShot's) is the entire damage model. Not shot: the removal test on the tail's cam path and frame, then g_hit_slots[obj+0x3C] = 0 and ActorDespawn. Shot: walk all 16 bone records at obj+0x280 + bone*0x90, and for each whose +0x00 has bit 3, swap in g_pBoneEffectSlots[type][bone][0] when that slot is > 2, spawn the hit sprite through SpawnBoneHitSprite, and score -- bone 2 pays 120 plus g_head_combo_bonus and then adds 10 to it, any other bone pays 10 and ZEROES the combo, both incrementing g_player_hit_count. Then 80 more to the player named by obj+0x34 bits 1/2 (rand() & 1 if neither), obj+0x34 bit 0 cleared, DAT_009A244A incremented, ActorSetMotionBlended(obj+0x194, 988, 0, 5) and on to OneHitTargetPlayDeathClip. obj+0x130C then selects the idle behaviour: 1 spins the yaw by +0x40 or -0x40 BAMS a frame depending on whether the s16 at obj+0x11C is non-zero, 2 clamps x and z into the tail's box and turns 0x100 BAMS away at each wall, 0 does neither. Ends with DrawSkinnedModelAndShadow, obj+0x194 += 1, obj+0x34 bit 3 cleared and RegisterForShotTest when bit 0 is set.

Class 0x20's death state. Draws, steps obj+0x194, and when the play cursor obj+0x19C reaches g_motion_play_length[obj+0x1B4] it UNDOES that step -- so the clip holds its last frame -- sets obj+0x1330 = 0x78 as a 120-frame countdown, calls SpawnGroundRingEffect and goes to OneHitTargetSinkAndDespawn. In g_GameMode 2 block 0xD with DAT_009C72F2 set it diverts to OneHitTargetHoldDrawn instead.

Class 0x20's corpse. Draws (without stepping the motion, so the pose is held), counts obj+0x1330 down from 120 and sinks obj+0x44 by 0.04 a frame; at zero it clears g_hit_slots[obj+0x3C] and calls ActorDespawn. Two seconds of body, sunk 4.8 units.

Class 0x20's held state, reached only in g_GameMode 2 (arcade) block 0xD. It draws the actor and does nothing else -- no motion step, no shot test, no removal -- until DAT_009C72F2 is clear and DAT_009C72F1 set, at which point it clears obj+0x34 bit 3, calls RegisterForShotTest and returns the object to OneHitTargetUpdate. That pair of bytes is written by FUN_00497640/FUN_00497760 and read by ZombieAdvanceMotion, CivilianUpdate and class 0x31 as well; what they are is [open].

Class 0x20's per-bone draw callback, installed at obj+0x12EC by OneHitTargetInit. Switches on the skeleton node's bone index at node+0x14: bones 4, 7, 11 and 14 draw the node's own asset slot and then a second asset from the node's attachment record at node+0x18, translated by that record's three floats; bone 2 draws at DOUBLE SCALE in g_GameMode 1 when DAT_009C88A8 is set; every other bone draws its slot plainly. Renderer-only -- it writes nothing to the actor.

Class 0x31, subtypes 0x16-0x19. Subtype 0x16 is zsass.bin and puts asset slots 0x1FA2 and 0x1F9E into bone 5 and bone 8's draw slots (obj+0x4DC / obj+0x68C) -- the hands, holding an item, in place of the bare-hand parts 0x1F9F and 0x1F9B. Stage 2 block 5 spawns two of them at y=87 with 130 hit points, out of walking reach, so the item is thrown. Seeds obj+0x136C = (s16)obj+0x1316 | 0x180000 -- the descriptor's +0x20 word, so the starting surface, the draw-path bit and the throw-table bit all come from the spawn record -- then derives the stance as 3*bit8 + 2*bit7 + bit6 and writes obj+0x134C = 0.0/1.0/2.0/3.0 for it, raising obj+0x136C bit 5 for a non-ground stance. obj+0x1320 and obj+0x1324 take the two 16-bit outputs of FUN_004016B0, i.e. BAMS angles, not the frame counters other classes keep there. Installs ThrowerDrawBonePart at obj+0x12EC and ThrowerPushOutOfWorld at obj+0x12F0. Its state machine is g_class31_states (0x00592960), 36 entries, dispatched by EnemyThrowerUpdate.
Class-0x31 update: a cooldown, a pre-hook, dispatch through g_class31_states, then velocity += acceleration and position += velocity -- this class integrates ballistically, unlike class 0x30.

Class 0x31's per-frame shot drain, run before the state dispatch. Calls DispatchHit -- which is where ResolveHit actually applies the damage -- then walks g_hit_player_order (0x009C8908; it is NOT g_hit_slots), writes the bone index to obj+0x1368, and runs ThrowerShotFeedback. Unless obj+0x34 bit 0x100, hit result 5, or obj+0x136C bit 0x200000 already latched, it releases the attack permit and picks the reaction: on the killing blow state 2 with voice kind 2 for bone 2 else 1; alive and obj+0x34 bit 0x2000 clear, state 0x21 for character type 0x18, state 1 when already in state 7 and on the ground, otherwise state 2 -- and obj+0x136C bit 0x400000 latches a re-entry when a reaction was already running. It never writes obj+0x1364, which is where ZombieOnShot puts the hit result.  Its voice kinds are the same rule as ZombieOnShot's, which is what makes the reading a rule rather than one function's habit: 00449a76 CMP EAX,0x2 on the hit result, kind 2 when it is 2 and kind 1 otherwise (00449A7E and 00449A8B).

Class 0x31's copy of ActorShotFeedback. Forces g_hit_result to 5 while obj+0x34 bit 0x100 is set, so a downed thrower only ricochets. Result 1 on bone 2 with head model 0x2002 swaps in 0x2015, sets obj+0x136C bits 0x6000000 -- the knocked-down latch that later routes states 1 and 2 into the get-up -- and shouts voice kind 3; otherwise blood at 0.75, 0.5 for result 2, 1.0 for result 3, and nothing at all for result 4. Result 5 spawns sprite 0x51 for character type 0x18 else 3, and clinks 0x1516A9 for type 0x17, 0x0F16A9 for 0x19, 0x1116A9 otherwise.  Its own kind-0 site is 00449D11, unguarded -- the class's shot feedback plays the hurt voice where ZombieOnShot gates the same kind on the result not being 5.

the per-frame collision hook EnemyThrowerInit installs at obj+0x12F0; class 0x30's slot holds ZombiePushOutOfWorldAndActors. Push out of actors (radius*2/3, depth*0.1, x/z only) on bit 0x100000, out of the world (full radius, full depth, all three axes) on bit 0x80000, then ThrowerSnapToSurface in states 7 and 8 only. EnemyThrowerInit seeds both bits

class 0x31's ActorUpdateBoundingSphere. obj+0x12C = pos, with y lifted 1.4*radius on the ground, LOWERED 1.4*radius on the ceiling (bit 0x100) and level on a wall (bits 0xC0). Not class 0x30's radius+constant
Class 0x31's copy of ZombieAdvanceMotion.

Class 0x31's per-bone draw callback, installed into obj+0x12EC by EnemyThrowerInit. Aims bone 2 at the camera through FUN_00453BE0, then draws the part id from g_skeleton_node_out. Character type 0x18's parts 0x1FED and 0x1FF1 grow a companion piece by 0.025 a frame clamped at 1.0 under a Y-only scale; part 0x1FB9 ping-pongs a morph weight over 120 frames at 1/60 a frame; parts 0x2016 and 0x204A cycle 0x2017 and 0x204B plus the global frame counter modulo 0x32. The 0x1FF0 arm is unreachable -- the guard admits only 0x1FED and 0x1FF1 but the branch compares against 0x1FEE -- so 0x1FF4 is always drawn.

Draws one part for class 0x31, choosing the engine entry point: FUN_004185E0 when obj+0x136C bit 0 is set AND the global at 0x009A2BB4 (written by EvtOpSetSceneLighting14) is non-zero, else FUN_00418560. Bit 0 is never written by class-0x31 code -- it is seeded from the spawn descriptor's +0x20 word via obj+0x1316, and 18 of the 51 shipped class-0x31 spawns set it. What the alternate entry point does is [open].
As ThrowerDrawPart, but takes a second argument -- the alpha at obj+0x138C at every call site -- and passes it to FUN_00418620 or FUN_004185A0. Same obj+0x136C bit 0 / 0x009A2BB4 selector.

Picks between ThrowerDrawPartWithAlpha and ThrowerDrawPart on obj+0x136C bit 2 (TEST byte ptr [EAX + 0x136c], 0x4 -- f6806c13000004 at 0x0044A285), which is the bit EnemyThrowerInit, ThrowerStateCorpseBlink, ThrowerStateGrabPlayer and ThrowerStateBlinkInThreeHops raise. That bit is what makes obj+0x138C reach the draw at all.

[likely] Draws the part a skeleton node names: MOVSX EAX, word ptr [arg+0x14] indexes the 0x90-stride table at 0x009CA0A4 and the part id is that record's first dword. Character type 0x18 goes through ThrowerDrawPartAlphaIfBlinking with obj+0x138C; every other type through ThrowerDrawPart.

The alternate obj+0x12EC draw hook, installed by EnemyThrowerInit when g_GameMode and DAT_009C88A8 are both 1 (item code 0x15) alongside doubling obj+0x3A4. Draws nothing while DAT_009C88A8 is clear, and wraps ThrowerDrawBonePart in a 2x scale for bone 2 only.

Class 0x31 state 1, the stumble. Clamps obj+0x1368 -- which ThrowerOnShot set to the bone index -- to 15, looks the group up in g_bone_reaction_group and the motion in g_class31_hit_reactions[set], and cross-fades it over 0x14 frames for bones under 9 or hard-sets it for 9 and above, so a leg shot cuts where an arm shot blends. On the clip's last frame it clears obj+0x34 bit 0x40000000 and obj+0x136C bit 0x400000, then goes to state 17 if obj+0x136C bit 0x4000000 is set -- which only a decapitation sets -- and otherwise asks ThrowerPickNextState.

Class 0x31 state 2, the knockdown and the death fall. Sub 0 clears the surface bits, plays g_class31_motion_sets[set][5] -- the airborne clip, 0x3A6 / 0x3A4 / 0x1BC / 0x3A6 by set -- blended on a first entry and hard-rewound on a re-entry (obj+0x136C bit 0x400000, which also counts obj+0x1328 up), and launches ThrowerBeginKnockbackArc while obj+0x1328 is at most 1. Sub 1 rides the arc, freezing the pose at frame 35/20/44/44 by character type, then sets obj+0x5C = -0.05444444. Sub 2 falls until QueryGroundHeightAt(x, y+4.5, z) catches it or obj+0x1338 reaches 0x78, snaps, records the surface in obj+0x1350, bounces with vel.y *= -0.5 and vel.xz *= 0.5, plays effect 0x46 and sound 0x2716A9, and re-bounces while the vertical speed is over 0.15 -- character type 0x16 never re-bounces. Sub 3 splits: alive and not on surface 0x5A, it lies still for (rand()%10+1)*3 frames, plays 0x11B unless it is character 0x17 and gets up through sub 4 into state 0x11 when obj+0x136C bit 0x4000000 is set or ThrowerPickNextState otherwise; dead, or on surface 0x5A, it waits for obj+0x1F1 -- the motion block's clip-ran-out flag -- and goes to state 3 for character 0x16 or ThrowerEnterCorpseState for the rest, spawning effect 0x61 on a 0x5A landing in scene 3 block 4.

Class 0x31 state 3, reached by character type 0x16 only. Sub 0 hard-rewinds the death clip -- 0x11E for 0x16, 0x1BC for 0x17, 0x11D for 0x18 and 0x19 -- then releases the attack permit and the tracking slot in that order; sub 1 waits for obj+0x19C to reach the clip's length minus one and hands to ThrowerEnterCorpseState. Entered from state 2 sub 3 and from ThrowerStateFallToSurface; the switch still covers the other three character types, which is residue.

Class 0x31 state 4, the corpse for every character but 0x18. Sub 0 spawns the ground ring -- from y+5.5 when the frozen clip is 0x3A6, because the ring is placed from the feet -- sets obj+0x1330 to 0x78 and obj+0x34 bit 0x20000; then 120 frames of y -= 0.04 while obj+0x194, the motion play cursor, is pinned to a pose frame drawn from g_class31_corpse_frames_m11d, _m11e, _m1bc or _m3a6 by rand()%17>>4, so the second entry comes up once in seventeen. On the last frame it frees the tracking slot if this was the last enemy present, frees the hit slot and despawns.

Class 0x31 state 5, the corpse for character type 0x18. The same opening as state 4 -- the ground ring, obj+0x1330 = 0x78, obj+0x34 bit 0x20000 and the same pose-frame pin -- but it does not sink: it flickers, setting obj+0x138C to 1.0 and clearing obj+0x136C bit 2 on an even counter and 0.0 with the bit set on an odd one, testing the parity before the decrement so the first frame is visible, then despawns the same way after 120 frames.

Class 0x31's leave-the-field helper, and the routine sitting in state slot 6. Retires from the alive count and then the present count, releases the attack permit, frees the tracking slot and clears obj+0x34 bit 0 before ActorDespawn. Called directly by ThrowerStrikeConnect and ThrowerStateGrabPlayer; nothing anywhere writes 6 to obj+0x1310, so it is never entered as a state.

Class 0x31's next-state router, called from states 7, 1 and 17. Dispatches on the ground distance to the camera: d <= 30 (15 for character type 0x17 standing on surface 0x35) goes to state 8; otherwise the band is 1 for 40 < d <= 50 and 2 everywhere else, and it draws a candidate state from g_class31_action_picks[set][band][(rand()>>4)%10 + (obj+0x1318 & 7)*10] and offers it to ThrowerTryEnterState, latching obj+0x135C and obj+0x136C bit 0x2000 on success and falling back to state 7 on refusal. Band 0 of the table is never reached and the band != 0 test is dead code.

Gate for a proposed class-0x31 state on the current actor; writes obj+0x1310 and obj+0x1312 and returns 1 only if it is legal. 7 always; 8 only when ThrowerTryClaimAttackSlot FAILS and 9 only when it succeeds; 0xC and 0xD need a permit and refuse character type 0x18; 0xE and 0xF need obj+0x136C bit 0x20 clear and a successful ThrowerFindWallBeside at -1.0 or +1.0; 0x10 needs bit 0x20 clear and ThrowerFindCeilingAbove; 0x1D and 0x1E only from state 7 and only when ThrowerHasBareHand; 0x1F needs ThrowerBothHandsArmed plus a permit; 0x20 needs a permit and ground surface 0x35; everything else returns 0.

Class 0x31 state 7, the hub. Plays the idle for the actor's current stance -- the ground picks a walk variant from g_class31_motion_sets, the three wall and ceiling stances have their own clips 0x138, 0x137 and 0x131 (0x20F, 0x20C and 0x212 for character type 0x18) -- turns toward the camera with TurnActorAwayFromPointTestArrival at 0x200 a frame, then offers state 0x1D (0x1E for character 0x18, the re-arm) to ThrowerTryEnterState and otherwise asks ThrowerPickNextState what to do next. An actor off the ground does not turn. Ends by emitting the movement trail with ThrowerEmitGroundDust(0x5A).

Class 0x31 state 8. Idles in the pose its stance names -- 0x129, 0x124 or 0x134 off the ground, the motion set's own idle pair on it -- until ThrowerTryClaimAttackSlot succeeds, then plays sound 0x2416A9 and goes to state 9, the pounce, for character types 0x16, 0x18 and 0x19. Character 0x17 instead goes to state 0x20 when it is standing on surface 0x35 above the camera, else state 0x18.

Copies the current attack's arc motion script into the actor's slot. The stance row is bit6 + 2*(bit7 + 2*bit17) + 3*bit8 of obj+0x136C, the entry is g_class31_melee_attacks[obj+0x130C] + (obj+0x131A + row*4)*0x10, and the pointer at that entry's +0x00 is copied as 12 dwords into g_arc_scripts at 0x009C8AA0 + obj+0x3C*0x30.

Class 0x31 state 9: off the roof and into shot. ThrowerStatePathFollow hands here for every character type but 0x17, having claimed an attack permit first. Sub 0 picks a landing point with ThrowerPickLandingPoint, faces g_camera_yaw_bams and begins an arc to it with step 1; the arc is stepped, the actor is re-snapped to the point each frame outside Training Mode, and at the end of the clip it goes to state 10.

Class 0x31 state 10, the leap back out of the player's face after a pounce. Picks a point 5 units to one side of the camera and 50 in front of it in the camera's yaw-only frame, traces a vertical segment there from y-1000 to y+1000 with ColiTraceSegmentAllSets and lands on what it hits -- falling back to g_camera_fixed_eye_y when the trace misses -- then arcs to it with ActorArcBeginToWaypoint under a three-stage arc motion script chosen by character type and stance. Plays the motion set's landing clip and returns to state 7 once 0x5A frames have passed or the actor is 50 units clear.

Class 0x31 state 11.
