Sub 0 records the start height in obj+0x1388, sets obj+0x34 bit 0x2000 and plays 0x1BC for character type 0x17 and 0x3A5 for everything else; sub 1 falls under obj+0x5C = -0.05444444 until QueryGroundHeightAt(x, y+1.0, z) catches it, then picks a landing clip by the drop measured against g_coli_hit_y -- over 15 units the same long clip again, between 10 and 15 the short 0x1BA for type 0x17 and 0x3A9 otherwise, under 10 none at all -- and zeroes obj+0x1388 whenever it plays one, which is what lets sub 2 exit at once instead of waiting the fall clip out. Sub 2 goes to state 10 when obj+0x34 bit 0x20000000 is set and state 7 otherwise; a dead actor, or any actor whose landing surface is 0x5A, is killed and routed to state 3 for character 0x16 or ThrowerEnterCorpseState for the rest.

The gate on class-0x31 states 14 and 15. Refuses unless the actor is facing the camera within 0x2000 and obj+0x136C bit 1 is clear, then traces horizontally from a point 60 units to the actor's own left (argument -1.0) or right (+1.0), at the ground height under it plus rand()%20 + 9.0, back to the actor. On a hit it stores a point 4.5 units short of the wall in obj+0x13D8..E0 and returns 1 -- so with no wall there, the actor simply does not go.
The gate on class-0x31 state 16. Traces from 1000 units above the actor in its own frame down to the actor, and on a hit stores the contact point in obj+0x13D8..E0 and returns 1.

Class 0x31 states 14, 15 and 16: the leap onto a wall or the ceiling. ThrowerFindWallBeside / ThrowerFindCeilingAbove have already put the destination in obj+0x13D8..E0; this begins the arc with ActorArcBeginToAtSpeed, installs the state's own three-stage arc motion script (g_class31_arc_to_wall_b for 14, g_class31_arc_to_wall_a for 15, g_class31_arc_to_ceiling for 16), plays sound 0x2416A9, and on arrival sets the stance bit its state id names -- 14 sets 0x80, 15 sets 0x40, 16 sets 0x100 in obj+0x136C -- plus 0x20, off the ground. Those bits are the stance that selects every later motion and attack row. Returns to state 7.

Class 0x31 state 17, and it is the decapitation recovery: only ThrowerShotFeedback's head-model swap sets the obj+0x136C bit 0x4000000 that routes states 1 and 2 here. Sets obj+0x34 bit 0x100 -- the window in which shots ricochet -- plays motion 0x127 with a 5-frame fade for every character type, plays sound 0x1C17A9, and on the last frame clears both that bit and the knocked-down latch before asking ThrowerPickNextState. Character type 0x18 can never reach it, since ThrowerOnShot diverts it to state 0x21; and 0x127 is a szom.bin clip, so character type 0x17 -- the only one on kame.bin's skeleton -- asks here for a clip its own rig does not have. [open]

probes 1000 units in (1500 on the ceiling) to a point 4.5 past the actor and returns the hit itself, with NO standoff. Used by the knockdown bounce. ThrowerSnapToSurface does NOT call this -- see ThrowerFindSurfaceUnderfoot at 0x44C640

Calls ThrowerFindSurfaceUnderfoot and, when it answers, moves the actor onto the contact point. Run every frame by ThrowerPushOutOfWorld but only in states 7 and 8, which is what keeps a wall-clinging actor stuck to its wall while it stands and waits -- and what drops it into state 11 when the wall has gone.

what ThrowerSnapToSurface actually calls -- NOT TraceActorSurfaceContactPoint (0x44C370), which looks identical for its first forty lines. Probes 10 units each side of the actor (15 on the ceiling). On a WALL it re-places the actor 6.5 units off the surface it found, keeping the actor's own y; on floor/ceiling it takes y from the hit and keeps x/z. Misses answer (1000,y,1000) for a wall and -1000 for a ceiling so the range test fails and the actor goes to state 8 or 11

Class 0x31's copy of TryClaimAttackSlot, instruction for instruction. Neither tests the distance queue -- that gate lives in ZombieStateApproach, before the call -- so a thrower may claim from any range.

Where a thrower lands, and it is a place on the **screen** rather than in the world: a pixel offset divided by g_projection_distance_px and unprojected at a fixed depth, so the actor always arrives the same distance in front of the camera however the camera is pointing. Depth -15.5 (-6.0 from state 0x17); vertical offset 390px for character type 0x16, 320 otherwise, and -350 from states 0x16/0x17. Sideways is +/-160px by attack permit and zero when g_max_attackers is 1.

Class 0x31's strike connect, run every frame of an attack state. Tests no range at all. Picks the 32-bit table g_class31_melee_attacks[set] entry obj+0x131A + obj+0x1364*4, or g_class31_throws entry obj+0x131A when obj+0x136C bit 0x400 is set, fires when obj+0x19C equals the entry's hit frame -- or, in the 32-bit table, when that frame is -1 and the arc has reached phase 4 -- passes the cancel-mask test (obj+0x1318 & mask & 7) != mask, then calls PlayerTakeDamage(obj+0x121, kind, the entry's player motion) and latches obj+0x136C bit 0x800. kind is 1 normally and 0 when obj+0x34 bit 0x2000000 is set, in which case the actor despawns immediately after the hit.

class 0x31's ReleaseAttackSlot. Frees g_attack_permits[obj+0x121] and, if obj+0x136C bit 0x8000 is set, lowers g_attack_committed. THE BIT IS 0x8000, NOT 0x20000: FUN_00456520 is the class-0x30 twin and tests 0x20000 of the same word. Calling the wrong one leaves the latch up and no enemy in the scene can claim again. Eight class-0x31 call sites
Decrements g_enemies_alive exactly once per actor, guarded by obj+0x136C bit 0x800000.
Decrements g_enemies_present exactly once per actor, guarded by obj+0x136C bit 0x1000000.

class 0x31, called by every fall state. If obj+0x34 bit 0x4000000 or hp<1: untrack from the camera (obj+0x120, NOT the permit) unless this is the last enemy present, then ThrowerRetireFromAliveCount. So g_enemies_alive falls when the actor is knocked off its feet, not when the body settles

Puts the actor into its corpse state: clears obj+0x136C bits 0x180000, sets obj+0x34 bits 0xC001 (bit 14 freezes the motion advance), retires from g_enemies_present unless obj+0x38 bit 0, steps the motion play cursor back one frame, then enters state 5 for character type 0x18 and state 4 otherwise.

where a shot class-0x31 body flies. t = 15.0/|obj+0x70..0x78| * 10.0, clamped at 0, *1.5 if obj+0x34 bit 0x4000000 (already dead); destination is the view-space tracked point with z REDUCED BY t, transformed back through the view-to-world matrix at DAT_009A6040 + block*0x1A4. The camera space has -z in front (ThrowerPickLandingPoint unprojects at -15.5), so z-t throws the body AWAY from the viewer, keeping its screen x and y. Two callers: FUN_0044A450 and ThrowerStateKnockedTumbling

Thunk to ActorSetMotionBlended on the current actor's motion block. Its first argument is read but never used, so it always drives DAT_009A26A0 + 0x194; every caller passes obj+0x194 anyway. The third argument is a start frame inside the clip, not a blend length.

Effect emitter keyed by a code. 0x46, from the ground bounce, is one-shot per bounce on obj+0x136C bit 0x4000 and spawns sprite 0x61 in rain or on surfaces 0x37 and 0x05 and sprite 0x46 otherwise, oriented to g_coli_hit_normal. 0x50, from an arc landing, needs obj+0x34 bit 0x10000000 clear and bit 0x20000000 set and spawns sprite 0x4B scaled 0.4, 2.0, 0.2. 0x50 and 0x5A then share a movement trail for character type 0x16 that spawns two sprites at the midpoint of obj+0x13E4..EC and the current position, sized by distance * 0.05981133 with scale 0.8 and 0.2, at +0x4000 and +0x8000 BAMS.

Stretches an installed arc motion script onto obj+0x1334 for every character type but 0x19. slack = duration - script[10] - script[6] - script[7] + script[5]; with room to spare it grows both stages' fade lengths (indices 6 and 10) a frame at a time until they fill it, clamping each at 0x7F, and when it is tight it walks stage 1's start frame up and its threshold down until the three stages fit. Called from ActorArcStep phase 0.

Begin the leg of a path: ActorArcBeginTo to the waypoint's destination, then install the waypoint's motion set. Character type 0x19 uses a different arc builder. When the set is the default it instead draws an attack index from g_class31_picks the way ZombieStateStrike does, so a waypoint can arrive swinging.
Advance one frame of an arc begun by ActorArcBegin. Returns 0 once the frame counter passes the duration, which is how the leap states know they have landed.

Copies a 12-dword three-stage arc motion script -- {s32 motion, s32 start frame, s32 fade, s32 threshold} x 3 -- into g_arc_scripts at 0x009C8AA0, stride 0x30, indexed by the actor's enemy slot obj+0x3C. ActorArcStep plays stage 0 at the start of the arc, stage 1 once the clip frame passes threshold [3], stage 2 once it passes [7], and reports the arc finished past [11]. Every script in the program names the same motion in all three stages, so a script is one clip cut into windup, flight and landing.

ActorArcBegin whose duration it works out itself: the horizontal distance at a fixed 30 world units per minFrames, where minFrames is 10 when obj+0x136C bit 0x2000000 is set and obj+0x34 bits 0x44000000 are not, else 15 -- so 2.0 or 3.0 units a frame -- clamped up to minFrames. ActorArcBeginToWaypoint uses this instead of ActorArcBeginTo for character type 0x19.

Record a ballistic arc: source in obj+0x13C0/C4/C8, destination in obj+0x13CC/D0/D4, duration in obj+0x1334, frame counter obj+0x1330 reset. ActorArcVelocity then rebuilds the velocity every frame from those.

Begin an arc from the actor's position to a named point. Records src in obj+0x13C0..C8 and dst in obj+0x13CC..D4, zeroes the frame counter, and sets the duration at obj+0x1334 to n - n%step where n = (int)(dist2d * step) -- the **2D** distance, x and z only, y is not in it. So step is frames per unit: 1 gives a unit a frame, 2 gives half. The same value is passed to ActorArcStep as the arc kind, so it selects which axis carries the arc as well as the speed. Ghidra drops the FPU argument to __ftol here and shows the distance as nothing at all.

Advances g_cur_actor's ballistic arc by param_1 frames and writes obj+0x40/0x44/0x48. Reads the six-float arc record ActorArcBeginTo laid down -- obj+0x13C0/13C4/13C8 the start, obj+0x13CC/13D0/13D4 the destination -- with obj+0x1330 as the elapsed frame count and obj+0x1334 as the total. Gravity is 0.027222222 on the Y term. Returns 0 once elapsed reaches the total. Only two callers (FUN_0044D780, FUN_0045E010), but classes 0x2D, 0x30, 0x31 and 0x40 all re-implement the same maths on the same offsets, so those offsets are a convention the whole game shares rather than one routine's private state.

ActorArcVelocity (FUN_0044DE80) case 0 with the axis selector taken out: one frame of the shared arc record as a velocity, the parabola on y. Advances obj+0x1330, returns 0 once it has reached obj+0x1334, and computes the velocity for frame t+1 while testing with t. Two callers: ThrowerStateFallAndLand (0x0044A561) and ZombieStateDeathKnockbackArc (0x0045534C).

The arc itself, and it is exact projectile motion: vel.xz = (dst - src)/T flat, and vel.y = -0.027222222*n + (T*T*0.027222222 + 2*dy)/(2*T) for frame n of T. The 0.027222222 is half the 0.05444444 gravity ThrowerStateFallAndLand uses, which is what a discrete `pos += vel; vel -= g` integrator needs. The six cases select which axis carries the arc.
Zeroes the current actor's acceleration (+0x58/5C/60) and then its velocity (+0x4C/50/54).

The same fit for character type 0x19, and it moves start frames rather than fades. slack = duration - script[10] - script[6] - script[7] + script[5] and k = (int)(|slack| * 0.5): a positive slack adds k to both fade lengths and puts the remainder on stage 1's, a negative one advances stage 1's and stage 2's start frames (indices 5 and 9) by k, each clamped at its own threshold, and puts the remainder on stage 1's -- so a short leap skips into the middle of the clip rather than playing it slowly. Ghidra drops the FPU argument to __ftol; the 0.5 is float ptr 0x004C43AC = 0x3F000000.

Class 0x31 state 18, an entrance. Plays the walk variant from g_class31_motion_sets[set] chosen by obj+0x34 bit 27, records the start position in obj+0x13C0..C8, and hands to state 7 once the 2D distance travelled reaches the float at descriptor tail +0x04. Stage 2 block 17 step 5 spawns two zstin this way with a distance of 15.0. Raises obj+0x136C bit 0x1000 on entry (OR CH, 0x10 -- 80cd10 at 0x0044E32E) and clears it on the way out (0x0044E3DE). Nothing in the program tests that bit. [open]

Class 0x31 state 19, an entrance. Plays the motion named by the int at descriptor tail +0x04 once -- 296 for every stage-2 zstin that uses it -- then plays sound 0x2916A9, sets obj+0x136C bit 0x80000 and hands to state 7.

Class 0x31 state 20, and how a spawn placed in the air reaches the ground. Sub 0 hands the actor's position and the descriptor's destination (float x,y,z at +0x04/08/0C) and duration (s32 at +0x10) to ActorArcBegin; each frame ActorArcStep integrates the arc, and when it ends the actor drops into state 7 to stand and throw. Stage 2 block 5 spawns two zsass at y = 87 whose descriptors name the street at y = 37, 50 units down over 30 and 35 frames.

Class 0x31 state 21, an entrance no shipped spawn uses and no state can reach -- cut content. Rides object path 0x14F (op_st2 local 7) at g_cam_path_frame for 0xC4 frames; both the slot and the count are immediates, not descriptor fields. Copies position and all three BAMS angles out of CamEvalObjectPath6 -- which returns three floats then three ints, whatever Ghidra's signature says -- holds obj+0x34 bit 0x100 while riding, then claims an attack permit, discards the answer, and goes to state 9.

Class 0x31 state 22, an entrance no shipped spawn uses and no state can reach -- dead code. When ThrowerTryClaimAttackSlot fails it forces obj+0x121 from g_active_player -- 1 gives player 1, 2 a coin flip, 0 or -1 player 0 -- and attacks with no permit actually held. Draws obj+0x131A from g_class31_attack_picks, installs the arc script with ThrowerLoadAttackArcScript, and arcs to ThrowerPickLandingPoint over the s32 frame count at descriptor tail +0x04, calling ThrowerStrikeConnect every frame IsPlayerAttackable allows. Ends in state 10.

Class 0x31 state 23, both an entrance and an attack. Sets obj+0x1F8 bit 0x10 and plays the motion at descriptor tail +0x04 for the frame count at tail +0x08; then clears the bit, claims a permit, draws an attack index, and arcs from where it stands to ThrowerPickLandingPoint taken at g_camera_eye_y over that same count, rolling obj+0x6C back to level at 0xCCC a frame and calling ThrowerStrikeConnect every frame. Ends in state 25. Stage 2 block 21 step 2 spawns two zstin this way, motion 310 over 45 and 60 frames.

Class 0x31 state 24. Takes ThrowerPickLandingPoint as its target, draws an attack index, plays the g_class31_throws entry's approach clip until it is within that entry's own distance of the point, then plays its strike clip and calls ThrowerStrikeConnect on the frame the entry names. Ends in state 25.

Class 0x31 state 25, the retreat the two scripted attacks end in. Plays the motion set's landing clip and returns to state 7 once 0x5A frames have passed or the actor is more than 50 units from the camera -- 30 units and no clip test for character type 0x17, which also faces away from its strike anchor while it goes. Releases the permit with ThrowerReleaseAttackPermit on the way out.

Class 0x31 state 26: follow a predefined path. Sub 0 reads a delay from descriptor +0x04 and points obj+0x1394 at the waypoint list, which starts at descriptor +0x08 and runs in **16-byte entries** -- {s16 step, s16 motion_set, f32 x, f32 y, f32 z} -- terminated by a step of -1. Sub 1 counts the delay down; sub 2 begins the leg with ActorArcBeginToWaypoint; sub 3 steps the arc and, on arrival, plays sound 0x2916A9 and advances the cursor. At the terminator, character type 0x17 goes to state 7 and everything else claims an attack permit and goes to state 9.

Class 0x31 state 27, an entrance; four shipped spawns, all zslman in st5evtbl. Six sub-states over an 0x18-byte tail: three floats at +0x04 are the destination camera-relative offset of which only +0x08, the Y, is ever read; s16 +0x10 the camera path frame to drop on, matched against g_cam_path_frame or camera block 2's frame at 0x009A6458; s16 +0x12 the descent frames; s16 +0x14 the hold frames; s8 +0x16 the player to grab, -1 meaning at random. It anchors to the camera every frame, drops on the cue at obj+0x50 = dY/frames, blinks for the first fifteen hold frames, then takes g_attack_permits[p] outright with a two-player fallback, plays 0x1E5 or 0x1E7 at random and damages on obj+0x19C == 30. Subs 2 to 4 ride MatrixTranslate(camera eye) then MatrixRotateY(g_camera_yaw_bams + 0x8000) and write only X and Z; sub 5 tracks the camera by delta through obj+0x137C..0x1384. Sounds 0x2516A9 ENE_WALK2 on the cue frame and again at half the finish clip, 0x2916A9 ENE_WALK6 on landing, 0x1F23A9 LASER_SWORD on as the hold begins and 0x2023A9 LASER_SWORD off on every frame of the solid phase. The last pair is a looping pair from g_looping_se_ids / g_looping_se_stop_ids, so the off id calls SoundStopAllLoopingSe before playing; it still fires once per solid frame, which is the engine's own behaviour and not a dedupe.

Class 0x31 state 28, an entrance; six shipped spawns, all in trnevtbl. The tail is 0x0C bytes: s32 +0x04 the motion, played from rand() modulo its own length with a 4-frame blend; s16 +0x08 the condition -- 0 a frame count in obj+0x1330, 1 g_cam_path_frame, 2 g_script_flags -- and s16 +0x0A the operand. Then it jumps to the signed byte at tail +0x03, which is 7 in every shipped record. Any selector above 2 waits for ever.
True when character 0x16 or 0x18 still holds a weapon in either hand -- the gate on state 0x1F, the throw. Character types 0x17 and 0x19 always fail it, which is why zstin never throws.

Returns the bone index of the hand still holding a weapon: 5 for the right (draw slot obj+0x4DC) or 8 for the left (obj+0x68C), 0 if neither. The armed part ids are 0x1FA2 and 0x1F9E for character type 0x16 and 0x1FF3 and 0x1FEF for 0x18; every other type returns 0 without a test. The rand() parity picks which hand is PREFERRED, not which one throws: parity 0 tests bone 8 then bone 5 and parity 1 tests bone 5 then bone 8, each later test overwriting the earlier, so a bare preferred hand falls through to the other one and only two bare hands give 0. [proved]

True when one of character 0x16's or 0x18's hands has thrown its weapon and the other has not been restored -- the gate on states 0x1D and 0x1E, the re-arm. Character types 0x17 and 0x19 have no weapon and always fail it.

Class 0x31 state 29, character type 0x16's re-arm and its only caller-visible effect. Plays motion **5** -- 0044f7b9 6a05 / 0044f7c6 6a05, SetCurrentActorMotionBlended(obj+0x194, 5, 0, 5), the id and the fade both 5 -- and at the clip's exact MIDPOINT (obj+0x19C == g_motion_play_length[obj+0x1B4] / 2) swaps each bare hand model back to its armed one: obj+0x4DC 0x1F9F -> 0x1FA2 with the four attach floats at 0x554..0x560 and obj+0x1318 &= ~2, and obj+0x68C 0x1F9B -> 0x1F9E with 0x704..0x710 and obj+0x1318 &= ~4. Both tests are sequential, not exclusive, so a zsass that has thrown twice gets both weapons back on one frame. Exits to state 7 at play_length - 1 and clears obj+0x34 bit 0x2000. Those two hand slots are exactly what ThrowerHasBareHand (FUN_0044F720) reads, so this routine failing to run is self-perpetuating: state 7 offers 0x1D to ThrowerTryEnterState BEFORE it asks ThrowerPickNextState, so a thrower whose hands never re-arm re-enters this state every frame and the router -- the only route to state 8 and therefore to any attack at close range -- is never reached.

Class 0x31 state 30. Waits for obj+0x136C bit 0x8000000 to clear, then puts both of character 0x18's weapons back -- bone 5's draw slot 0x1FF1 becomes 0x1FF3 and bone 8's 0x1FED becomes 0x1FEF, each with its hit sphere restored from PTR_DAT_004D032C -- and clears that arm's destroyed-zone bit. Returns to state 7.

Takes an attack permit, picks a hand with ThrowerPickThrowingHand (FUN_0044F630), reads its entry from g_class31_throws[obj+0x130C] at index obj+0x131A<<4, plays the throw clip and calls SpawnThrownWeapon on the frame the entry names. Then hands to state 7. The three sub-states at obj+0x1312 FALL THROUGH into each other -- SUB EAX,0/JZ then DEC EAX/JZ twice at 0x0044FB16..0x0044FB23, each arm ending in INC word [ESI+0x1312] and running straight on -- so a throw can start and release on the same frame. Sub 0 also passes a START CURSOR to ActorSetMotionBlended, not frame zero: PUSH 0x4/PUSH 0x1a (6a04 6a1a) at 0x0044FB87 for every type but 0x18 and PUSH 0x4/PUSH 0x0 (6a04 6a00) at 0x0044FC68 for 0x18, both into the one CALL 0x004119a0 at 0x0044FC74, and FUN_004119A0 writes that third argument into obj+0x19C outright (param_1[2] = param_3; param_1[6] = param_3/2). So a zsass throw is 22 cursor ticks of wind-up against its entry's release frame of 48. Sub 2 is the exit: g_motion_play_length[obj+0x1B4] - 1 <= obj+0x19C plays sound 0x2916A9 and writes obj+0x1310 = 7, obj+0x1312 = 0 (66c786101300000700 at 0x0044FCE1). It re-arms NOTHING and releases NOTHING -- state 7 offers 0x1D (0x1E for type 0x18) to ThrowerTryEnterState before it asks the router, and the permit rides the projectile out of SpawnThrownWeapon; FUN_0044CFB0 has eight call sites and this is not one. Character type 0x18 is diverted out of that path TWICE, by two copies of CMP word ptr [ESI+0x1f4], 0x18 (6683bef401000018). At 0x0044FB7A it picks the CLIP: other types take it from the entry's +0x00 (MOVSX EDX, word ptr [EDI] -- 0fbf17 at 0x0044FB84), 0x18 jumps to 0x0044FB98 and indexes the 32-byte selector table at 0x0044FD1C by handIdx + 10*stance, stance = 3*bit8 + 2*bit7 + bit6 of obj+0x136C, bounded by CMP EAX,0x1f/JA at 0x0044FBC4, out through the nine-entry jump table at 0x0044FCF8 to motions 0x1F7/0x1F6/0x1FC/0x1FB/0x1F2/0x1F1/0x204/0x203 plus a default that plays the actor pointer itself as a motion id. At 0x0044FC83 it picks the RELEASE FRAME: other types compare obj+0x19C against the entry's +0x08 at 0x0044FC8D, 0x18 compares it against obj+0x1350, into which all eight arms have written the constant 0x19 = 25 (c7865013000019000000). That is the SAME word states 2 and 33 use for the landing surface -- one address, two readings, both inside class 0x31. The table at 0x0044FD1C is .text, not .rdata: one xref (the MOV CL at 0x0044FBCF), nine jump targets all inside this function, 24 of its 32 bytes unreachable dense-switch padding, and the clip ids MOV immediates in the arms. So it is NOT exportable as data; it is transcribed in web/src/game/class31/thrower.ts as THROW_BY_STANCE_ZSLMAN and ZSLMAN_RELEASE_FRAME under the .rdata/.text rule in docs/formats/bundle.md. [proved]

Projectile state 0. Launch sets ttl = distance * 0.8333 and velocity = (target - pos)/ttl, so the flight is a straight line at a constant speed. Every flight frame it tumbles the weapon by adding obj+0x135C to **obj+0x68** -- the Y term of ThrownWeaponUpdate's Rz*Ry*Rx draw, so the spin is about the weapon's own vertical -- negated unless obj+0x1358 is 5, which is which hand threw it. On ttl expiry it calls PlayerTakeDamage outright: the hit is TIMED, not tested. Then AimThrownWeapon points it back at the camera, it sticks for 0x1E frames and blinks for 0x3C by toggling obj+0x1F8 bit 0. The blink running out is where the THROWER'S ATTACK PERMIT is finally given back: CALL 0x0044cfb0 (e88ccfffff at 0x0045001F) on the projectile, whose obj+0x121 SpawnThrownWeapon copied off the thrower, immediately followed by the despawn. So a class-0x31 throw holds its permit for the whole flight plus 90 frames, and ThrowerStateThrow never releases one itself. [proved]
Projectile state 1, entered when the weapon is shot out of the air. Spawns an impact sprite, plays BULLET_MET3, picks a random direction and flies off before despawning.
Sets the weapon's target to a point 4 units in front of the camera, offset sideways by 0.6 per player in two-player.

Allocates the projectile at the throwing hand's bone position, sets its model from the character type, leaves the hand bare, marks that arm's destroyed zone, and passes the thrower's attack permit to the weapon -- so the projectile damages the player the thrower had claimed. The hand-off is literal: MOV AL, [EDI+0x121] (8a8721010000 at 0x004506BB), MOV [ESI+0x121], AL (888621010000 at 0x004506C4) and then MOV [EDI+0x121], BL (889f21010000 at 0x004506D5) with BL zero from 0x0045050A -- the thrower is left holding 0, NOT -1 -- and the off-screen commit latch obj+0x136C bit 0x8000 moves across with it (TEST EAX,ECX/JZ at 0x004506DB, OR on the weapon's word, AND AH,0x7F on the thrower's). The projectile's own state and sub are zeroed at 0x00450742, and it frees the slot at the end of its life in ThrownWeaponFlyToTarget. [proved]

The projectile's own update: two states at 0x00592AE0, then draws its model as Rz(obj+0x6C) * Ry(obj+0x68) * Rx(obj+0x1364 + obj+0x64). The **Y** term is the tumble -- ThrownWeaponFlyToTarget accumulates it into obj+0x68 -- and the X and Z terms are zero in flight, set only when the weapon lands and turns to face the camera. Registers for both the shot test and camera tracking, so a thrown weapon can be shot down and the camera will follow it.

Class 0x31 state 32. Plays motion 0x1B8, pins itself to where that clip ended, then loops: claim a permit if it has none, draw an attack index, play its strike clip calling ThrowerStrikeConnect, then the motion set's second idle for 0x78 frames, and strike again. It never leaves the state.

Sets obj+0x1354, the arc kind ActorArcVelocity switches on: 0 floor, 1 ceiling, 2 wall at +X, 3 wall at -X, 4 wall at -Z, 5 wall at +Z. Derived from the cardinal-snapped yaw and obj+0x136C bits 0x40, 0x80 and 0x100, and it agrees with the acceleration ThrowerStateKnockedTumbling writes on the same axis.

Class 0x31 state 33, the shot reaction character type 0x18 takes instead of the stumble. Sub 0 picks the knock clip by stance -- 0x215 ground, 0x1FE and 0x1F4 the two walls, 0x206 ceiling -- fades it over 5 frames on a fresh knock or hard-cuts it on a re-entry (obj+0x136C bit 0x400000, which also skips the velocity clear and counts obj+0x1328 up), launches ThrowerBeginKnockbackArc while obj+0x1328 is under 2, and calls SelectActorGravityAxis. Then it rides the arc and bounces off whichever of the six axes obj+0x1354 names, standing 4.5 units off a wall, negating that axis by -0.5 and halving the other two, playing sound 0x2716A9 each time, until the speed on that axis drops to 0.15 or obj+0x1338 reaches 0x78. Landing waits (rand()%10+1)*3 frames, plays the stance's get-up clip -- 0x216 / 0x1FF / 0x1F5 / 0x207 -- and returns to state 7 with obj+0x133C = 0x14, a 20-frame window in which shots do nothing. A dead actor, or surface 0x5A under it, goes to ThrowerEnterCorpseState instead.

Class 0x31 state 34, an entrance; eight shipped spawns, all zslman in st6evtbl, covering all four surface stances. A three-hop blinking materialisation, not a retreat -- the earlier name ThrowerStateBackAwayThreeUnits was wrong. After the s32 delay at descriptor tail +0x04 it hops to origin + RotY(obj+0x68) * (0, 0, obj+0x1348 * 30) with obj+0x1348 counting 3, 2, 1, so 90 then 60 then 30 units from the origin it captured at entry, 30 frames apart -- obj+0x1344 is set to 30.0 and decremented on the hop frame itself -- blinking obj+0x138C and obj+0x136C bit 2 on g_frame_counter parity throughout. The stance idle is an immediate rather than a table lookup: 0x208 ground, 0x1FD, 0x1F3 and 0x205 by obj+0x136C bit6 + bit7*2 + bit8*3. It ends on sound 0x2225A9 STAGE6_SE MONITOR3, goes solid, and jumps to tail +0x03. EnemyThrowerInit special-cases this state for character type 0x18, starting it invisible.

Class 0x21's handler -- the RESCUE TARGET, and the only branch writer arcade reaches whose class is an enemy. Builds a skinned character on motion 0x3E6 -- MOV dword ptr [EDI + 0x20], 0x3E6 (c74720e6030000) at 0x00451747 with EDI = obj+0x194, so the clip is a LITERAL and not read from the descriptor -- increments BOTH g_enemies_present (0x009C7006) and g_enemies_alive (0x009C904A), takes its hit points from g_class21_hp_by_rank (0x00565F0C, s16[16] indexed by g_damage_rank, giving 1 to 4), then enters RescueTargetRideInState. It also calls FUN_00452120(0), which is what SPAWNS THE STAGE-2 CAR object. One spawn in the shipped data: stage 2 block 0 step 2, script address 0x07D0, character type 7 (char_adv00), whose route record is {kind 1, next = 11, 1, -1}.

Class 0x21's entrance. obj+0x1312 is the sub-state: 0 rides the object in along the active camera path -- its position is rebuilt every frame from (0, 50 - g_cam_path_frame, 50 - g_cam_path_frame) rotated by obj+0x68 -- and advances to 1 once the path frame passes 0x31. Sub-state 1 waits for the path frame to pass 0xBD, skipping frames 0x5A and 0x8C, then hands over to RescueTargetHeldState. g_cutscene_skipping (0x009A2230) short-circuits both.

Class 0x21's live state, and one of the sixteen writers of g_script_branch_var. Walks its SIXTEEN body parts; a part with obj+0x34 bit 3 set decrements obj+0x11C by one, pays 10 points (120 plus the head combo for part 2) and clears the bit. When obj+0x11C reaches 0 the target is RESCUED: g_script_branch_var = 1, g_civilians_rescued_total and g_civilians_rescued_by_scene[scene] both increment, 0x36 is recorded in the per-scene rescue list at 0x009C8EC0, the player is paid 0x50 + 400, motion 0x3CC plays and both enemy counters come back down before it enters RescueTargetFreedState. The player credited is decided by obj+0x34 bits 1 and 2 -- bit 1 alone gives player 0, bit 2 alone player 1, and both or neither draws rand() & 1. g_script_flags[0] short-circuits the whole state into a despawn, as does the camera reaching path 0x39 frame 0x121, which is the abandoned path into RescueTargetAbandonedState.

Class 0x21 when the camera has left it behind -- entered from RescueTargetHeldState at path 0x39 frame 0x121, with both enemy counters already given back. Runs its idle animation until the camera reaches path 0x39 frame 0x181, then despawns.
Class 0x21 after the rescue: plays out the freed animation and, once obj+0x1F1 is raised, sets a 0x78-frame countdown, spawns the ground ring effect and moves to the routine at 0x00451DF0.

Class 0x21's pose: CamEvalObjectPath6(g_st2car_path_table[obj+0x1350], g_cam_path_frame) written straight onto obj+0x40/44/48 and obj+0x64/68/6C. [proved] the rescue target rides the STAGE-2 CAR's own object path -- index 0 is op_st2 0x148 during camera 0x38 and index 1 is op_st2 0x14E during 0x39, the same two routes FUN_004521B0 gives the car. Called first by RescueTargetRideInState in both sub-states.

RescueTargetPoseFromRoute plus a per-frame delta: obj+0x13CC/0x13D0/0x13D4 = new pose - old pose, written before obj+0x40/44/48 are replaced. The only difference between the two, and the pair is near-identical on purpose. RescueTargetHeldState calls this one.

Class 0x21's draw. Loads the view matrix from g_camera_matrices + g_active_view * 0x69 dwords, transforms obj+0x40 into camera space, and draws through FUN_00411090 only if the transformed z is below float[0x004C436C]. L37: Ghidra's pseudocode ends at the MatrixStackPop and shows NONE of the distance test or the draw -- the tail is at 0x00452055-0x0045207C.

The per-frame footstep and swish hook, called from EnemyZombieUpdate (FUN_004533F0) and nowhere else. A switch over the CURRENT MOTION at obj+0x1B4 -- 0xB, 0xB3, 0xC3, 0x108, 0x114, 0x1AE, 0x1C1, 0x1C3, 0x1C4, 0x2B5, 0x307, 0x30A, 0x310, 0x3B0, 0x3B1, 0x3C8 -- each arm naming one or two exact frames of that clip and one SE: 0x2616A9 (COMMON\ENE_WALK3_16), 0x2916A9 (ENE_WALK6_22), 0x3C16A9 and 0x3D16A9 (SWORD11_22 and its _1 twin). The play happens at 00452C51 only when the frame matched, the id is non-zero AND obj+0x1314 -- a s16 latch -- does not already hold the frame; then obj+0x1314 = obj+0x19C. Every arm reads obj+0x19C, so these are exact-frame cues on the play clock and not a timer. Sound only: nothing else reads obj+0x1314.

class 0x30. params[0] = character type, params[2] = initial state (obj+0x1310), obj+0x1B4 = motion 0x3BC (956, zom.bin) or 0x41E on a branch. **It counts the actor into both enemy counters** -- g_enemies_present and g_enemies_alive each ++ -- but only when the character type is not 9 AND the initial state at obj+0x1310 is not 0x1F: state 31 (ZombieStateWaitScriptFlagThenEnter) counts itself in later, when its script flag comes up, which is the whole point of that state. Character type 9 gets a different update handler (LAB_00453290) and is not an enemy at all. Also seeds obj+0x136C from the descriptor, exactly as EnemyThrowerInit does: MOVSX EDX, word ptr [ESI+0x1316] (0fbf9616130000) at 0x00452E9A, OR EDX, 0x60000000 (81ca00000060) at 0x00452EA4 -- class 0x30's own CollideWorld|CollideActors -- then MOV dword ptr [ESI+0x136c], EDX (89966c130000) at 0x00452EAF. 76 of 345 shipped class-0x30 descriptors set that word, 52 of them to 0x20. The port exports the word as desc_flags but EnemyZombieInit does not yet read it; the bit names are [open].

EnemyZombieInit's per-character-type tail, and it opens with three flag MOVES that are not about the character type at all. 00453000: if obj+0x136C bit 0x20 then obj+0x38 |= 8, which only DrawCharacterPartSlot reads -- 55 shipped class-0x30 spawns set it, 20 in stage 2 and 35 in stage 4. 0045300B: if obj+0x34 bit 1 then CLEAR it and obj+0x38 |= 0x10; 00453045: if obj+0x34 bit 2 then CLEAR it and obj+0x38 |= 0x20. Both are cleared at the source, so nothing downstream can find them at obj+0x34 -- and bits 1 and 2 there are the two MarkActorShot later uses to name the player who fired, which is why they cannot be left. Then the switch on obj+0x1F4: types 2 and 3 load a held prop and TAKE THE HELD-WEAPON LOOP -- not a spawn cry, as this row used to say. At 00453133 it plays 0x4D17A9 (COMMON2\CHAIN_SAW_22.wav) for type 2 or 0x1F25A9 (STAGE6_SE\LASER_SWORD_22.wav) otherwise, but ONLY when g_weapon_loop_holders is still 0; both ids are in g_looping_se_ids (entries 4 and 34) so PlaySoundId plays them LOOPED. Then g_weapon_loop_holders++ and obj+0x131B = 1, and ZombieReleaseWeaponLoopSe stops the loop when the last holder dies or loses the weapon. So the chainsaw and the laser sword are one shared looping SE per scene, refcounted, and not per actor. 9 is the twin's own init (0.25f at obj+0x138C), 0xC branches on the body condition, 0xE loads a prop, and TYPE 0x12 (znele, thirteen spawns, all stage 6) ALLOCATES A SECOND CLASS-0x30 ACTOR beside itself unless obj+0x34 already has 0x10000000 -- ActorAlloc(EnemyZombieInit, 0x13F4), the host's 0x18-dword transform copied in, obj+0x13A4 pointed back at the host, the host's behaviour set carried over, character type stamped 9 and obj+0x11C 999. That twin runs ZombieTwinFollowHost (0x00453290) and wears the host's pose. THE FOURTH FLAG MOVE, and it is not a flag move: 0045301D TEST byte ptr [obj+0x34],DL with DL=8, i.e. descriptor bit 3. When set, the routine treats the descriptor's position and yaw as CARRIER-LOCAL: it copies obj+0x40/0x44/0x48 to obj+0x13D8/0x13DC/0x13E0 and obj+0x68 to obj+0x135C, ORs obj+0x136C bit 0x10000000, calls ZombieAttachToCarrier (00453053) so the actor is on the carrier from frame one, and then ORs obj+0x136C bit 0x100000 (the carried bit). EnemyZombieUpdate re-runs the attach every frame while 0x10000000 is up, before the state dispatch. Exactly four shipped descriptors set bit 3 -- st5evtbl 0x1D44, 0x1D74, 0x1DA4 (state 32) and 0x1DD4 (state 18), block 2 step 2 op 38 -- and they ride the class-0x33 car spawned at op 37, evt 0x1CE4. On the two bits it DOES move: obj+0x38 bit 0x10 has exactly one reader in the image, ZombieStateStandAndThrow's ending (0045945C and 004595B4), and EXACTLY TWO shipped records set the obj+0x34 bit it comes from (stage 3 block 2 step 4's two axe men, evt 0x3078 and 0x30BC, init_flags 0x20002); obj+0x38 bit 0x20 gates TurnActorTowardCameraEye(obj, 0x1A0) in ZombieStateRideCarrier (004589F5) and ZombieStateDelayedStrikeInPlace (0045EAEA) and nothing else, and its three source records are stage 2's first three state-29 riders (evt 0x5030, 0x506C, 0x50A8). Char type 2 also gets obj+0x136C bit 0x400, the ONE-SHOT latch ZombieStateHoldAtRange clears only when the idle clip reaches play_length - 2, so that character stands through a whole idle before its first attack.

The update EnemyZombieInit installs for character type 9 (znjikken1.bin, 'experiment 1') instead of the ordinary FUN_004533F0, and the only thing that ever runs it: type 9 has no spawn record anywhere in the shipped game and is created at runtime by EnemyZombieInitByCharType's type-0x12 arm. obj+0x13A4 is the back-pointer to the host. Every frame, while obj+0x138C > 0 AND the host's obj+0x34 lacks 0x4000000, it runs FUN_00453EB0, raises its own 0x80040000, and -- unless the host is mid-attack (host+0x34 & 0x10000000) -- copies the HOST's 0x18-dword transform block plus obj+0x1320/0x1324 (the clip pair), 0x1B4/0x1B8 and 0x194/0x198, so the twin wears the host's pose and animation exactly. Then ZombieAdvanceMotion and the camera-space position at obj+0x70. Either gate failing is FUN_00409CC0, a despawn. EnemyZombieInit does not count it in g_enemies_present or g_enemies_alive, so it is not a room-clear blocker.

per frame: dispatches g_pZombieStates[obj+0x1310], then integrates velocity IN ORDER: ZombieTickAltHitReaction, ZombieClearHitReactionWhenDone, ZombieOnShot (00453eb0); then, at 0045341C, TEST obj+0x136C 0x10000000 and if set CALL ZombieAttachToCarrier (00453424) -- the rigid re-seat onto g_carrier_object, and it happens BEFORE the state dispatch, so a carried actor's obj+0x40/44/48 and obj+0x68 are overwritten from the carrier every frame no matter which state it is in and no matter that the state itself never touches the position. That is the whole reason the four stage-5 block-2 spawns with descriptor bit 3 ride the car while sitting in states (32 and 18) that move nothing. Then dispatch g_class30_states[obj+0x1310] (00453434), integrate obj+0x4C velocity into obj+0x40, ZombieAdvanceMotion, RegisterForDistanceRank unless obj+0x136C bit 0x8000000, ActorRegisterCameraPoint(4.0), the obj+0x12F0 hook (ZombiePushOutOfWorldAndActors) and, unless obj+0x1368 bit 1, the draw.

Class 0x30's per-frame shot drain, run before the state dispatch -- the mirror of ThrowerOnShot. Gated on obj+0x34 bit 8 (a shot the update has not drained); calls DispatchHit FIRST, so the damage lands either way, and only then refuses on obj+0x34 bit 0x100 (ShotImmune). Per player in g_hit_player_order it writes the hit result to obj+0x1364, clears obj+0x136C bit 0x400, RAISES obj+0x34 bit 0x8000000 -- 00453f17 81c900000008 OR ECX,0x8000000, the same sprint bit ZombieStateAttackRun indexes its motion pair with, so a zombie that has been shot switches to the run of the pair -- and runs ActorShotFeedback. Then obj+0x136C bit 0x80000000 latches the death once; a live actor takes ActorReactToHit plus FUN_0040A6F0(obj,0) unless the result is 5, and a dead one latches 0x80000000, plays the death voice and picks the state: bit 0x4000 (mid-leap) vetoes everything, else sub = 0 and state 9 when the state is 0x34, obj+0x136C bit 0x100000 is set, or the body condition is 5 or 6 -- with obj+0x136C bit 8 raised first when the state is 0x1B or 0x1C and the actor is within 18.0 of obj+0x13CC/0x13D4 -- and state 6 otherwise.  THE VOICE KIND IS THE HIT RESULT CODE AND NOTHING ELSE, which matters because the port's render-side copy keys on killed/head instead. Dead path: 00453f6e CMP EAX,0x2 on the result read back out of [EBP] -- kind 2 when it is 2 (HitResultCode.Plain), kind 1 otherwise. Live path: 00454025 CMP EAX,0x5 -- ActorPlayHitVoice(obj, 0) unless the result is 5 (NoEffect). Never a test of whether the bone was the head or whether the actor died of it; and kind 2's two ids in g_hit_voice_table are the SAME PAIR as kind 1's, so the only audible difference between them is the impact -- two head impacts against the five body ones.
Draws the hit: blood at the bone scaled by g_hit_result, or -- on result 5 -- an impact sprite and a metal ricochet, because the shot did nothing.

Derives obj+0x130C, the body condition, from which parts are gone, and is ActorShotFeedback's (FUN_00454050) only caller -- the sibling of ActorBodyConditionFromHands (0x00455920), which runs from the hub state instead. Switches on obj+0x1F4 and counts how many of the two hand slots (obj+0x4DC left, obj+0x68C right) still hold their authored prop: type 1 wants 0x1BA9/0x1BA5, type 2 wants 0x1BD2/0x1BCC, types 0x13/0x14 want 0x1ECE/0x1ECA or 0x1EF9/0x1EF5, type 0xE wants 0x1E55; none left means condition 0, and for type 2 one armed hand gives 1 and two gives 2. For TYPE 2 with NEITHER hand armed it also calls ZombieReleaseWeaponLoopSe (FUN_00456600): shoot the chainsaw out of its hands and the looping CHAIN_SAW_22 stops, which is the second proof that that loop belongs to the weapon and not to the actor's voice. Types 0x13 and 0x14 refuse to touch conditions 7 and 5, as 0x00455920 does. Last, obj+0x136C bit 0x40 with condition 0 and both obj+0x1318 bits 1 and 2 (both arm zones destroyed) forces condition 5, which ChooseDeathMotion reads, and clears the bit.

Records the last-hit zone in obj+0x1319 (1 torso, 2 head) and decides whether the hit interrupts what the actor is doing. Results 1 and 3 always react; 2 and 5 only for character types 3 and 0x12. AND IT IS THE ONE PLACE IN THE IMAGE THAT TESTS A CHARACTER TYPE AGAINST 0x0A: result 1 on character type 10 (znjoe) in zone 1, with obj+0x34 bit 0x400 still clear, raises 0x4000400 as a once-only latch, pays ScoreAddForPlayer(player, 0x50), records the shooter at obj+0x131C and drops the actor into STATE 0x19 sub 0 -- ZombieStateReleaseBodyCreature -- instead of staggering. Result 4 with zone 1 or 9 calls FUN_0045D9F0 instead.

The stumble. g_pHitReactionMotions[char][obj+0x130C][g_bone_reaction_group[bone]] cross-faded onto track 1 -- or hard-set with no fade when the bone is 9 or above, the pelvis and legs. It opens with two refusals and the second is the one that matters: 004544cc TEST EDX,EDX / JZ (bone 0) and then 004544d8 f7463400200010 TEST dword ptr [ESI+0x34], 0x10002000 / JNZ -- so an actor holding bit 0x2000 or bit 0x10000000 plays NO reaction at all. 0x2000 is the no-hit-reaction latch: eight routines raise it while something else owns the body (ZombieStateEmerge 0x00458532 OR DH,0x21, ZombieStateDelayedLeap, ZombieStateArcScriptedEntrance, ThrowerStateFallToSurface, ZombieApplyScriptMode's 0x2400, and this routine's own alt arm at 004545f5 OR CH,0x20) and each clears it on the way out. ThrowerOnShot is the only other reader -- 00449a95 f6c420 TEST AH,0x20 / JNZ skips the stumble, the knockdown and the tumble -- so the bit is read in exactly two places and both refuse a reaction.

Runs every frame from EnemyZombieUpdate while obj+0x34 bit 0x40000000 is up (a hit reaction is playing) and takes it back down. obj+0x136C bit 0x1000 marks the overlay track (motion obj+0x1B8, cursor obj+0x1A0) as busy and bit 0x2000 the base track (obj+0x1B4 / obj+0x19C); each is cleared when its own byte flag says so (obj+0x1CA == 0 for the overlay, obj+0x1F1 != 0 for the base -- [open] what those two bytes are) or -- unless obj+0x1364 == 3 -- once the cursor has passed a QUARTER of g_motion_play_length for that clip. When obj+0x136C & 0x3000 is zero it clears obj+0x34 bit 0x40000000. So those two bits, not a timer, are what ends a stumble.

Start a motion unless obj+0x136C bit 0x2000 holds the current one, the motion is already playing, or bit 0x1000 asks for the track to be stopped instead. The states call this rather than ActorSetMotion so a reaction in progress is not cut off.

Runs every frame from EnemyZombieUpdate. When obj+0x136C bits 0x100 AND 0x200 are both set and obj+0x34 & 0x50000000 is clear, cross-fades onto track 1 (FUN_00411B20, layer 1, fade 5) the motion at PTR_PTR_00592CBC[charType][obj+0x130C] + 0x10 + (s8)obj+0x1319 * 4 -- the row slot indexed by the LAST-HIT ZONE. If that clip is already on obj+0x1B8 and obj+0x1CA != 0 it instead waits for the base cursor obj+0x19C to reach half of g_motion_play_length[obj+0x1B4] and then clears obj+0x34 bit 0x2000. This closes the [open] on globals.tsv's 0x00592CBC row: the gate is 0x100 AND 0x200 together, not 0x100 alone.

Class 0x30's post-state motion step: draws the skinned model and then advances the motion frame counters at obj+0x194 and obj+0x198. Gated off by obj+0x34 bit 0x4000, which is how a state freezes a pose -- the gate is on the counters only, so the model is still drawn, but root motion is a frame-to-frame delta and a frozen counter therefore also stops the actor moving. ZombieStateMotionCue21 is the only thing that clears the bit for a spawn record that sets it. In g_GameMode 2 the advance additionally needs DAT_009c72f1 == 1 and DAT_009c72f3 == 0, and swaps the hook at obj+0x12EC between FUN_004534A0 and LAB_00453B30.

The per-frame hook EnemyZombieInit installs at obj+0x12F0 and EnemyZombieUpdate calls through PTR_FUN_00592BC0. Pushes the actor out of the world collision (ColiTestSphereAgainstFullSet) AND out of other actors (ColiTestSphereAgainstActors) at 0.1 of the penetration, 1.8x while airborne -- so there IS an actor-versus-actor separation pass, contrary to an earlier note in the port. Also runs the obj+0x1338 countdown: 60 frames after a shove it flips obj+0x136C bit 0x400000, which is the direction ZombieStateBackOff retreats in.

Rebuilds the actor's body sphere each frame: centre (x, y + obj+0x128 + 1, z) into obj+0x12C/130/134, with obj+0x124 -- g_actor_radius_by_char -- as the radius. The +1 becomes +0.5 when obj+0x136C bit 0x2000000 is set. That centre is what RegisterForShotTest publishes into the dynamic list, so it is read by the gunshot test, by the frustum test at FUN_0045CA60 AND -- via FUN_00405360's copy to 0x005A30A0 -- by ColiTestSphereAgainstActors. An earlier note here said the last of those was not a reader; it is.
Called by ZombiePushOutOfWorldAndActors unless obj+0x34 bit 0x20000 (airborne) is set.

Class 0x30 state 11, the drop. Where ActorSnapToGroundHeight sends an actor more than ten units above the floor that carries obj+0x136C bit 0x4000000. Gravity -0.16333 on obj+0x50, or -0.08167 with clip 0x41D for body condition 4, which bounces at -0.25 of the impact speed until it is under 0.15. Probes the ground at obj+0x104, the TRACKED point, not the feet. A live actor plays 0x3BA from frame 15 on landing; then state 1.

Class 0x30 state 6. sub 0 chooses the death motion; sub 1 raises obj+0x34 bits 0x22000, sets obj+0x136C 0x60000000, plays the death voice (FUN_00456600, which also counts down DAT_009C8A74) and runs ZombieReleasePermitAndUntrack (FUN_004565A0) -- so the permit and the commit latch are freed on death, by the state machine, not by the shot. sub 2 waits for the clip: at g_motion_play_length - 1 it hands to FUN_00456740, or to state 12 when obj+0x34 bit 0x1000000 is set.

The pose pin both class-0x30 corpse states call every frame: writes obj+0x194 -- the base track's frame counter -- from a table chosen by obj+0x1B4, picking between each table's two entries with rand() %% 17 >> 4, so the second comes up once in seventeen. DAT_0059301C is the general table for the eight directional deaths 0x3D9..0x3E0; the special cases are DAT_0059305C (clip 0x3F8), DAT_00593064 (0x1DF), DAT_0059306C (0x41A), DAT_00593074 (0x404) and DAT_0059307C (0x3F7). The class-0x31 twin is ThrowerCorpsePoseFrame's table at 0x00592AC0.

Class 0x30 state 7, the corpse. Sub 0 spawns the ground ring effect, clears obj+0x136C bits 0x20000000 and 0x200 (AND EDX, 0xdffffdff -- NOT bit 0x100, whose only clue this instruction used to be), raises obj+0x34 bits 0xA0000 (Airborne, so the ground snap lets it sink, and 0x80000 which FUN_0040A590 reads before it draws the ground decal), arms obj+0x1330 = 0x78 and stashes the spawn yaw obj+0x68 at obj+0x1350. Then each frame: the timer down one, obj+0x44 down 0.04, and the pose pin FUN_00454E00. At zero it raises obj+0x34 bit 0x10000, zeroes g_enemy_slots[obj+0x120*8] and calls ActorDespawn -- so a class-0x30 corpse leaves the pool on its own after two seconds and no sweep has to remove it.

Class 0x30 state 8, the corpse that flickers instead of sinking -- character types 0x12 and 3, which is the test ZombieEnterCorpseState makes. Identical to ZombieStateCorpseSink except that the countdown's parity drives obj+0x1F8 bit 0 and FUN_00409D10(obj+0x194, even), which writes that byte into every part of the skinned model, and the body does not move. The twin of ThrowerStateCorpseBlink (FUN_0044AB70).

Class 0x30 state 9, the *other* death -- ZombieOnShot picks it over state 6 when the actor is in state 0x34, carries obj+0x136C bit 0x100000, or has body condition 5 or 6. Sub 0 raises obj+0x34 bit 0x20000, runs ZombieReleasePermitAndUntrack, builds a landing point in the camera's own matrix (g_camera_matrices + DAT_009C6F00 * 0x1A4) whose offsets and scale come from the body condition -- condition 4 also jitters obj+0x64 by rand()%%5 * 0x100 -- overrides it with obj+0x13CC..0x13D4 when obj+0x136C bit 8 is set and bit 0x10 is not, calls ActorArcBeginToAtSpeed, then ChooseDeathMotion. Sub 1 rides the arc through FUN_0044DDE0. Sub 2 falls under gravity (0xBD16872B, or 0xBCDF0123 for conditions 4 and 5), treating surfaces 5 and 0x37 as g_camera_fixed_eye_y, bouncing at -0.25 until it settles or 0x78 frames pass, and ends in ZombieEnterCorpseState.

ReleaseEnemyAliveCount, ReleaseEnemyPresentCount and ReleaseAttackSlot, then clears g_attack_permits[obj+0x120] and ActorDespawns. The terminal arm of ZombieStateWalkDistance, taken when obj+0x34 bit 0x20000000 is set -- which no class-0x30 spawn record does.

Class-0x30 state 1. Plays the run motion, closes on the camera, and switches to state 2 when TestApproachRing returns 1. The motion is row[2 + ((obj+0x34 >> 0x1B) & 1)] from a RANDOM start frame -- rand() %% g_motion_play_length[motion], fade 10 -- and the pair is a jog and a sprint, not two takes of one gait: measured on the shipped banks, 0.30 units an authored frame against 1.29 for char_adv02 and 0.32 against 1.00 for char_adv01. Bit 0x08000000 of obj+0x34 is never ORed anywhere in the image; it arrives from the spawn record's own flags word through ActorInitFlags, so which gait a zombie uses is placement data. 192 of the 402 class-0x30 spawns in the shipped stages set it. Also rolls rand() & 0xFF < 4 each frame and, when obj+0x136C has both 0x2000000 and 0x1000000, clears 0x1000000 and calls FUN_0045D9F0 -- a 1-in-64 shout.

Class 0x30 state 5, and the way back into the attack loop. Plays the in-place walk from the motion row, turns to the camera at 0x40 a frame, and returns to state 1 the moment `(s8)obj+0x131D < obj+0x1358` -- its rank in the distance queue is inside the allowance again. ZombieStateAttackRun sends an actor here when it drops out of that slice, so the queue throttle is a round trip and not a one-way exit. Note the **signed** read: EnemyZombieInit writes 0xFF to obj+0x131D, which is -1, so an actor that has not been ranked yet passes the test rather than failing it.

Class-0x30 state 2, and WHERE THE STANDING GROAN COMES FROM. Calls TestApproachRing and then ActorBodyConditionFromHands -- it is the only call site of the latter in the whole binary, so the body condition is refreshed exactly once per frame an actor spends at the ring and never while it is walking in. Then: holds inside the inner ring, and on the frame the in-range idle STARTS -- 004558B0 CMP EAX,EDI / 004558B2 JZ, the one gate, obj+0x1B4 against row[0] -- it calls ActorSetMotionBlended(obj+0x194, row[0], rand() %% 5, 10) and immediately PlaySoundId(0x1917A9) at 004558D6, which is COMMON2\ZOMBIE_041_16.wav. That PUSH at 004558D2 is the ONLY occurrence of 0x1917A9 anywhere in .text, so this state is the whole of the zombie idle voice: one shot per entry into the idle clip, not periodic, not random, and not one of ActorPlayHitVoice's five kinds. On the attack cooldown it asks TryClaimAttackSlot again -- success moves to state 3, the strike. Drops back to state 4 if the actor has drifted inside inner-1.

Derives obj+0x130C from whether bones 5 and 8 -- the hands, at obj+0x4DC and obj+0x68C, which are 0x20C + bone*0x90 -- still hold their original draw slots, and sets the matching destroyed-zone bits via g_bone_damage_zone. Character type 1 only ever falls to 0; types 0x13 and 0x14 write the armed-hand count (0, 1 or 2) but REFUSE to touch conditions 7 and 5, which are the stationary thrower's own row and the row it leaves behind. That refusal is what makes 7 sticky, and the write is what takes a condition-8 walker off the throw row (attacks[7] and attacks[8] are the throw: reach 99, clip 1005/1004) before ZombieStateStrike can read it as a melee. ZombieStateHoldAtRange (0x00455720) is its only caller. Engine bug at 0x0045599C: the left-hand test is CMP EDI,0x1EF5 with EDI still holding [EAX+0x4DC], the RIGHT hand's slot -- so a znonoopa's left hand can never count as armed and every one of them lands on condition 1 with the left-arm zone bit set.

Class-0x30 state 3. Sub 0 draws an attack from g_class30_attack_picks by (rand%10 + destroyed_zones*10) and indexes g_class30_attacks BLIND -- obj+0x131A = picks[...] and the entry pointer is base + index*0x10 with no validity test of any kind; sub 1 plays the lunge until inside the attack's own distance then starts the strike with ActorSetMotionBlended(obj+0x194, entry+0x00, 0, 5), which writes the play cursor obj+0x19C = 0, and shouts (ActorPlayHitVoice kind 3); sub 2 runs the clip. Sub 2 is two independent tests in one pass, and the order and the operators are the whole behaviour: the strike is 00455bdf CMP ECX,EAX / 00455be1 JNZ over CALL 0x00456490, i.e. obj+0x19C == entry+0x08 EXACTLY, and the exit is 00455c02 MOVSX EDX,[ECX*2 + 0x4e07d0] / 4a DEC / 3bc2 CMP EAX,EDX / 7c12 JL, i.e. g_motion_play_length[obj+0x1B4] - 1 <= obj+0x19C -> obj+0x1310 = 4, obj+0x1312 = 0. So a hit frame at or past the strike clip's play length fires NOTHING: the equality is never reached, the state is not aborted and nothing is retried, the clip simply runs to its end and hands to ZombieStateBackOff. The shipped tables use that: character types 0x07, 0x0B and 0x0C share a body-condition-4 entry 2 of clip 997 at hit frame 40 where g_motion_play_length[997] is 20, and their cond-4 pick rows are ten 2s then ten 3s per zone combo, so an UNDAMAGED crawler always draws that entry and always misses, while one with its head shot off draws entry 3 (clip 1018, hit frame 3) and connects.

Class-0x30 state 4, entered after a strike. Plays the back-away walk from g_class30_motion_rows[cond][4], turns away from the position recorded when the strike began, and KEEPS the attack permit until the actor is back outside the inner approach ring or 240 frames have passed -- only then does it release and hand to state 2. That retreat is the pause between attacks; there is no cooldown timer for an ordinary zombie.

An approaching enemy asks permission to attack. One permit per player in g_attack_permits, count from g_max_attackers; on success it stores the permit index in obj+0x121 and returns 1, which is what lets ZombieStateApproach hand over to the attack state -- and what makes the camera focus on that enemy.

Class 0x30: snap the yaw at obj+0x68 straight to the player and record that player's position in obj+0x13E4/E8/EC. With one attacker the target is the camera eye; with two it is a point (+/-1.2, 0, -1.5) in front of the camera per permit index, so the two zombies converge on different shoulders. ZombieStateStrike measures its lunge distance against the recorded point, not against the camera.

special deaths for a destroyed part (obj+0x1368 bits 0x8/0x10/0x40/0x80 -> motions 0x1AC/0x1A5/0x279/0x229, set by ZombieStateTargetMotionScript and ZombieStateDragTarget from the kill-move clip id), else falls through to the directional pick. Also: condition 4 with obj+0x136C bits 0x2000000 AND 0x8000000 gives 0x3DA, character type 10 with obj+0x136C bit 0x8000 and character types 0xF-0x11 with bit 0x100000 give 0x3DB, obj+0x34 bit 0x1000000 gives 0x3F9, and conditions 5-6 fall through only when obj+0x136C & 7 is zero. Called only from ZombieStateDeath6 (0x00454D3A) and FUN_004550E0 (0x00455304), so every bit it reads is a class-0x30 bit -- including 0x8000, which ThrowerFlag calls the thrower's off-screen permit latch.
camera_yaw - actor_yaw against four +/-45 degree arcs: 0x4000 -> 992, 0xC000 -> 991, 0x0000 -> g_pDeathMotionsArc0[4], 0x8000 -> g_pDeathMotionsArc8000[6]

ChooseDeathMotion's tail: points obj+0x13A0 at the dust/splash cue list for the death clip it just chose -- DAT_005930AC..DAT_00593100 for motions 0x3D9..0x3E0 and DAT_00593124 for everything else. ZombieDeathEffectCueTick (FUN_004569B0) is what walks it.

Lands the strike on the player named by the attack permit (obj+0x121). The whole routine is one guard: (obj+0x121 == 0 || == 1) && ((s16)(char)(obj+0x1318 & 7) & entry+0x0C) != entry+0x0C, then FUN_00415300(player, 1, entry+0x0A) -- or FUN_00415300(player, 0, ...) plus ZombieReleaseAndDespawn when obj+0x34 bit 0x2000000 is up. So it whiffs when every zone in the entry's cancel mask has been shot off -- blowing an arm off stops the attack that swings it -- and a cancel mask of ZERO whiffs unconditionally, because 0 != 0 is false. The ten zeroed attack entries the shipped tables carry (types 0x00 cond 0/1, 0x01 and 0x13/0x14 cond 4, 0x07 cond 6, 0x09/0x0F/0x10/0x11 cond 3) therefore deal no damage even though ZombieStateStrike does call this on their frame 0.
Frees the attack permit at obj+0x121 and clears the global commit latch.
Decrements g_enemies_alive exactly once, guarded by obj+0x38 bit 1. This is what opens wait_enemies_alive.
Decrements g_enemies_present exactly once, guarded by obj+0x38 bit 2. This is what opens wait_enemies_present, and it is separate from the alive count.

ZombieStateDeath6's sub-1 teardown, and the only thing that takes a dead class-0x30 zombie out of the attack system. Calls ReleaseAttackSlot (FUN_00456520) first -- which frees obj+0x121 AND clears the g_attack_committed latch when the actor held an off-screen permit -- then, unless obj+0x38 bit 0 is set, raises obj+0x34 bit 0x10000 to drop it from camera tracking and zeroes its camera slot at DAT_009a5ec0 + obj+0x120 * 8, skipping that arm for the last enemy alive when obj+0x34 bit 0x800000 is set. A port that clears the permit array without clearing the latch stalls every remaining enemy: TryClaimAttackSlot reads the latch on its first line and gives up before a player is picked.

Releases the one looping held-weapon SE a class-0x30 actor may hold, and it is NOT a death scream -- the ids prove it. Does nothing unless obj+0x131B is 1, the latch EnemyZombieInitByCharType raises at 0x00453164 when it takes the loop. Then, only while g_weapon_loop_holders is exactly 1 -- this actor is the last holder -- it plays 0x4E17A9 for character type 2 and 0x2025A9 otherwise, which are COMMON2\CHAIN_SAW_22_OFF.wav and STAGE6_SE\LASER_SWORD_22_OFF.wav and are entries 4 and 34 of g_looping_se_stop_ids, so PlaySoundId calls SoundStopAllLoopingSe before playing them (and the _OFF wavs are among the 36 the game never ships). Then it clears the latch and counts g_weapon_loop_holders down. Two callers: ZombieStateDeath6 sub 1, and ZombieRefreshBodyConditionAfterShot (FUN_00454270) when a type-2 actor has lost both hand props.
Returns which advance ring the actor is in -- 1 inside the inner radius (strike range), 2, 3, 4 outward -- and sets obj+0x1358 to the step count that band allows.

Class 0x30 state 6 sub 2 hands here when the death clip ends: the twin of ThrowerEnterCorpseState. Clears obj+0x136C bits 0x60000000 (out of both pushes), sets obj+0x34 bits 0xC000 and clears 0x20001, and -- unless obj+0x38 bit 0 is set -- calls ReleaseEnemyPresentCount. **That is the second half of the enemy accounting**: ReleaseEnemyAliveCount runs at death, in ZombieReleasePermitAndUntrack, and the present count only falls here, when the corpse is finished. A corpse still on stage is present and not alive, which is exactly what separates wait_enemies_present (0x43) from wait_enemies_alive (0x44). Then it steps obj+0x194 back one frame and enters state 7, or state 8 for character types 0x12 and 3.

Runs every class-0x30 frame unless obj+0x1368 bit 1 is already set. Queries the ground at y+20 and, if the surface underneath is 5 or 0x37 -- the two WET_SURFACES -- and the actor has fallen below it, calls FUN_00408740 to put it in the water and latches bit 1 so it only happens once.

g_class30_states[0x37], called every frame of ZombieStateDeath6 sub 2 through PTR_FUN_00592BC4. When obj+0x19C reaches the next cue in the list at obj+0x13A0 it queries the ground at y+20 and spawns a dust puff (FUN_004073A0, kind 0x46) or, in rain or on surfaces 5 and 0x37, a splash (FUN_00407340, kind 0x61, and FUN_004567C0 twice), then advances the cue pointer. Effects only, plus obj+0x136C bit 0x10000 as the splash's once-only latch.

g_class30_states[0x38], reached through PTR_FUN_00592BC8. The one-shot landing puff, gated on obj+0x136C bit 0x10000 and raising it: a splash on surfaces 5 and 0x37, sound 0x61 in the rain, a dust puff otherwise. ZombieStateDeathFallAndBounce and ZombieStateArcScriptedEntrance both call it.

Per-class hook called as a strike begins. In body condition 6 -- wading -- it queries the ground under the actor and, if g_coli_hit_surface is 5 or 0x37, plays a splash and spawns sprite material 0x61 (0x62 in state 0x17). The same two surface ids as coli.py's WET_SURFACES.
The per-frame half of the same hook: one splash 0x14 frames before the clip ends, latched by obj+0x136C bit 0x10000.

Class 0x30 state 12, where ZombieStateDeath6 sends an actor that dies still holding something (obj+0x34 bit 0x1000000, which is also why ChooseDeathMotion gave it clip 0x3F9). Sub 0 drops obj+0x136C bit 0x20000000, clears obj+0x34 bit 0x4000 and sets obj+0x5C = 0xBD16872B (-0.03675f). Sub 1 holds until obj+0x19C reaches 0x3C, then clears obj+0x136C bit 0x10000 and puts 0x20000000 back. Sub 2 freezes the pose once clip 0x3F9 is spent, integrates the fall, and on hitting the ground bounces at -0.25, fires the landing effect through PTR_FUN_00592BC8 once, cuts to clip 0x3F8 at rand()%10 over a 10-frame fade, and enters ZombieEnterCorpseState once |vel.y| <= 0.15.

Class 0x30 state 13 -- 16 spawns, the come-up-out-of-the-water entrance that waits on the CAMERA rather than on a delay (contrast ZombieStateEmerge, state 27, which counts a descriptor delay down). Sub 0 raises obj+0x34 bits 0x4100 (freeze the pose, and the no-ricochet bit) and plays clip 0xB8 for character types 0xF/0x10/0x11 and 0x3D8 for every other, with ActorSetMotion and no fade. Sub 1 waits for g_cam_path_frame >= (u32)tail+0x04 -- a >=, not the == states 18 and 19 use -- then clears both bits. Sub 2 plays it out, and while the clip is 0xB8 throws splash effect 0x62 at play-clock 0x15 and 0x1B, the second preceded by two FUN_004567C0 ripples at 1.0 and 0.5. Exit at g_motion_play_length[motion] - 1 <= obj+0x19C: to state 15 with obj+0x1370 = (float)(u32)tail+0x08 when tail+0x03 is 15, else to state 1. The +0x08 walk distance is only meaningful on that arm -- for the other 13 spawns those bytes are the next descriptor.

Class 0x30 state 14 -- 2 spawns. Runs on the spot for a fixed number of frames and then joins the attack run. Sub 0 latches obj+0x1330 = tail+0x04 (30 frames in stage 1, 5 in stage 2). Sub 1 plays row[2 + ((obj+0x34 >> 0x1B) & 1)] -- the same run pair ZombieStateAttackRun and ZombieStateWalkDistance pick between -- from a random start frame rand() %% g_motion_play_length[motion], fade 5, and counts the timer down. At zero it records obj+0x13D8/DC/E0 = position (the same three words ZombieStateWalkDistance writes when it arrives) and hands to state 1. Like state 15 it never moves the actor itself: SkeletonApplyRootMotion does, out of the clip.

Class-0x30 state 15, the commonest scripted entrance after the attack run: 50 spawns across the game. sub 0 latches obj+0x1370 from the FLOAT at descriptor tail +0x04 and falls through into sub 1, which records the start point at obj+0x13C0/C4/C8 and parks sub at 2. Every frame after that it plays row[2 + ((obj+0x34 >> 0x1B) & 1)] from a random start frame -- row[4] instead when obj+0x34 bit 0x20000000 is set -- and writes the 2D distance from the start point to obj+0x1374. Reaching obj+0x1370 records obj+0x13D8/DC/E0 and hands to state 1, or to ZombieReleaseAndDespawn on the 0x20000000 arm. It never moves the actor: SkeletonApplyRootMotion does, out of the clip. There is no destination and no route -- class 0x30 has no path-following state at all (PATH_STATES is class 0x31 only), so everything past tail+0x08 belongs to the next descriptor, not to this one.

Class 0x30 state 17 -- 38 spawns, the commonest unported entrance and the second commonest of all after the attack run. Plays one clip for a fixed count and then branches to the state the descriptor names. Sub 0 latches obj+0x1330 = tail+0x08. Both subs then, unless obj+0x34 bit 0x40000000 is set, ActorSetMotion(tail+0x04) whenever obj+0x1B4 is not already it -- so the clip is re-asserted every frame rather than started once. At the countdowns end: to state 15 with obj+0x1370 = (float)(u32)tail+0x0C when tail+0x03 is 15 (and sub 1, skipping ZombieStateWalkDistances own latch), else to (s8)tail+0x03 with sub 0. Shipped values are motion at +0x04, 14 to 420 frames at +0x08 and a 1-to-10 unit walk distance at +0x0C.

Class 0x30 state 18 -- 39 spawns. Holds a clip until the camera path reaches an exact frame, then branches. Sub 0, unless obj+0x34 bit 0x40000000 is set, ActorSetMotion(tail+0x04) whenever obj+0x1B4 is not already it, and returns while neither g_cam_path_frame nor g_cam_path_frame_2 EQUALS (s32)tail+0x08 -- an equality, so the frame must be hit exactly, and the actor waits for ever on a path that skips it. On the match sub goes to 1 and falls straight through to the branch: state = (s8)tail+0x03, sub = 0. Same shape as ZombieStateWaitScriptFlagThenBranch (state 20) with a different gate, and as ZombieStateWaitForCameraFrame (state 19) without the freeze and the permit claim.

Class 0x30 state 19. Holds the actor -- optionally frozen, tail+0x0C -- until the camera path frame reaches tail+0x08, then optionally claims an attack slot (tail+0x0D) and counts tail+0x0E frames down at obj+0x1330. **This is the only place in class 0x30 that arms the attack cooldown**: it sets obj+0x1368 bit 0 and obj+0x133C = (s16)tail+0x10, then enters the strike. Every other zombie has obj+0x1368 bit 0 clear, so ZombieStateHoldAtRange forces obj+0x133C to zero and there is no wait between swings beyond the strike clip and the retreat.

Class 0x30 state 20 -- 2 spawns, both stage 2. Byte-for-byte ZombieStateWaitCameraFrameThenBranch with the camera gate replaced by g_script_flags[(s32)tail+0x08] == 1: it holds ActorSetMotion(tail+0x04) until the evt script raises that flag, then hands to (s8)tail+0x03. Both shipped spawns wait on flag 53 playing clip 198.

Class 0x30 state 21, the entrance that arrives on a clip -- the stage-2 van zombies and four more in stage 5, all six playing motion 923. sub 0 sets the descriptor's clip (params+0x04) with ActorSetMotion, no fade, and arms params+0x08 frames at obj+0x1330; it falls straight into sub 1, which counts that down and then **clears obj+0x34 bit 0x4000**; sub 2 plays the clip out. This state is the ONLY thing in the game that clears the three bits the spawn record sets to park the actor inside the vehicle: 0x4000 when the delay expires, 0x100 at obj+0x19C == 0x26 of clip 0x39B (the landing, so it stops ricocheting), and 0x2000 as it hands over. Exit is g_motion_play_length[motion] - 1 <= obj+0x19C -- the play clock, not the authored frame count -- to descriptor byte 3, substituting state 1 if that byte names 21 again; on the byte-3 == 4 arm it inlines TestApproachRing to seed obj+0x1358 first, an arm no shipped record takes. Skipping this state leaves the freeze bit on for ever: ZombieAdvanceMotion then never advances obj+0x194/0x198, and since a zombie is carried only by its clip's root motion it can never close either.

The advance. Sub-state 0 measures the actor's distance to the CAMERA (not to a player) and picks a step count from which of g_enemy_approach_rings' three radii it falls inside; sub-state 1 walks that many steps and then hands to the state named by the descriptor tail's byte 3.

Class 0x30 state 23 -- 6 spawns. A one-shot scripted kill: the actor plays a grab clip, takes the player on an exact frame and then removes itself. Sub 0 latches obj+0x1330 = tail+0x04 and, when tail+0x08 is 0xBA, plays 0xBB with only bit 0x100 raised, else plays tail+0x08 with 0x4100 (pose frozen); obj+0x136C |= 0x100000. Sub 1 waits until obj+0x1330 is -1 (fire at once, which two stage-1 spawns take) or either camera path frame equals it, then blends 0xBA on the 0xBA arm, calls TryClaimAttackSlot and ActorFacePlayerTarget, clears 0x4100, runs the per-class hook at PTR_FUN_00592BCC and records obj+0x13C4 = y. Sub 2 calls PlayerTakeDamage(obj+0x121, 1, kind) at obj+0x19C == tail+0x0C, the kind being 9 unless the clip is 0xB1, in which case 0. Sub 3 waits out g_motion_play_length[motion] - 1, throws effect 0x62 at the actor and calls ZombieReleaseAndDespawn. This is the only class-0x30 entrance that ends in a despawn rather than in a state.

Class 0x30 state 24. Sub 0 reads a destination (float x,y,z at descriptor +0x04/08/0C) and a frame count (s16 at +0x10) and sets obj+0x4C velocity = (dest - pos)/frames, which EnemyZombieUpdate then integrates -- a scripted leap or drop, not gravity. On arrival it parks the position in obj+0x13C0..C8, claims a permit, plays the clip at descriptor +0x18 and calls PlayerTakeDamage on the frame at descriptor +0x1C.

Class 0x30 state 0x19, reached only from ActorReactToHit's znjoe arm -- no spawn record sets it. Sub 0 zeroes obj+0x11C, raises obj+0x34 0x3500 and obj+0x136C 0x80000000. Sub 1 loops motion 0x1E3 until the actor is at or beyond its outer approach ring from the camera. Sub 2 plays motion 0x1DF at a random phase with blend 10 and arms a countdown of rand()%10 + 0x5F, i.e. 95..104 frames. Sub 3 counts it down once, and on the frame it lands: obj+0x328 = 1 and obj+0x29C = the u16 at g_character_parts[type] + 0x0E, which SWAPS A BONE'S DRAW SLOT, then SpawnBodyCreature (0x0043E720) releases the creature, obj+0x136C gains 0x8000 so it happens once, and obj+0x1328 goes to -1. The clip ending hands over to state 6.

Class 0x30 state 26, the burst-out entrance -- fourteen spawns. Sub 0 raises obj+0x34 bit 0x2000 and copies the tail into obj+0x1334 (delay, tail+0x04), obj+0x1374..0x137C (destination, tail+0x08..0x10) and obj+0x1380 (gravity, tail+0x14). Sub 1 counts the delay down and calls ActorArcBeginFalling, which solves the parabola and writes its frame count to obj+0x1330; the clip is 0x3BB at fade 1, or 0x399 at fade 5 when obj+0x34 bit 0x1000000 is set -- three stage-1 spawns. It then clears obj+0x136C bits 0x20000000 and 0x10000, sets bit 0x4000, and clears obj+0x34 bit 0x1000000. Sub 2 is the 0x399 wind-up ONLY: it holds in place to play frame 0x1A, integrates from 0x1A to 0x23, and at 0x23 cross-fades 0x3BB and advances -- obj+0x1330 is NOT decremented there, so that arm falls about 0x23 frames further than the solution and does not land on its point. Any other clip falls straight through to sub 3. Sub 3 integrates obj+0x4C += obj+0x58 each frame and, crucially, holds obj+0x34 bit 0x4000 -- THE POSE FREEZE -- for the whole flight except before the clip has started and for the last 0x15 frames, so the jump clip contributes no root motion while the arc owns the position; a port without that freeze applies both and sinks through the floor. While frozen, an actor whose hit points have gone below 1 switches to clip 0x3F7, which is the limp of a corpse shot out of the air and NOT a landing animation -- a live actor plays no landing clip at all. On the last frame it restores obj+0x136C bit 0x20000000, clears the velocity, sets obj+0x1350 = g_motion_play_length[current clip] - rand() %% 30 - 1, clears obj+0x34 bit 0x20000 unless obj+0x136C bit 0x10000000 is set, plays sound 0x1C16A9 with DAT_009C8E8C = 0x20 for body condition 5 or the per-class hook and 0x2A16A9 otherwise, and shouts. Sub 4 hands a dead actor to state 6 with obj+0x136C bit 0x80000000, and a live one to state 1 once obj+0x1350 <= obj+0x19C.

Class 0x30 state 27, the come-out-of-the-water entrance -- eighteen spawns, and the reason a spawn's y is where the entrance STARTS rather than where the actor stands. Sub 0 holds motion 0xB9 with the clock frozen and root motion off (obj+0x1F8 &= ~1) and arms tail+0x04 as a delay; sub 1 counts it down, turns root motion back on and plays the clip at tail+0x08 -- 178 for the water spawns, 183 for the ground ones -- whose own translation lifts the actor out; sub 2 plays it through, throwing effect 0x62 at frame 0x16 and 0x61 at frame 0x23 when the clip is 178, then goes to state 1. Three writes to obj+0x34 span the state and they are what makes an emerging zombie unstaggerable: 00458532 80ce21 OR DH,0x21 raises 0x2100 in sub 0 -- 0x100 ShotImmune, which makes ZombieOnShot return before it can pick a death state, and 0x2000 the no-hit-reaction latch ActorPlayHitReaction tests at 004544d8; 004585ec 81e2fffef6ff AND EDX,0xfff6feff drops 0x90100 as the emerge clip starts, so the actor becomes shootable again while still holding 0x2000; and 0045869f 80e6df AND DH,0xdf clears 0x2000 on the same instruction pair that writes state 1. So the whole emerge plays no stagger, and the first half of it takes no death state either.

Class 0x30 state 29 -- 6 spawns, all stage 2. The actor is a PASSENGER: it stores its own spawn position at obj+0x13E4/E8/EC (x, y, z -- note 0x13E8 is y and 0x13EC z, written out of order) and every frame sets its position to that offset PLUS g_carrier_objects own, so it rides the rideable and moves with it. Plays row[0] from rand() %% 5, fade 10, and raises obj+0x136C bit 0x100000 for as long as it rides. It reads NOTHING from the descriptor tail but byte 3: the tail belongs to the state it hands over to, which is why the three spawns whose byte 3 is 26 carry a ZombieStateDelayedLeap tail and the three whose byte 3 is 30 carry a ZombieStateArcScriptedEntrance one. The ride ends when the carrier raises its own obj+0x34 bit 0x10000000.

Class 0x30 state 30 -- 3 spawns, all stage 4, all reached from ZombieStateRideCarrier. Waits, plays a crouch, then rides a scripted ballistic arc to a world point. Sub 0 latches obj+0x1330 = tail+0x18. Sub 1 either waits for a camera frame (when the descriptors own byte +2 is 0x16, an arm no shipped record takes) or counts the timer down, then plays 0x10C for character type 0 and 0x39F for every other, arms obj+0x1330 = 0x21 or 0x2C respectively, and raises obj+0x34 bit 0x2000. Sub 2 holds until obj+0x19C reaches that. Sub 3 calls ActorArcBegin(pos, tail+0x04..0x0C, tail+0x10) and InstallArcMotionScript with DAT_00567898 for type 0 and DAT_00567958 otherwise, then resets obj+0x1360 = 0. Sub 4 runs ActorArcStep(tail+0x14) to completion, mapping its five phases onto obj+0x136C bits 0x100000 (in flight) and 0x10000, playing the landing thud through PTR_FUN_00592BC8 and sound 0x2A16A9 -- or, for body condition 5, sound 0x1C16A9 with DAT_009C8E8C = 0x20. When the step reports done it clears 0x2000 and goes to state 1, or to state 3 keeping the permit when obj+0x121 is not -1.

Class 0x30 state 31 -- 4 spawns, all stage 2 and all with the same shape. Unlike state 20 this one is not counted as an enemy until its flag comes up. Sub 0 raises obj+0x34 bit 0x100 and plays tail+0x08 (919 for all four) from rand() %% g_motion_play_length, fade 5. Sub 1 waits for g_script_flags[(u8)tail+0x04] -- flag 129 -- to equal 1, then clears obj+0x34 bit 0x10000, INCREMENTS g_enemies_present and g_enemies_alive, and latches obj+0x1330 = tail+0x0C (0, 50, 70 or 100 frames). Sub 2 counts that down then plays tail+0x10 (920) from rand() %% 10. Sub 3 hands to state 1 and clears bit 0x100 as soon as the clip is not 920 or the play clock has passed 0x4D. The two counter increments are the point: these four are invisible to wait_enemies_alive until the script lets them in.

ZombieStateAttackRun's router into state 33. Requires body condition 8, the camera yaw within 0x400 of the actor's own facing (FUN_0040A040), a free attack permit, and at least one hand still holding its original slot. Fourteen shipped spawns are condition 8, so an ordinary walker throws only when it is already facing you.

Chooses which hand throws and writes the attack index at obj+0x131A: 0 for bone 5, 1 for bone 8. Tosses a coin for which to prefer and falls back to whichever hand still holds its original draw slot -- 0x1BA9/0x1BA5 for char type 1, 0x1ECE/0x1ECA for 0x13, 0x1EF9/0x1EF5 for 0x14. Returns the bone number, 5 or 8, or 0 when both hands are empty.

Class 0x30 state 33 (0x21), the stationary thrower -- char types 1 (znassb), 0x13 (tutorial) and 0x14 (znonoopa), and the only state that never moves the actor at all. Seven shipped spawns start here, every one of them body condition 7. Subs: 0 latches the idle delay from the descriptor tail by how many hands still hold a weapon (tail+0x04 for two, tail+0x08 for one, ZombieReleaseAndDespawn for none); 1 plays row[0] and counts that delay down; 2 waits for TryClaimAttackSlot, then takes the permit, picks a hand with ZombiePickThrowingHand, plays g_class30_attacks[type][cond][obj+0x131A]'s strike motion from frame 0 and shouts; 3 waits for obj+0x19C to reach the entry's hit frame (+0x08) and calls ZombieThrowHandWeapon; 4 waits out the clip, drops the commit flag, and goes back to sub 0 while a hand is still armed -- or, for condition != 7, straight back to state 1; 5 idles tail+0x0C frames and then TAKES ONE OF TWO ENDINGS, chosen at 0045945C by obj+0x38 bit 0x10 (TEST byte ptr [ESI+0x38],0x10 -- f6463810). Bit CLEAR: state 15 with obj+0x1370 = tail+0x10 when tail+0x03 is 0, or state 26 with the point at tail+0x10..0x18 and the gravity at tail+0x20 otherwise; the state 15 exit is what raises obj+0x34 bit 0x20000000, the arm of ZombieStateWalkDistance that retires the actor instead of attacking. Bit SET: it never moves again -- ReleaseEnemyAliveCount, ReleaseEnemyPresentCount and ReleaseAttackSlot on the spot, g_enemy_slots[obj+0x120*8] and the hit slot cleared, obj+0x1330 = tail+0x1C, obj+0x34 |= 0x10100 (NoCameraTrack | ShotImmune), sub 6. Sub 6 (LAB_00459562, which the retire arm falls into on the same frame) plays row[0] and despawns once g_enemies_present < 1 AND g_players_in_play != 0 AND --obj+0x1330 < 1, so the wait_enemies_alive this actor was holding opens the moment it stops rather than at the end of a walk. EnemyZombieInitByCharType is what puts that bit there, from obj+0x34 bit 1; two spawn records in the game set it and both are stage 3 block 2 step 4's axe men. Note obj+0x34 bit 0x1000000, which sub 0 tests and the walk arm clears, is written by NOTHING in the image -- the test is always true and the clear is a no-op.
