Class 0x30's straight-flight projectile state, slot 1 of g_zombie_thrown_weapon_states. Sub 0 solves ttl = |target - pos| / obj+0x1370 and the per-frame velocity from it. Sub 1 is the flight, and its tumble is ONE instruction: obj+0x64 += obj+0x135C at 0x00459731 -- into the **X** term of the draw, with no sign test on the throwing hand. That is the half class 0x31 does differently: ThrownWeaponFlyToTarget accumulates into obj+0x68, the Y term, and negates it unless obj+0x1358 is bone 5. Subs 2-4 are the landing: yaw from the direction plus 0x8000, a one-off random kick of (+/-1)*(rand&2)*0x100 into obj+0x64, then 0x1E frames stuck and 0x3C blinking. NOTHING writes the projectile's obj+0x135C -- both launchers leave it, and FUN_004A6FA0 clears only the first 0xD dwords over FUN_004A7400's uncleared free-list block -- so the rate is recycled arena memory.

Thrown-weapon state 2, the arced throw char type 1 uses. Sub 0 hands ZombieThrownWeaponBeginArc a gravity of +0.009 for bone 5 and -0.009 for bone 8. Sub 1 integrates the arc and, on arrival, calls PlayerTakeDamage(player, 1, 6). Subs 2 to 4 are the same stick-to-the-screen and blink tail as ZombieThrownWeaponStateStraight.

Solves the ballistic velocity for a thrown weapon. Four FUN_0040A040 angle-window tests on the heading from the thrower to the target decide whether the curve bends along X or Z; the flight time is the distance in the two axes that are not the curve's divided by the speed, and the curved axis gets `(2*delta - g*t*t) / (2*t)` with the acceleration in obj+0x58..0x60.

Thrown-weapon state 3: the player shot it out of the air. Sub 0 spawns sprite effect 0x52, raises obj+0x34 bits 0x4008000 and releases the attack permit. Sub 1 picks a point 10 to 100 units away from where the weapon was in camera space, in a random direction on both axes, and a random spin. Subs 2 and 3 tumble it there and despawn after 180 frames.

Writes the projectile's target at obj+0x13C0..0x13C8: a point in camera space transformed to the world. The axe (0x249) aims 1.5 below and 4 in front of the eye, everything else 4 in front; with two players the x is offset -0.6 or +0.6 by the permit the projectile inherited, so each player is thrown at rather than both at the midpoint. obj+0x1360, copied from g_max_attackers at the throw (NOT from the player count), selects the fixed centre instead: the offset is applied only when the game is running two permits.

Throws the weapon out of bone `hand`. Allocates a 0x13F4 object running ZombieThrownWeaponUpdate, positions it at that bone's world matrix (obj + bone*0x90 + 0x274), gives it radius 2.0 in both spheres and obj+0x1F8 = 5 so it draws and registers, hands it the thrower's attack permit and clears the thrower's, parents it at +0x1390 and remembers the hand at +0x1358. The thrower's hand slot is swapped to the empty-hand variant AND that same bone record's +0x78 is zeroed -- MOV [EDI+0x554],EBX (899f54050000) at 0045A2B2 for bone 5 and MOV [EDI+0x704],EBX (899f04070000) at 0045A2DB for bone 8, with EBX zero. 0x554 is 0x20C + 5*0x90 + 0x78, INSIDE bone 5's own record and not the base of another one; SkeletonWalkNode writes that field as the bone's hit-sphere radius, so the hand it has just emptied stops being shootable. SpawnThrownWeapon (00450540) does the identical write for class 0x31, where Ghidra renders it as bone*0x90 + 0x284. The projectile's own asset is obj+0x13F0: 0x249 (znonoo.bin part 0, the axe) for char types 0x13 and 0x14, and znassb.bin parts 2 and 3 for char type 1. The axe flies straight (state 1, speed 1.5 for body condition 7 and 1.0 otherwise); anything else arcs (state 2, speed 1.0).

The class 0x30 thrown weapon's per-frame entry, and it has no class id at all: its only reference in the binary is the allocation in ZombieThrowHandWeapon, so it is never reached through g_class_handlers. Dispatches g_zombie_thrown_weapon_states[obj+0x1310], then draws the model as Rz(obj+0x6C) * Ry(obj+0x68) * Rx(obj+0x1364 + obj+0x64) -- the same product ThrownWeaponUpdate (0x00450780) emits for class 0x31, even though the two states accumulate their tumble into different terms of it. A hit that is not already flagged 0x4000000 scores against the player and jumps to state 3.

Class 0x30 state 34 (0x22), and the whole reason obj+0x1394 exists on a zombie: the actor walks at the object at obj+0x1394 -- for the 47 class-0x10 captors that is the civilian CivilianInit built them for -- and NOT at the camera. Sub 0/1 take a {f32 arrive_dist; u16 loops; u16 motion; u16 frame} header from ZombieScriptForState and leave the cursor at header+10; sub 2 turns toward the target with TurnActorAwayFromPoint at 0x1A0 each frame and, once the 2D distance is inside arrive_dist, switches to state 35 sub 1 and raises 0x800 in the civilian's OWN wait word (sub+0x00), which is what releases the civilian's script. If the target dies it parks in state 45. Every one of the 23 spawns in the game that starts here is a civilian's captor.

Class 0x30 state 35 (0x23), the scripted attack the walk hands over to. Steps a list of s16[4] {motion, frame, loops, mode} through the cursor at obj+0x1398, advancing it by one entry each time. sub 0 selects the blob with ZombieScriptForState and points the cursor past the first entry; sub 1 loads the entry the cursor already points at -- it does NOT re-select -- and advances it; sub 2 plays, fires the kill cue when obj+0x19C reaches the entry's mode (raising 0x4000000 on the target's obj+0x34, the same bit a killing shot raises), and on g_motion_play_length - 1 counts the loop down. At zero it takes the next entry, or ZombieScriptEnded when the cursor's motion short is below 1. A negative mode clears obj+0x34 bit 0x10000000; a non-negative one sets it, so an entry with a kill cue is also the one that will not be re-ranked out of its swing.

Class 0x30 state 36 (0x24). ZombieStateTargetMotionScript with a fifth short per entry: a g_script_flags index raised on the cue frame, which is how a set piece's zombie tells the evt it has finished.

Class 0x30 state 37 (0x25). Allocates a 0x19C-byte companion object running FUN_00442740 with +0x198 = this and +0x194 = the script record -- the thing the zombie is carrying or wielding -- turns toward the CAMERA, and raises 0x800 in the civilian's wait word when that companion's +0x11C drops below 1. [open] the companion class is unread.

Class 0x30 state 38 (0x26), the commonest attack state of the captor family. Header is {f32 x, y, z; s16 motion, frame; s16 loops, mode} and then s16[4] entries. The per-frame arm switches on the mode: 0 and 1 retire through ZombieRetireAndCredit as soon as ActorBoundsOnScreen says the actor has left the frame, 1 and 2 also turn toward the header's point, 3 retires when the loop count runs out.

Raises 0x4008001 on obj+0x34, credits obj+0x131C to the player named by the target civilian's sub+0x6C (or a random one when that is -1), runs the two count releases and parks sub at 4. This is how a captor leaves once its script is done -- and obj+0x131C is exactly the byte CivilianPruneDeadChildren reads back to decide who is paid the 400.

Class 0x30 state 39 (0x27). Reads the CIVILIAN's own sub-block and waits on the pair op 0x1A writes there: sub+0x2E is a COUNT of captors still to order (each one parked here consumes one, so op 0x1A(35,1) raises exactly one and a script that wants two issues it twice) and sub+0x2C the order. 0x31 means die -- the zombie flags itself dead and takes its killer from the civilian's sub+0x6C -- anything else is a class-0x30 state id it switches to and dispatches immediately, a tail call through g_class30_states so the new state runs on the same frame. This is the civilian script driving its own captors. Sub 0 also HIDES the actor and sub 1 puts it back: obj+0x1350 = obj+0x34; obj+0x34 |= 0x18000; obj+0x1F8 &= ~1 (model+0x64 bit 0, what FUN_0040A590 reads before the ground decal); and 0045bb31 MOV EAX,[ESI+0x1d4] / 0045bb37 MOV byte ptr [EAX+1],DL with DL=0 -- model+0x40 is the part array and +1 of the first record is the draw gate SkeletonDrawWalk (FUN_004110D0) reads. So stage 2 block 16's two znebi2 are invisible in the water until their civilian's killed script calls them up.

Rotates a world point into the actor's own frame by the inverse of its yaw/roll/pitch and returns whether the local z is positive. The arrival test for the states that walk PAST a point rather than up to it.
Class 0x30 state 40 (0x28). Header {f32 x, y, z; s16 motion, frame}; walks until ActorPointIsAhead says the point is behind, then either ends the script or hands over to state 35.
Class 0x30 state 41 (0x29). The same header, but the arrival test is a 2D distance of 5.0 and the actor turns toward the point at 0x1A0 while it closes.

Class 0x30 state 42 (0x2A), reached only from ZombieScriptEnded when a captor's exit lands on AttackRun and its descriptor tail+0x0C is not -1. Runs g_class30_states[obj+0x132C] every frame as a delegate, re-captures whatever state the delegate asked for, forbids it reaching Strike (bounces to HoldAtRange and frees the permit at g_attack_permits[obj+0x121]), and graduates to the delegate only when g_active_cam_path == (s16)tail+0x0C and g_cam_path_frame == (s16)tail+0x0E. 3 of the 69 captor spawns pass through it. The only captor-family code that touches g_attack_permits.

Class 0x30 state 43 (0x2B). Copies the civilian's position AND rotation onto the zombie every frame -- the two are one animation -- plays motion 0x1A4, and on the header's cue frame kills the civilian and switches to 0x1A8. If the civilian is already dead it plays 0x1AA instead.

Class 0x30 state 44 (0x2C). Claims the civilian's sub+0x64 slot so only one zombie pounces at a time, leaps at a point one unit up and 2.5 forward of the civilian's own bone matrix under gravity -0.0408, and on contact kills it and plays 0x0D16A9. A zombie that finds the slot taken idles at motion 0x41F.

Class 0x30 state 45 (0x2D). Stands in the character's own walk clip for rand() %% 11 + 10 frames and then returns to the state and sub remembered at obj+0x1354 / obj+0x1358. Where a captor goes when the thing it was working on dies under it.

If the passed object is non-null and carries 0x4000000 on obj+0x34, end the current script through ZombieScriptEnded and report 1. A null target reports 0, which is what lets the same states run on a spawn that has no civilian.

FUN_0045C8D0. The captor family's terminator, and where a captor turns on the player: if obj+0x1310 already equals the descriptor tail's attack state (s8 tail+0x03) it goes to AttackRun, otherwise it enters that attack state. The WalkPastPoint arm additionally shortcuts straight to AttackRun when ActorPointIsAhead says the script's point is already in front. Clears obj+0x34 & 0xFFFFDAFF (the three bits ZombieApplyScriptMode sets) for every state but WalkToTarget, and issues no motion call of its own.

The captor family's script selector: descriptor tail +0x08 when the actor is in the tail's attack state (tail+0x03), tail +0x04 otherwise. Two blobs per spawn, and both are entry lists of s16[4] {motion, frame, loops, mode}. **It is called only where the engine WRITES obj+0x1398** -- ZombieScriptEnded's 0x23/0x24 arm, ZombieStateWalkToTarget subs 0 and 1 (which store blob+10, past the head), and ZombieStateTargetMotionScript / ZombieStateTargetScriptWithFlag sub 0 (blob+4, past the first entry). Every step in between READS that pointer back and never re-selects. The distinction matters because the two are not the same answer: a captor whose initial state is 0x23 and whose attack state is 0x22 has its walk leave the cursor in the ATTACK blob and then enter state 0x23, which is not its attack state -- so re-deriving from the state at that point hands back the TARGET blob and replays a list already finished.
Applies a script entry's mode word to obj+0x34: -3 sets 0x100, -2 sets 0x400 and clears 0x2000, anything else sets 0x2400.

A second, looser on-screen test than ActorIsOnScreen (0x00409C10): projects the actor's view-space bounding interval at obj+0x10C/0x110 padded by obj+0x124 and asks whether any of it lands inside 640x480. ZombieStateRetireOffScreen uses it to decide when a captor may vanish.

The noise a zombie makes as it kills a civilian, by clip and then by character type: 0xFE/0xFF and 0x3CB give 0x1D16A9, otherwise type 2 gives 0x0516A9, 0x0D gives 0x1B16A9, 0x0E/0x13/0x14 give 0x0316A9 and everything else 0x1A16A9.
Called when an attack is interrupted: releases the slots, sets body condition 4 and hands the actor to its leave state.

Places a class-0x30 actor rigidly on g_carrier_object (0x009A5C34), position AND yaw. MatrixTranslate(carrier+0x40/44/48), MatrixRotateY(carrier+0x68), MatrixRotateY(0x8000), then MatrixTransformPoint of the actor's stashed local offset obj+0x13D8/DC/E0 into obj+0x40/44/48; MatrixToEulerBams (FUN_00401AE0) takes the composed yaw into obj+0x68 and obj+0x135C, the stashed local yaw, is added on top. Only the carrier's +0x68 is read -- its pitch and roll are ignored. TWO CALLERS, BOTH CLASS 0x30. EnemyZombieInitByCharType calls it once at 00453053, in the arm taken when obj+0x34 bit 3 is set: that arm is what stashes 0x13D8/DC/E0 from the descriptor position and 0x135C from the descriptor yaw, and raises obj+0x136C bit 0x10000000. EnemyZombieUpdate then calls it EVERY FRAME while that bit is up, at 00453424, BEFORE the state dispatch at 00453434. So for such a spawn the descriptor position is a CARRIER-RELATIVE OFFSET and not a world position, in whatever state the actor is in -- the 0x13D8 stash is the only surviving copy of it, and the state machine never sees the difference. Exactly FOUR shipped descriptors set obj+0x34 bit 3, all class 0x30, all in st5evtbl block 2 step 2 op 38: 0x1D44 (-4.6,10,-16.5) state 32, 0x1D74 (-4.6,5,-2.6) state 32, 0x1DA4 (-4.6,5,7) state 32 and 0x1DD4 (4.6,0,0) state 18. The scene reset. Copies the three approach-ring radii from DAT_004C4CD0/D4/D8 into g_enemy_approach_rings and its two neighbours -- **one table, no difficulty index**, so the rings and therefore the attack queue are the same on every setting. Also clears the camera easing, the fixed-y flag and the per-scene route history.
evt 0x4E. Sets g_evt_yield and does not advance pc, so the VM re-runs it every frame forever -- a park, not the end of a scene. Confirmed as slot 0x4E of the dispatch table at 0x005931D8.

Event opcode 0x4F. Advances the STEP, and only follows the route table when the step list is exhausted:      step += 1;     if (EvtGetStep(scene, block, step) == -1) {   /* steps ran out */         r = g_scene_routes[scene] + block*8;      /* 8-byte route record */         switch (r.kind) {           case 0: block = r.next[0];              break;           case 1: block = r.next[branch_choice];  break;           case 2: block = block + 1;              break;         }         step = 1;     }     pc = EvtGetStep(scene, block, step);     branch_choice = 0;  It touches NO actors: no despawn, no sweep, no counter reset beyond the cursor. A block's steps are one continuous room and this fires between them, so anything that retired actors here would empty a room mid-encounter -- measured over the shipped scripts, 71 step boundaries and 19 block boundaries are crossed by live enemy-class spawns with no intervening enemy gate. The only wholesale sweep in the game is the scene change, which rebases the 16 MB object arena in FUN_004A7310.  Formerly named EvtAdvanceBlockOrRoute, and the opcode formerly `end_block`; both read as a block terminator, which is what this is not.  The `branch_choice = 0` at the bottom is on the NORMAL RETURN PATH, after pc = EvtGetStep(...), so it fires on every STEP advance and not only on a block change -- three documents and the browser port all had it as `reset on every block change`, which is a much weaker claim. It is why almost every branch block spawns the actor that decides the branch in the block's LAST step: a write made earlier is cleared by the next step boundary. The scene-over path returns before it, leaving the last value standing. THE SCENE-OVER PATH IS WHERE THE NEXT STAGE'S STARTING BLOCK COMES FROM. When EvtGetBlock(scene, block) returns -1 -- the route walked onto a hole -- it calls MarkSceneOver and then, for every game mode but 2, does g_evt_block_index = *(s16*)(g_scene_routes[scene] + g_evt_block_index * 8 - 6) (0x0045F0DA). That address is record (block-1) at +0x02, which is next[0] of the record the walk just left -- and since a kind-2 record ends a scene by doing block+1 onto the hole that follows it, THE TERMINAL RECORD'S next[0] IS THE BLOCK THE NEXT SCENE STARTS AT. Mode 2 takes DAT_009A2BBC (the training lesson) instead. The pc then goes to scene 7 block 0 step 0, the inter-stage stub inside comevtbl. Measured over the shipped route tables: stage 3 can start at block 0 or block 7 and stage 4 at block 0 or block 4, depending which ending the previous stage reached; every other stage has one. Arcade and Original reach the same set.

The run-phase dispatcher: one indirect call, (*g_pfnRunPhaseHandlers[g_nRunPhase])(). Thirteen handlers at 0x005679A8, and this is their only caller. Phase 0 ResetGameOnStart starts a run, 1 AdvanceToNextScene loads the next stage, 2-4 are the continue screen, 5 RunPhaseArmSceneAdvance and 6 RunPhaseStepToNextScene are the two-frame stage-to-stage step.

The new-game reset, one level above ResetSceneOnEnter (0x0045EDD0). Picks the opening scene and block by g_GameMode -- scene 6 / DAT_009A2BBC for mode 2, scene 0 / block 0x10 for mode 3, scene 0 / block 0 otherwise -- fills the 0x28-entry g_route_history with -1, zeroes the run totals g_civilians_seen_total and g_civilians_rescued_total and the first three dwords (six scenes) of both g_civilians_seen_by_scene and g_civilians_rescued_by_scene, clears the three-dword-stride block at DAT_009C8EC0, and ends by calling FUN_00460030, which loads the scene and calls ResetSceneOnEnter. So the per-scene tallies are zeroed here for the whole run and again per scene there.

The stage-to-stage transition. Walks the two players (stride 0x98 shorts = 0x130 bytes) and puts any whose g_player_state is 5 -- in play -- back to 2, then calls LoadSceneAndReset and steps the phase counter DAT_009C90A4. So a player is parked out of "in play" for the duration of the load, which is why IsPlayerAttackable refuses and no enemy commits an attack across a scene change.

Load the scene g_scene_index names and reset it -- the only caller of ResetSceneOnEnter (0x0045EDD0) in the playable path, and its last act. param_2 == 1 takes the attract path (a DAT_00598028-times preload loop through FUN_00437F90/SetupSceneProjection) and 0 the ordinary one; then per g_GameMode and g_wCaptionMode it queues the caption and title assets, drains the asset jobs, allocates the scene task at LAB_00460710, calls CameraClearHookAndPose, and finally ResetSceneOnEnter. Three callers, all of them "enter a scene": ResetGameOnStart (0x0045FEF0) for the first scene of a run, AdvanceToNextScene (0x0045FFF0) for each stage transition, and RunAttractDemo (0x00426800) for the demo playlist.

Run phase 5, the frame before RunPhaseStepToNextScene. Sets g_nRunPhaseDelay = 1 and steps g_nRunPhase to 6, then falls into the same player-state test FUN_004601D0 runs: a player whose state has no row in the table at 0x00579CD4 sends the phase to 3 (the continue screen) or 0xB instead, so a stage only advances with a player still in play.

Run phase 6, and the one instruction that moves the game from one stage to the next: g_scene_index = g_scene_index + 1 for game modes 0 and 1, then phase 1 (AdvanceToNextScene) -- or phase 7 when the increment reaches 6, which is past the last stage. It does NOT choose the block: EvtAdvanceStepOrRoute already wrote g_evt_block_index from the terminal route record, and nothing between here and FUN_0045EBC0 touches it. Waits for g_nRunPhaseDelay to reach 0 first. Mode 2 goes to scene 6 instead; mode 3 reads the {scene, block} pair at 0x0055CBBC indexed by DAT_009A2268.

Builds g_class41_fragment_counts[placer+0x1F4] objects running PropUpdateType40, each carrying its index at obj+0x1B8 and the placer's +0x1F4 as a sub-kind at obj+0x1BA, with obj+0x11C copied from the placer, a 5.5 hit radius and flags 0x80000001. The breakable prop placed by PlaceBreakableGroup. Despawns once g_evt_step_index has changed more than its +0x199 lifetime times -- a lifetime in event STEPS, not blocks. On a shot: +0x11C 2 -> 1 cracks it, plays 0x1D16A9 and sets +0x2C0 = 1.0 so it shakes, and marks every member it supports to shake too; +0x11C 1 -> 0 destroys it, plays 0x1A16A9, awards through BreakablePropAwardHit, clears its slot in g_breakable_members and decrements g_item_set_countdown -- releasing the set's item when that reaches zero. Destroying and toppling are DIFFERENT: a destroyed prop at stack level 0 has its object entry point overwritten with BreakableEffectUpdate and becomes a puff for 0x48 frames, and one above level 0 shatters through BreakablePropSpawnShatter -- neither falls. Falling (state 1 -> 2, settled by BreakablePropGroundContact) happens only to a prop whose supporting members have all gone, which is what makes a stack collapse from the bottom. Note also that only the destroying shot pays: the crack calls BreakablePropAwardHit with award=0.

Resolves which player's shot landed from obj+0x34 bits 1 and 2 -- both set means rand() picks -- then awards 10 points unless the caller passes 0 or g_GameMode is 2, and counts the hit into g_player_hit_count for the accuracy grade.

Breaks a stacked prop into 15 fragments: allocates a 0x2B4 object running FUN_004653b0 and seeds each fragment from g_shatter_fragment_offsets and g_shatter_fragment_angles, with a radial velocity of 0.1..0.3 about the fragment's own bearing and a random spin of +/-0x400 on each axis.
The break puff. Draws the effect record at +0x324 for 0x48 frames and then kills itself.

In the falling state it records the first such point in +0x198; in the toppling state it keeps the lowest and re-seats the prop's origin on it, which is how a broken prop comes to rest leaning on a corner. The impact spark on a prop hit. Allocates a 0x50 object with effect id 0x904 at the shot's screen point unprojected to the prop's depth.

The prop PlaceKindedProp builds -- class 0x41 type 4, 70 spawns and the most-placed constructor in the game. Shot handling depends on the model: a 0x19E8 crate takes two (the first cracks it, pays nothing and hides the model behind 0xFFFF), every other kind takes one. The destroying shot pays 10 through BreakablePropAwardHit, plays g_prop_kind_params[kind]+4, runs the break effect at +0x324 for DAT_004E07D0[effect]-2 frames and then despawns -- and releases the item set in +0x194 through the SAME g_item_set_countdown and the same switch BreakablePropUpdate uses. 37 of the 70 hide an item, which is more than the group placer accounts for. Draw-time shake, ground shadow 0x10D0 or 0x10D1 by kind.

Class 0x41's shared prologue: 25 of the update routines open with it. Despawns the prop when g_evt_step_index has CHANGED more than obj+0x11C times -- the counter is the step index, so this is a lifetime in event STEPS, not blocks -- and immediately when g_scene_index==1 and g_script_flags[0x77] is set. This is what makes obj+0x11C a LIFETIME IN EVENT STEPS -- PlaceGenericProp writes the descriptor's +0x11C to both this and obj+0x28C, and only types 5, 12 and 33 ever draw the slot.

g_class41_updates[5] (0x005936BC + 5*4), the object PlaceGenericProp allocates for descriptor type 5. Its whole body is MatrixStackPush, MatrixTranslate from +0x19C/1A0/1A4, roll/yaw/pitch from +0x1D4/1D0/1CC, AssetDrawSlot((s16)+0x28C), MatrixStackPop. No hit test, no state, no break path: a class-0x41 type 5 prop is scenery, and nothing in the engine smashes it when an actor walks through it.

g_class41_updates[70] AND [71] -- 23 spawns, Original Mode's collectible. Despawns at once unless g_GameMode == 1, then runs PropExpireByStepLifetime and a per-scene removal rule. Shooting it (bit 3, and not already taken) pays the hit, increments g_original_items_taken[obj+0x290] up to 99, calls FUN_00475E40 with the pickup id from g_original_item_records + 0x8, plays 0x3616A9 and starts a 0x32-frame pickup animation from slot 0x119C or 0x116A. THE BRANCH: in scene 2, block 4, with g_script_flags[0x13] raised, it writes g_script_branch_var = g_scene_index -- which in that scene is 2. That is the only write, and it happens whether or not the item was taken. The rest of the routine is the bob-and-spin idle and the two draws.

The g_GameMode == 1 release -- original/story per the g_GameMode row -- taken when the prop's +0x2A0 is not -1. Builds a 0x378 object running FUN_004675a0 with +0x2A0 as its kind. Three shipped members carry one: group 0 member 0 has kind 2 and group 7 members 3 and 4 have kind 5, and all three also hide an ordinary item set, so mode 1 substitutes its own drop for theirs.

g_class41_updates[14]. A shootable object that flips the route branch. On the first hit -- obj+0x34 bit 3 set and bit 0x40000000 clear -- it pays the hit, writes g_script_branch_var = 1 - obj+0x11C, plays sound 0x1116A9 and latches 0x40000000 so it fires once. So the DESCRIPTOR'S +0x11C names the default route and shooting it takes the other: a descriptor of 0 branches to 1 when shot, one of 1 branches to 0. It then falls, spins at rand()%0x81 + 0xC0 BAMS a frame, lands on one of four rails, swings to 0x4000 and stops, giving back g_enemies_alive on the way -- the object is counted as an ENEMY, and PlaceGenericProp case 0x0E increments that counter and seeds g_script_branch_var with the same +0x11C. Un-shot it retires itself at frame 0xD1. While upright it overrides the scene light direction with its own spin. One shipped spawn: stage 2 block 5 step 4, +0x11C = 0, in a block whose route is {21, 6, -1}.

g_class41_updates[19]. The same branch mechanism as PropUpdateType14: first hit pays, writes g_script_branch_var = 1 - obj+0x11C, plays 0xF16A9, latches 0x40000000, gives back g_enemies_present and starts falling at -0.02722 a frame. PlaceGenericProp case 0x13 likewise increments g_enemies_present and seeds the branch variable with the descriptor's +0x11C, so this too is an enemy whose default route is in the descriptor and whose alternate is one shot away. The rest of the routine is a four-swing idle on obj+0x1E8, a script-flag reaction (g_script_flags[0x21]) that plays 0x2116A9 and runs a hinge curve from g_pHingeCurvesXYZ, and a lifetime that despawns it after three step changes. One shipped spawn: stage 2 block 7 step 4, +0x11C = 0, route {8, 25, -1}.

One segment of the chain PlaceChainSegments builds, and a writer of g_script_branch_var. Re-registers itself in g_chain_segments every frame and expires on obj+0x11C step changes. A hit pays the award, plays 0xF16A9, sparks, and shakes the two neighbours either side of it by writing their +0x1B8/+0x1BC swing rates. THE BRANCH: with g_GameMode == 1, group id 1, g_evt_block_index == 0x16 and segment 0 of that group not yet latched, it sets that segment's +0x1B0 to 1 and writes g_script_branch_var = 2 -- so shooting ANY link of chain group 1 in block 0x16 opens the route, once. Segment 0 additionally fires FUN_004699C0 when its +0x1B0 reaches 1. Each segment hangs from the one above through the matrix at +0x1C0, which is how the whole chain swings from one hit.

g_class41_updates[25]. Writes g_script_branch_var = 1 when shot, but ONLY while g_evt_block_index == 0x17 -- the block its one shipped spawn stands in (stage 2 block 23, route {24, 26, -1}). Pays the hit, plays 0x2F16A9, calls FUN_00420810(2, 0x14), gives back g_enemies_present and latches obj+0x34 bits 0x44000000. PlaceGenericProp case 0x19 increments g_enemies_present and seeds the branch variable to 0, so this is the same default-then-flip shape as types 14 and 19 with the default written as a literal. Opens with PropExpireByStepLifetime and retires itself at frame 0xFE; the tail plays an effect through obj+0x324/0x328 on alternate frames.

Class 0x41 type 32, the lift. Script flag 0x37 holds obj+0x1A0 at g_camera_block_eye.y - 15, and stage 2 raises it over cp_st2 path 28 (slot 83), whose eye climbs 55.0 -> 144.2 -- an 89-unit vertical ride starting exactly at the spawn's Y of 40.0. Flags 0x6B and 0x6C fold the near and far pairs of cage leaves 0x200 BAMS a frame from 0x4000->0x8000 and 0x8000->0xC000, each playing COMMON\\DOORKICK3_22K_1.WAV on its first frame; obj+0x2A0 counts frames flag 0x6B has been up and releases an overhead panel (obj+0x1CC, 0->0x1000) after 0x27. Every angle test is < limit+1, so each hinge rests one step past the round number. Models are komono_suimon.bin entries 5/6/9 -- the FILE is named for the area, not for this object; rendered it is a folding lattice cage gate. Stage 2 places one, block 17 step 8.

The container PlaceFallingContainer builds -- class 0x44 selector 16. Two shots: the first pays nothing, swaps to slot 0xA51, plays 0xE16A9 and knocks it loose with an upward 0.8..1.09 and gravity 0.05444, so it tumbles and settles against the 48-point hull at 0x00594788; the second pays 10, plays 0x1716A9 or 0x1616A9, throws three FUN_0046AD20 fragments and releases its item set. Same g_item_set_countdown and the same release switch as class 0x41, so the two classes share one countdown per set. Lifetime is in evt blocks like the rest.

g_class41_updates[40] -- 28 spawns, the most-placed of the branch writers. A shootable object that bursts into FORTY fragments: the hit fills obj+0x23C.. with forty positions, spins and velocities from rand(), pays the hit with an award, plays 0x2D16A9 or 0x2C16A9 and latches obj+0x1B9; the fragments then fall at -0.02722 a frame, bounce off g_camera_fixed_eye_y + 1 at -0.4, and are drawn from slot 0xCA5 + i for 100 frames under a light colour this routine sets itself. obj+0x1BA is a sub-kind from the placer. THE BRANCH: sub-kind 9 counts its own breakages in g_branch_prop_shot_count (0x007DCF18) while g_GameMode == 1, and once that reaches 2 -- both of them shot -- with g_script_flags[0x11] raised, it writes g_script_branch_var = 2 and stores -1 in the counter so it fires once. Also despawns at camera path 100 frame 0x50 and path 0x67 frame 10, and on g_script_flags[0x77] in scene 1.

g_class41_updates[56]. Original Mode's branch: when g_script_flags[5] is raised and obj+0x192 is still 0 it latches 1, plays 0x2116A9, calls FUN_00420810(4, 0x14) and -- if g_GameMode == 1 AND g_evt_block_index == 9 -- writes g_script_branch_var = 2. So the shot is not what opens this route; a script flag is, and the route only exists in story mode. Being shot separately pays the hit, raises DAT_009C720E, plays 0xF16A9 and starts it falling. Draws slot 0x1866 with a 0x10D3 sub-part, and once latched runs 60 frames of g_pHingeCurvesXYZ. One shipped spawn: stage 4 block 9, route {11, -1, 17}.

g_class41_updates[69]. Original Mode only -- the routine's first line despawns it unless g_GameMode == 1 -- and it is dead in blocks 8 and 3. When g_script_flags[0x23] is raised, obj+0x192 is positive and g_script_branch_var is ALREADY 1, it promotes the branch to 2 and spawns a story-mode item at a fixed point. So this is the one writer that reads the variable before writing it: it upgrades a rescue's route to the story route rather than choosing one outright. Being shot pays the hit, plays 0x1D16A9, sparks and starts a fall. Draws slots 0x13F8 and 0x13F7. Two shipped spawns, stage 1 blocks 1 and 9.

g_class41_updates[73]. Original Mode only. Despawns while g_app_state is 5 (the attract demo) and expires on obj+0x11C step changes. When shot in block 7 with g_GameMode == 1 and g_script_flags[0x12] raised, it pays the hit, plays 0xE16A9 and -- IF the player is carrying original item 5, 6 or 0xC (PlayerHoldsOriginalItem) -- latches obj+0x192, writes g_script_branch_var = 2 and plays 0x381BA9. So this route is behind the key as well as the shot. It then plays object path 0x179 forward, firing 0x371BA9 at frame 0x46 and stopping at 0x69. Draws slot 0x1871. One shipped spawn: stage 4 block 7, route {8, -1, 22}.

g_class41_updates[75] (0x005936BC + 75*4 = 0x005937E8, its one xref). One shipped spawn: stage 4 block 2 step 5, at 9580, a 'generic' placement with type 75, slot/lifetime 2. It raises g_script_flags[20] on THREE instructions, not one -- 0x004710D7, 0x00471120 and 0x00471263 -- and stage 4 block 2 step 7's wait_script_flag 0x14 is the only gate on that flag in the six shipped scripts; no set_script_flag in stage 4 names it. Head: if (g_GameMode != 1) { g_script_flags[0x14] = 1; ActorDespawn(obj); return; } -- so in Arcade it raises the flag and leaves on its first frame, which is NOT the plain despawn the other Original-Mode-only types (70, 71, 72, 77) take. Then an INLINE variant of PropExpireByStepLifetime (FUN_00466640) with the scene-1 sweep left OUT and two extra lines folded in: on every change of g_evt_step_index it increments obj+0x2A4 and, when that reaches exactly 2 and obj+0x192 is still 0, raises the flag again; then the ordinary ++obj+0x197 > obj+0x11C despawn. The CMP g_GameMode,1 / JNZ at 0x00471161 is dead -- the head already proved it equal. Shot arm (obj+0x34 bit 3 and obj+0x192 == 0): BreakablePropAwardHit(obj+0x34, 0), a crosshair spark through FUN_004666B0(obj, (flags&2)?0:1, 1.5f), PlaySoundId(0xE16A9) and PlaySoundId(0x391BA9), a no-op call to PoseHookNone, obj+0x2A0 = 1, obj+0x192 = 1, and SpawnStoryModeItem (FUN_00467B90) with obj+0x19C/1A0/1A4 TEMPORARILY overwritten to (142.0, -59.8, -888.7) and put back straight after, plus DAT_007DCD14 = 0. Then while obj+0x192 == 1 it adds 1.0 a frame to obj+0x2C0 and at >= 290.0 (0x0056914C) sets obj+0x192 = 2, DAT_007DCD14 = 1, g_script_flags[0x14] = 1 and PlaySoundId(0x3A1BA9). The tail rides object path 0x178 by obj+0x2C0 through CamEvalObjectPath6, draws AssetDrawSlot(0xA6B), and registers its shot sphere at its own origin -- and it NEVER clears obj+0x34 bits 1..3, unlike the thirty routines that share the prologue.

g_class41_updates[76]. Original Mode only, expires on obj+0x11C step changes. The first hit pays, sparks and plays 0xF16A9; the branch then opens on either of two conditions -- the placer's byte at obj+0x194 is 1 and g_evt_block_index == 5, or g_evt_block_index == 0xE and the player carries original item 0, 2 or 0xB. Either writes g_script_branch_var = 2, latches obj+0x192 and 0x40000000, and plays 0x2116A9. It then runs 60 frames of g_pHingeCurvesXYZ -- a door swinging open. Two shipped spawns, stage 4 blocks 5 and 14, whose route records are {7, -1, 21} and {15, -1, 20}.
Releases item-set 1: a 0x378 object running ExtraLifePickupUpdate, one unit above the prop, turned to face the camera.

The extra-life pickup, drawn as asset 0x10C3. When shot it calls GrantExtraLife for the player who hit it, plays 0x3616A9, swaps to the floating award sprite (0x116A/0x119C with 0x1256/0x1257 above it) and fades out over 0x31 frames. BreakablePropAwardHit is called with 0 here, so the pickup itself pays no 10 points.

Releases item-set 3: a full 0x13F4 actor of character type 0x1C, whose skeleton slots all resolve to frog_gold.bin -- the golden frog. It is placed at the prop, turned to face the camera, and runs FUN_00471fa0 with FUN_00463f90 installed at +0x12EC.

Releases item-sets 2 and 5..8: a 0x378 object running ScorePickupUpdate with the set id as its kind, at the prop's position raised by g_item_pickup_y_offset[kind] and drawn with g_item_pickup_slot[kind].

The generic score pickup. On being shot it plays 0x416A9 or 0x3B17A9, awards g_item_score_table[kind], swaps to a floating score sprite (0x116A/0x119C), fades over 0x31 frames and despawns. Drawn as g_item_pickup_slot[kind] with a ground shadow at slot 0x10D0.
class 0x44, indexes the 18 builders at g_pPropBuilders

g_class44_subtypes[0], and the only selector-0 builder in the game: stage 1's two window/gate halves at evt 0x1580 and 0x15CC. ActorAlloc(ScriptFlagEffectUpdate, 0x378), obj+0x34 |= 0x51, then everything else out of the parameter tail and two literals. obj+0x28C = u16 tail+0x04 (the asset slot, which this family never draws through AssetDrawSlot(obj+0x28C) and which is only ever read as the branch below). The dword at tail+0x04 == 0x13F5 picks the pair: effect id obj+0x324 = 2 and capture bone obj+0x2A0 = 2, else effect 3 and bone 1. obj+0x328 = 0x1D7 (motion 471) always; obj+0x32C/+0x330 zeroed -- those four words are EffectDrawTree's {effect, motion, frame, prev} state block. obj+0x124 = 40.0f (the shot radius) and obj+0x14C = tail+0x08. No MatrixTranslate anywhere in the family: the spawn's own position is never copied to obj+0x19C and the effect's motion carries world coordinates.
selector 1, 37 spawns: one hinge from the parameter tail
selector 2: two doors at literal offsets (+/-9.29, 11.5, 22.68), slots 0x1794/0x1795, half a turn apart
selector 4, 13 spawns: as selector 1 with a per-instance scale and the flags at different offsets
g_class44_subtypes[16]. Allocates a 0x378 object running FallingContainerUpdate. Two spawns, both stage 2.

g_class44_subtypes[17]. Allocates a 0x378-byte object running StoryModeSwitchUpdate. Twelve shipped spawns across stages 1, 2, 3 and 5, and it is the branch writer with the widest reach: five of them stand in branch blocks.

The object PropBuildScriptFlagEffect allocates, and the whole of what class 0x44 selector 0 is. Three script-flag rules and a draw: g_script_flags[0x13] despawns it (ActorDespawn, not ActorKill); g_script_flags[0x12] steps obj+0x32C while it is below g_motion_play_length[obj+0x328] - 2; and the frame it lands on is matched against a cue list -- g_script_flag_effect_cues_a for effect 2 through the cursor at obj+0x2A4, g_script_flag_effect_cues_b otherwise through obj+0x2A8 -- each hit playing PlaySoundId(0x1816A9) and wrapping the cursor at the list's -1. The draw is gated on g_motion_slots[471].state == 2 (the literal word at 0x009A469C, which is that record's state half) and is EffectDrawWithCapture(obj+0x324, obj+0x2A0, -1): the effect tree at its own world coordinates, with the captured bone's matrix landing in obj+0x338 and copied on to obj+0x150. The three writes to obj+0x64/+0x68/+0x6C afterwards read EffectFrameRotations at the RAW cursor rather than the half-rate key, so past key 100 they index outside the motion block; nothing in this routine or in RegisterForShotTest reads them back.

shared by class 0x44 selectors 1/2/4. Swings on g_script_flags[open_flag] through g_pHingeCurvesXYZ (selectors 0/2/3) / g_pHingeCurvesYaw; transform is RotY(base); RotZ(rz); RotY(swing); RotX(rx). obj+0x1DC is read for its SIGN only here (TEST/JLE at 0x473EE6: ADD vs SUB on rx, NEG on yaw) -- its magnitude is the shot-wobble amplitude at IMUL 0x473FB5, and 4 of 56 hinges carry +/-512 or +/-416. obj+0x2C0 (the FMUL on the yaw) is 1.0f from every constructor; obj+0x1CC/0x1D4 are never written. Frame stops at 60, 130 on curve 4.

The object PlaceStoryModeSwitch builds, and the branch writer with the widest reach -- twelve spawns over four stages. Despawns when the g_script_flags byte at obj+0x2A4 is raised, or in scene 1 when g_script_flags[0x77] is. Everything else is behind g_GameMode == 1. Once obj+0x192 has latched -- which a hit, or PlayerHoldsOriginalItem for any of the four ids at obj+0x1FC/0x202/0x208/0x20E, or DAT_009A26EC does -- it runs 60 frames of g_pHingeCurvesXYZ. THE BRANCH: while the g_script_flags byte named by obj+0x2A0 is raised, a SCENE AND BLOCK TABLE decides -- scene 0 block 4, scene 1 blocks 1, 3 and 0xC, and scene 4 block 4 all write g_script_branch_var = 2 and then clear obj+0x2A0 to -1 so it fires once. Those five (scene, block) pairs are exactly five of the branch records whose live alternate is slot 2: stage 1 block 4 {6,-1,13}, stage 2 blocks 1 {2,-1,29}, 3 {4,-1,30} and 12 {13,-1,31}, and stage 5 block 4 {5,-1,6}. In scene 2 it also spawns story-mode items in blocks 2 and 4 and raises g_script_flags[0x15].

Class 0x14's Init, per g_class_handler_pairs (0x14 -> 0x00475E90). The stage-2 boss: character type 0x47 = boss2.bin, five spawns in the shipped scripts (stage 2 blocks 35/37/39/41, stage 5 block 3). Allocates a 0xBC-byte per-boss block with FUN_004A74E0(0xBC), stores it at obj+0x1310 and in g_class14_state, points g_class14_char at obj+0x194 and g_class14_xform at obj+0x40, seeds the phase state from the descriptor tail's byte +0x01 and the route quad from tail +0x10..+0x2C, increments g_enemies_present and g_enemies_alive, and installs Class14Update (MOV dword ptr [ESI], 0x476150 at 0x00476143).

Class 0x14's per-frame update. Re-seats g_class14_char/state/xform and g_cur_actor, runs Class14ResolveShotBone, dispatches g_class14_states[state+0x04] (CALL dword ptr [ECX*0x4 + 0x596218]), runs Class14AdvanceMotionAndPublishPoints, steers the boss along the descriptor's route quad with three Class14FollowSegment calls unless state+0x00 bit 0 is set, then Class14AdvancePhase and Class14UpdateAdaptiveRank. Despawns when g_active_cam_path equals tail+0x30 and g_cam_path_frame equals tail+0x32.

Class 0x14's shot handler, called at the top of Class14Update. Returns at once unless obj+0x34 bit 3 (MarkActorShot) is set; picks the shooter from bits 1 and 2, or a rand() coin when both or neither, clears bits 1..3, then finds the first entry of obj+0x190.. that names a bone and transforms that bone's matrix translation into world space. What it does with the point is [open] -- the routine ends on MatrixStackPop.

Class 0x14's damage routine, called once per player from Class14ResolveShotBone. Tests the shot ray against a cone seated on the boss's bone matrix at char+0x130 (FUN_004062A0), and on a hit subtracts g_class14_bone_damage[zone + rank*2] at 0x00596697 -- doubled in Arcade Mode, scaled by the weapon's multiplier in Original Mode -- from obj+0x11C, bumps state+0x97, and pays 10 points. At zero hit points it raises obj+0x34 bit 0x4000000, drops g_enemies_alive and pays 0x5DC. Then, unless the actor is already reacting or bit 0x2000 is up, it saves the state and sub into state+0x06/+0x07 and enters state 0x11 (Class14StateKnockedDown) if the boss is airborne in state 9, 12 or 14, and state 0x10 (Class14StateCuedMotion) otherwise. **This is the only route into either**, and therefore the only route to the three deaths and to every one of the class's twelve script-flag writes.

Called every frame from Class14Update. Advances the boss's motion (FUN_0041DC70, FUN_00411090) and steps the play cursor at char+0x00 unless obj+0x34 bit 0x4000 is set, then publishes six world points derived from the two arm matrices (char+0x244 and char+0x1D8) into 0x009A3504..0x009A353C, and computes two fpatan angles off char+0x190/char+0x1FC. Pure pose/attack-point work.

Moves an x/z position toward the line through two points by a given step, and returns 1 when it is already on the far side. Class14Update calls it three times over the descriptor's route quad, which is what keeps the boss inside its patch of water.

Class 0x14's phase ladder, called every frame from Class14Update. When obj+0x11C <= obj+0x11E * g_class14_phase_hp_frac[phase] and the state is 5, 6 or 7, it advances state+0x08: 0 -> 1 (state 10), 3 -> 4, 5 -> 6, 6 -> 7 and 8 -> 9 (all state 6). Phases 1, 2, 4, 7 and 9 are advanced or ended elsewhere. The phase is what picks which of g_script_flags 10..17 and 31 the boss raises.

Class 0x14's adaptive rank, g_class14_state+0x96, 0..15. Adds one whenever state+0x97 is positive and subtracts three (two while the state is 10 or 11) each time a player's life count at 0x009A5C66 + player*0x98 has fallen since the last frame. The rank indexes g_class14_summon_delays_a/b and g_class14_summon_counts.

g_class14_states[0] and [3] -- the entrance the stage-2 boss plays for descriptor states 0 and 3. Plays the rise-out-of-the-water clips, and when g_bHudShutterState reaches 1 it moves to state 5, latches the boss's position into state+0x10..+0x18, clears state+0x00 bit 0 and raises g_script_flags[10] at 0x0047835B. Descriptor state 0 leaves phase (state+0x08) 0; state 3 takes the shorter arm.

g_class14_states[1] and [4] -- the entrance for descriptor states 1 and 4, which is the full stage-2 boss fight. Same shutter hand-over as Class14StateEntranceA, raising g_script_flags[10] at 0x004785E4, but it leaves phase 3 rather than 0, so the fight runs the whole 3->4->5->6->7 ladder and raises flags 11..16 on the way.

g_class14_states[2] -- the entrance for descriptor state 2, which is stage 5 block 3's single spawn. It waits on g_script_flags[11] rather than raising 10, leaves phase 8, and hands over to state 5 on the shutter exactly as the other two do. This is why stage 5 block 3 gates on flag 31 alone.

g_class14_states[5] -- the fight hub. Turns to face the camera and picks the next move from the phase at state+0x08: phases 0, 3 and 8 close to 55 units and go to state 8; phases 2 and 9 need 135 units and a heading inside 0x1FFF and go to state 9; phases 5, 6 and 7 use the same test and go to state 12.

g_class14_states[6] -- closes on the latched target point at state+0x10. With state+0x9C zero it swims in until the point is inside 5 units and enters state 7; with state+0x9C one it follows the route quad and enters state 15 the moment Class14FollowSegment says it has left the segment.
g_class14_states[7] -- plays anim slot 8 state+0x60 times, one sound each, then returns to state 5.

g_class14_states[8] -- the melee. Drags the camera in over motion frames 0x1E..0x37, opens obj+0x34 bit 0x2000 at frame 0x37, and at frame 0x3C calls FUN_00415300(player, 1, 6) -- one point of damage. Returns to state 6 at the end of the clip.

g_class14_states[9] -- the leap at the camera. Launches on motion frame 0x23 with a speed scaled by the distance (a shallower factor in phase 9), damages the player through FUN_00415300 when it lands within 22 units of the ground, bounces, settles and returns to state 6.

g_class14_states[10] -- the phase-1 summoning round. Calls FUN_00438640(x, y, z, 100, 1) to place class-0x51 water enemies while g_enemies_alive is under 4, spacing them by g_class14_summon_delays_a[rank] and counting them out of g_class14_summon_counts. When the round ends with g_enemies_present == 1 it returns to state 5 and sets the phase to 2, which is the phase whose death raises g_script_flags[17].

g_class14_states[11] -- the phase-4 summoning round, the same shape as Class14StateSummonRoundA with FUN_00438640(..., 0x50, 2) and g_class14_summon_delays_b. Raises g_script_flags[11] at 0x00479C78 once the camera has settled, and g_script_flags[12] at 0x0047A264 after the swim-away, then goes to state 13 with the phase set to 5.
g_class14_states[12] -- the phase 5/6/7 leap. Launches toward the camera on motion frame 0x23, damages the player on landing, bounces once and returns to state 6.
g_class14_states[13] -- puts the boss 65 units to one side of the route's mid-line facing along it, plays anim 0x38 or 0x39 depending on state+0x9C, and returns to state 5.

g_class14_states[14] -- the leap the scripted break hands over to. Places the boss 60 units to one side, launches at the camera, plays a dialogue line at motion frame 0x2D and damages the player on landing, then returns to state 6.

g_class14_states[15] -- the between-rounds cut. Plays anim 0x24, moves the boss 40 units back, and then drives the camera itself with CamEvalPath7 over cp slot 0x6C or 0x6D. Raises g_script_flags[13] (phase 6) or [15] (phase 7) at 0x0047B153/0x0047B14B when the camera settles, and g_script_flags[14] or [16] at 0x0047B1D7/0x0047B1CE at path frame 0xA1. Phase 4 sends it to state 11 instead.

g_class14_states[16] -- plays the anim named by state+0x62 and then jumps to the state at state+0x06 with the sub-state at state+0x07. On motion frame 0x14 with obj+0x34 bit 0x4000000 set -- ResolveHit's hit-points-exhausted bit -- it enters the death for its phase: phase 2 -> state 0x12 and g_script_flags[17], phase 7 -> state 0x13 and flag 17, phase 9 -> state 0x14 and g_script_flags[31] (0x0047B458, 0x0047B46B).

g_class14_states[17] -- the knock-back. Launches the boss away from the camera, lands it, plays the get-up and returns to state 6. Carries the same death branch as Class14StateCuedMotion, at motion frame 0x3C: phase 2 or 7 raises g_script_flags[17] at 0x0047BA6E, phase 9 raises g_script_flags[31] at 0x0047BA5B.
g_class14_states[18] -- the phase-2 death, entered after g_script_flags[17] is raised.
g_class14_states[19] -- the phase-7 death, entered after g_script_flags[17] is raised.
g_class14_states[20] -- the phase-9 death, entered after g_script_flags[31] is raised. Stage 5 block 3's gate is this one.

Class 0x32's per-frame update, installed by Class32Init (MOV dword ptr [ESI], 0x47c960, bytes c70660c94700, at 0x0047F76F). Publishes DAT_009A26A0 = obj, writes DAT_009C8E10 = obj+0x11C / obj+0x11E as a float (0.0 when hp <= 0), adds 1.0 a frame to obj+0x138C and at > 18000.0 resets it and writes obj+0x131E = 0x10, then calls Class32OnShot (FUN_0047CC20) and dispatches g_class32_states[obj+0x1310] (CALL dword ptr [EDX*0x4 + 0x596738] at 0x0047C9E1). obj+0x1310 is the STATE word and obj+0x1312 the sub-state, the same pair classes 0x30 and 0x31 use. Afterwards it integrates obj+0x4C/0x50/0x54 into obj+0x40/0x44/0x48, aims obj+0x68 at the camera through FUN_004016B0, and draws through FUN_0047FE40.

Class 0x32's shot handler, called by Class32Update before the state dispatch. Gated on obj+0x34 bit 3; calls FUN_0047CD40 to charge the damage, and then, only while obj+0x34 bit 8 (0x100) is clear: if obj+0x34 bit 26 (0x4000000) is set it writes obj+0x1334 = 8 and obj+0x136C |= 2 and enters STATE 2 -- and 0x0047CC61 is the ONLY write of state 2 in the image, so the whole death chain 2 -> 3 -> 4 begins on the frame this actor's hit points run out. Otherwise, if obj+0x11C fell this frame, it writes obj+0x1334 = 8 and enters state 5, the hit reaction, once the drop passes a threshold: obj+0x131A == 1 counts obj+0x1368 down instead, and every other case compares obj+0x11C against (obj+0x11E / 10) * DAT_00596774[obj+0x1364 * 8]. Read while establishing what it would take to open stage 5's two wait_script_flag 30 gates: it is what says they cost a full enemy port and not a flag write.

g_class32_states[1] (0x0059673C), reached from Class32StateWaitCamAndFlags. Sub 0 sets obj+0x34 bit 8, calls FUN_00435E50(320.0, 35.0), writes the destination obj+0x13C0/13C4/13C8 = (579.0, -65.0, -8832.0) and obj+0x1330 = 0x91, and divides the remaining distance by those 145 frames into obj+0x4C/0x50/0x54 -- Class32Update integrates them, so the object arrives exactly as the counter runs out. Sub 1 counts it down; at zero it clears obj+0x34 bit 8, draws obj+0x131E from FUN_0040A8A0, zeroes obj+0x132C and obj+0x138C, sets DAT_009CA0EA = 1 and takes the state from the WORD at 0x00596770 -- the first of the per-state constants that follow g_class32_states, so the combat loop's entry is data and not a literal.

Class 0x32's Init, per g_class_handler_pairs (0x32 -> 0x0047F5F0). Installs 0x0047C960 as the actor's update function (MOV dword ptr [ESI], 0x47c960, bytes c70660c94700, at 0x0047F76F) and seeds obj+0x12EC = 0x0047F780 as the node-draw hook. This is the family that uses obj+0x131E as a 0..15 counter, which is a different field from class 0x30's compacted queue rank at the same offset.

g_class32_states[0] (0x00596738) -- the state Class32Init leaves the actor in, since it writes obj+0x1312 = 0 and never touches obj+0x1310. Five subs, all falling through: 0 sets obj+0x34 bit 14 (0x4000); 1 rides object path 0x180 by g_cam_path_frame (0x009A6110) into obj+0x40/0x44/0x48 and obj+0x64/0x68/0x6C once that frame passes 0x1A3, and waits for it to pass 0x256; 2 waits for g_script_flags[0x16] (22); 3 waits for g_script_flags[0x17] (23); 4 writes state 1. Stage 5's script sets both 22 and 23, so this actor is gated on the script and on the camera path rather than on the player.

g_class32_states[2] (0x00596740). Entered only from Class32OnShot at 0x0047CC61, on the frame obj+0x34 bit 26 comes up -- the hit points running out. Four subs: 0 sets obj+0x34 bit 8, plays 0xC23A9 and stops the BGM (PlaySoundId(0x80000000)), sets g_bHudShutterState = 3 and obj+0x1330 = 0x3C; 1 counts those 60 frames down and starts motion 0x8F through ActorSetMotionBlended; 2 waits for obj+0x19C > 0x1E, plays 0x1023A9 and loads obj+0x1330 from descriptor+0x2C; 3 loops the clip near its end, calls FUN_004805C0 every descriptor+0x34 frames, and when obj+0x1330 runs out writes state 3. The four subs FALL THROUGH into each other.

g_class32_states[3] (0x00596744), reached only from Class32StateDeathSequence. Sub 0 is the give-back: obj+0x131A = 0xFF, obj+0x34 = (obj+0x34 & ~0x4000) | 0x10100, motion 0x8E through ActorSetMotionBlended, FUN_0047FFC0, g_enemies_alive -= 1, g_enemies_present -= 1, the camera-tracking slot DAT_009A5EC0[obj+0x120 * 8] cleared, FUN_0047FFE0, PlaySoundId(0xC23A9), DAT_009C6F2D = 1, DAT_009C6F2C = 0, and the object put at (580.0, -35.0, -8832.855). It then falls straight through to obj+0x1310 = 4, obj+0x1312 = 0, so state 4 begins on the SAME frame. Sub 1 -- steer toward obj+0x13C0/13C4/13C8 at descriptor+0x28 a frame and hand to state 4 on arrival -- is [open]: nothing in this routine ever leaves obj+0x1312 at 1, and no other write of state 3 was found.

g_class32_states[4] (0x00596748). A five-sub scripted exit: sub 0 raises obj+0x34 bit 0x10000, sets g_script_flags[0x18] and yaw 0x8000; sub 1 holds until DAT_009A6110 == 0xAA; sub 2 calls FUN_004807B0 and clears bit 0x20 of obj+0x136C; sub 3 counts 0x78 frames; sub 4 counts 0xB4 frames, then MOV byte ptr [0x009C721E], 1 -- g_script_flags[30] -- calls FUN_00425F40 and ActorDespawn (FUN_00409CC0). Read while chasing who raises flag 30; it is not the raiser in stage 3 block 2, where the class-0x10 civilian's stream is.

Class 0x24's handler, and an Init rather than an update: it builds the actor and then installs one of six state routines as the object's own entry point. The parameter tail at obj+0x1390 carries everything -- tail+0x04 the character type into obj+0x1F4, tail+0x05 the state selector into obj+0x130C, tail+0x0A the motion into obj+0x1B4. obj+0x11C is an animation PHASE SEED, not hit points: -1 draws a random start frame, anything else starts the clock there, which is how a row of identical props avoids moving in lockstep. Selector 0 splits on tail+0x0C: zero gives SetPieceStateIdle, non-zero SetPieceStateHoldThenPlay.

Class 0x24 selector 0: play the motion and wait to be removed. Every state shares that removal test -- obj+0x34 bit 0x2000000 chooses between "g_script_flags[tail+0x06] is set" and "g_active_cam_path == tail+0x06 and g_cam_path_frame >= tail+0x08".

Class 0x24 selector 0 with tail+0x0C non-zero: count obj+0x1320 up to tail+0x0C frames, then install motion tail+0x0E through FUN_004119A0 and become SetPieceStateIdle. The one state where tail+0x0E is a motion id rather than a camera path.
Class 0x24 selector 1: plays from the start and freezes -- obj+0x1324 = 1 -- once g_active_cam_path reaches tail+0x0E at frame tail+0x10.

Class 0x24 selector 2: starts frozen (the Init sets obj+0x1324 = 1) and takes two cues. tail+0x12/tail+0x14 clears the freeze and starts it playing; tail+0x0E/tail+0x10 sets it again. Both are a camera path plus a frame threshold.

Class 0x24 selector 3: starts frozen and falls. Sub 0 zeroes the velocity, sub 1 integrates obj+0x5C -= 0.027222222, obj+0x50 += obj+0x5C, obj+0x44 += obj+0x50 until it reaches g_camera_fixed_eye_y, then clamps to the floor and clears the freeze so the animation plays. The same 0.027222222 half-gravity ActorArcVelocity uses. Freezes again on the motion's last frame, g_motion_play_length[motion] - 1.

Class 0x24 selector 4: slides. Sub 0 sets a 0x27-frame timer and a fixed velocity of (0.646266, 0, 0.613497); sub 1 adds it to obj+0x40/obj+0x48 each frame until the timer runs out; sub 2 waits a further 0x19 frames; sub 3 stops. Freezes on the motion's last frame.

Class 0x24 selector 5: holds until the motion frame passes 0x32, then drifts down under a much gentler 0.0034027777 until it reaches the ground plane. Unlike the other five its removal test has no script-flag variant -- it is always the camera path.

The per-frame body every class-0x24 state ends with: pose the skeleton through FUN_00411090 and, if obj+0x1324 is zero, advance the motion frame at obj+0x194 by one. So obj+0x1324 is a FREEZE flag -- non-zero holds the pose. Also carries two hardcoded set-piece effects for character type 0x55 and an extra drawn asset (slot 0x1382) for type 0x53.

Class 0x25's handler, and an Init: it builds the actor and installs ScriptedHumanoidUpdate as the object's entry point. Everything comes from the parameter tail -- tail+0x00 the character type, tail+0x02/+0x04 the removal trigger (cam path and frame, or a script-flag index when obj+0x34 bit 0x2000000 is set), tail+0x08 a model handle into obj+0x1304, and tail+0x0C a pointer to the COMMAND BLOCK. The block's header gives the opening motion at +0x04 and a phase seed at +0x06, -1 meaning rand()%10, and the commands start at +0x08. In Boss Mode character types 0x39 and 0x3A are remapped to the player's selected character through DAT_009A2242/DAT_009A2256. obj+0x124 is a per-character hit radius from the table at 0x004C4D28.

Class 0x25's bytecode VM, and the second-largest class in the game at 142 spawns. Walks 8-byte commands -- {s16 op, s16 mode, s16 a, s16 b}, or 16 bytes when the command carries a point -- running them until one blocks; a command that cannot proceed leaves the cursor where it is and falls through to the per-frame tail, so a run of setup commands all take effect in one frame and only a wait costs one. 19 opcodes: 0/1/4 wait on a condition (frame count, camera path+frame, motion frame, script flag, or the point test in mode 4) -- and 0 and 1 differ in what they leave behind: obj+0x1324 is set to the OPCODE, and that word is the freeze flag the draw routine tests, so op 0 lets the animation run and op 1 holds the pose. MODE 4 PROCEEDS WHEN THE ACTOR HAS MOVED AWAY FROM THE POINT, not toward it: 0x004845FD FCOMPP compares |prev-point| against |pos-point| and 0x00484601 TEST AH,1 / JZ 0x00484A7B blocks unless C0 is set, i.e. unless the PREVIOUS distance was the smaller one. Mode 2 on op 0 can never fire -- 0x00484386 tests the opcode itself and jumps to the blocked path when it is zero -- and no shipped command uses it. 2/3 set the motion (2 is ActorSetMotion plus a phase into obj+0x194, -1 meaning rand()%%10; 3 is ActorSetMotionBlended with b as the start cursor and MODE as the fade length), 5/6/7 turn, 8 sets the position, 9 and 16 swap models from per-character tables, 10 skips an arm to the next -2 unless the player count matches, 11 rides an op_ object path through CamEvalObjectPath6 on the CAMERA's frame, 13 plays a sound, 14 sets the hand-prop draw mode at obj+0x1330, 15 jumps, 18 is ActorKill and -1 falls into ScriptedHumanoidIdle. Op 17 is FIVE DIFFERENT THINGS and only three of them leave: mode 0 installs LAB_00484DF0, mode 1 FUN_00484EA0, mode 4 FUN_00484F90 (after obj+0x50 = -0.408); mode 2 calls FUN_00484F50 and mode 3 spawns sprite effect 0x41 sub-type 2 at a hardcoded point -- (-189.3, -24.9, -1505.0) in block 9, (-1264.0, -24.9, -1353.0) elsewhere, immediates c33d4ccd/c1c73333/c4bc2000 and c49e0000/c1c73333/c4a92000 at 0x00484A05 and 0x00484A1F -- and BOTH of those stay in the VM and run the next command. The per-frame tail runs the turn, the path follow and the draw.

What class 0x25's opcode -1 installs as the object's entry point (0x00484A87: MOV dword ptr [EDI], 0x484d40). It runs the cutscene-skip teardown on g_cutscene_skipping (0x009A2230), then the same removal test ScriptedHumanoidUpdate opens with -- obj+0x34 bit 0x2000000 chooses g_script_flags[tail+0x02] or g_active_cam_path == tail+0x02 at frame tail+0x04 -- and then ScriptedHumanoidDraw (0x00484FF0). AND NOTHING ELSE: no obj+0x1320 increment, no turn, no object-path follow, no obj+0x13C0 prevPos capture. So a class-0x25 actor that ends its program stops turning and stops riding its path from the NEXT frame on; the frame that runs opcode -1 still falls through the normal tail at 0x00484A8D.

Class 0x25's per-frame draw, called from the tail of every blocked command. Poses the skeleton through FUN_00411090 and then advances the motion frame at obj+0x194 only while obj+0x1324 is zero -- the same freeze flag class 0x24 has. It reads obj+0x1330 nowhere, but that does NOT make the field cosmetic: the reader is ScriptedHumanoidBoneDrawHook (0x00485260), the per-bone callback installed at obj+0x12EC, so op 14 really is a draw mode. It also draws a per-spawn decoration chosen by tail+0x06: 1 and 2 are fixed props at hardcoded points, 3 rides an op_ object path, and 4 draws only while g_active_cam_path is 0x93.

Class 0x25's per-bone draw callback, installed at obj+0x12EC by ScriptedHumanoidInit (0x004841AD writes 0x485260 into model+0x1158). Takes the skeleton node in EBX and switches on its bone index at node+0x14. obj+0x1364 non-zero with bone 2 calls FUN_00485BA0; obj+0x1330 == 2 or == 1 select which hand prop to draw, each indexing a 13-byte cel table (g_class25_bone_prop_cels / _alt) by (obj+0x1334 %% 13), adding the cel to a per-character asset-slot base (0x14B3/0x14C3/0x14DA/0x14E1/0x1273/0xD28/0xC3A/0x149D by character type) and drawing it through FUN_00418560, then incrementing obj+0x1334. This is the reader that makes obj+0x1330 a DRAW MODE for class 0x25 -- ScriptedHumanoidDraw (0x00484FF0) never reads it, which had been taken to mean nothing did. It also reads byte obj+0x131B and word obj+0x1F4. FUN_00485BA0 and FUN_00485D70 are [open].

Zeroes the per-player Original Mode block at g_original_item_slots, stride 0x14: both item slots to -1, +0x02 the player index, +0x03 1, +0x04 3, +0x05 5, +0x06 0, +0x07 0, +0x08 the magazine size 6, +0x09 the weapon kind 0, +0x0C 1.0f. This is what proves +0x08 and +0x09 are fields of that block and not two loose bytes.

Class 0x10, the civilian. ActorAllocSub(0xC4) at obj+0x1310; the descriptor tail at obj+0x130C gives the character type (+0x00), the g_civilian_scripts index (+0x01), the removal cue (+0x02/+0x04/+0x06), a part list (+0x08) and a child count and array (+0x0C/+0x10). Every child is SpawnFromDescriptor'd and parented at child+0x1394, and its hit points are scaled by g_hp_percent_by_rank -- those children are the zombies holding the civilian, and nothing in the evt instruction stream points at their descriptors.

Class 0x10's per-frame entry. Prunes dead children, runs the sub+0x5C frame hook, turns toward the target, steps op 0x26's move, counts the clip's loops, calls CivilianStepScript and re-enters CivilianRunScript when it says so, then the shot branch, the queued sound and the removal countdown. The shot branch pays -100 to the shooter (or to both on a killing shot), calls PlayerTakeDamageTimed and switches to the sub+0x4C script.

Class 0x10's other entry, installed when the descriptor's +0x22 is non-zero. Pushes the carrier object's (sub+0x68) translate/rotate around a call to CivilianUpdate, so the civilian rides it; when the carrier dies it copies the position out and swaps itself for CivilianUpdate.

Decides whether class 0x10's parked wait command is over, and if so walks the cursor to the next one. Every bit of the wait word is a REASON TO KEEP WAITING, so the conjunction reads inverted: it breaks out when all the reasons still hold. **LAB_0048B52E is one label reached from three places** and holds the tail all the arrival arms share -- the in-front test (bit 0x40, against the RAW sub+0x30..0x38 target, not the mode-resolved point the reach and turn tests build), then the camera cue (0x80) and the in-play gate (0x40000000), then the timer at sub+0x14. A word with neither 0x10 nor 0x20 jumps straight there; the 0x20 arm goes there when the heading error is not yet zero; the 0x10 arm goes there while the actor is outside sub+0x3C. Splitting that tail per-arm is a bug: a word carrying 0x40 alone then runs no test at all and only its timer can release it. On success it zeroes the target mode at sub+0x40 (LAB_0048B67E) before advancing.

Walks class 0x10's stream from one wait command to the next, applying ONLY the opcodes a wait condition reads -- the clip and its loop count, the target point, the timer, the three count goals, the camera cue, the frame hook and the script-flag index. A block CivilianStepScript skips still has to leave those in place; its sounds, dialogue and score are not conditions and are not run.

Class 0x10's action VM. Dword commands, per-opcode length, opcodes 0x00-0x2C; stops before any opcode above 0x2B and parks the cursor at sub+0x48. Op 0x2C loads the wait word (masking off 0x04000000) and, when it carries 0x10000000, pays ScoreAddForPlayer 400 -- to sub+0x6C's player, or to both when that is -1. That is the rescue award. Op 0x10 installs a native per-frame hook which decides its own command length. OPS 0x00 AND 0x01 CARRY THE ROOT-MOTION SWITCH: inside their 'is this a different clip' test they write model+0x64 bit 1 from bit 0x00100000 of the wait word -- (*g_cur_civilian & 0x100000) ? (model+0x64 | 2) : (model+0x64 & 0xfffffffd) -- which is exactly the gate SkeletonApplyRootMotion (FUN_00410C50) tests. So a civilian's clip carries her only in the blocks whose wait word asks for it: 289 of the 596 shipped wait commands set the bit, 297 do not, and the write happens only on a clip CHANGE. Op 0x27 is the only command that touches model+0x116C, storing its operand verbatim into that float field (one instance in the shipped scripts, 0x42480000 = 50.0); ops 0x1B/0x23/0x24/0x25 do not touch it. [proved] OP 0x1B IS THE HUD SHUTTER, and through it the firing gate: 'CMP dword ptr [0x009c8e98],0xA / JZ / MOV DL,byte ptr [ESI+0x4] / MOV byte ptr [0x009ca0f4],DL' at 0x0048BF0A-0x0048BF16 -- a BYTE store of the low byte of a dword operand into g_bHudShutterState, skipped only while g_app_state is 10. HudDrawShutterState (0x00413970) picks the change up on its next draw and raises g_nFiringGate for a 1 or drops it at the end of a 3, so a CIVILIAN'S SCRIPT CAN GIVE THE PLAYER THE GUN BACK inside a letterboxed scene. 60 of the shared table's commands run it, 30 with 1 and 30 with 3. That is what makes stage 1 block 1 step 8's wait_enemies_alive clearable: the script closes the shutter at step 6 and never reopens it, and the mauled civilian's own killed script does. [proved]

Class 0x10's pose step: blends the clip, takes the root translation off the pol file's own frame, and turns the body by the difference between two bone directions. Driven by wait-word bits 0x8000/0x10000/0x18000/0x20000/0x200000.

Class 0x10's per-frame turn, run by CivilianUpdate whenever sub+0x40 (the target mode) is non-zero. Resolves the target the same way the wait tests do -- the camera for mode -1, the actor's position mirrored through the camera for any other negative, sub+0x30..0x38 for a positive one, and for a civilian riding a carrier it pulls the point into the carrier's frame first -- then calls ActorTurnTowardPoint with a **literal 0x100** cap. It does NOT read sub+0x0E: op 3 writes that field and nothing in the turn consults it, so a port that passes it instead turns every civilian at the op's default of ten, twenty-five times too slowly.

Turn an actor's yaw toward a point by at most cap BAMS. Builds the inverse of the actor's orientation (-ry, -rz, -rx), transforms actor MINUS target through it -- that order, not target minus actor -- takes fpatan of the transformed x and z as a s16, clamps it to +/-cap and adds it to xform+0x28. It also writes the transformed point back over its second argument, so the caller's local is clobbered; no shipped caller reads it afterwards.

Compacts class 0x10's child array, dropping every child whose obj+0x34 carries 0x4000000 and remembering that child's obj+0x131C in sub+0x6C -- which is the player the rescue pays. Wait bit 0x04 blocks until the array is shorter than sub+0x20.
Op 0x13: grow class 0x10's held-item array by one and append the command's two operands.
Op 0x14: the same, but the first operand is whatever CivilianPickHeldItem last chose (sub+0x74).
Op 0x15: walk a {weight, record} list terminated by weight -1, pick one with rand() %% total, store it at sub+0x74 and preload its two assets. The second comes from a per-kind table at 0x0056B0F4.
Draws class 0x10's held items, each on the bone the character type's attach set (sub+0x82) names. Compacts the array when an item raises the wait word's 0x400000.

The only other per-frame pose hook in the program. Ramps the actor's radius (obj+0x128) toward a target and pushes it out of world collision along the hit normal. It does NOT rotate any bone -- see the note on upper-body aim in docs/formats/combat.md.

Plays the voice a shot civilian cries out. sub+0x81 selects directly; 0xFF picks by character type -- 0x24/0x25/0x2E/0x31-0x33 -> 0x2000001A, 0x21/0x22 -> 0x20000011, 0x26-0x2C -> 0x2000000B, 0x20/0x23/0x2D -> 0x2000000D, else 0x20000012. Those five ids are COM\\220_Y_M, COM\\209_M, COM\\190_Y_W, COM\\207_OLD_W and COM\\200_C -- which is what proves the class is civilians.
Op 0x10 hook: zero the y velocity, set obj+0x5C to -0.02722 and install CivilianHookFallStep. Consumes two dwords.

Per-frame: obj+0x50 += obj+0x5C, obj+0x44 += obj+0x50, and when QueryGroundHeightAt(x, y+100, z) is at or above the new height, snap to it, raise sub+0x18 (which wait bit 0x400 waits for) and uninstall.
Op 0x10 hook: install CivilianHookRideChildrenStep. Consumes two dwords.

Per-frame: averages the surviving children's positions and turns the civilian toward it with ActorTurnTowardPoint capped at 0x80 BAMS -- a facing, not a carry. Uninstalls itself once the object is flagged dead, and does NOT raise sub+0x18, so wait bit 0x400 never ends on this one.
Op 0x10 hook: take one dword as the launch y speed, raise obj+0x34 bit 0x80000 and install the fall step. Consumes three dwords.
Op 0x10 hook: take three dwords as a whole launch velocity and install the fall step. Consumes five dwords.
Builds the 0x1314-byte decal object a shot civilian leaves, scaled by how far below the camera plane the point is, and picks asset 0x132D or 0x132E by which player fired.

Class 0x26's handler, and an installer rather than a per-frame routine: it switches on the s16 at obj+0x11C (0..7, JMP [EAX*4 + g_class26_states]), calls the chosen update once and writes it into obj+0x00 as the object's entry point, so this runs exactly once per spawn. 0 -> FUN_0048E350, 1 -> St1VehicleUpdate, 2 -> Class26Subtype2Update, 3 -> FUN_0048F050, 4 -> FUN_00475A50 then FUN_0048F190, 5 -> FUN_0048F560, 6 and 7 -> FUN_0048F930. obj+0x11C is the subtype here and NOT hit points -- see docs/LESSONS.md L3.

Stage-1 opening vehicle (car_pl.bin + char_adv00.bin occupants). Picks its route from g_active_cam_path: cp_st1 0/1 (0x20/0x21) ride op_st1 0/1 at min(g_cam_path_frame, g_cam_path_length[slot]); cp_st1 1 clears the moving flag obj+0x1320 past frame 0x15D and stops re-evaluating. cp_st1 2 (0x22) does NOT ride a path -- it parks the car with CamEvalObjectPath6(0xFE, 350.0), a literal, and reads op_st1 2 (0xFF) only for rot_y, which becomes obj+0x1334, the occupants' yaw, minus 0x4000. obj+0x1330 gains 0x2000 a frame while moving and spins the two wheel pairs.

Class 0x26 subtype 2 -- what Class26InstallSubtypeUpdate installs for obj+0x11C == 2. Stage 3's is descriptor 3244, spawned at (0,0,0) with a zero orientation. First call only: ORs 0x51 into obj+0x34, copies **obj+0x1390 into obj+0x14C, sets g_carrier_object = obj (so class 0x30 state 29 can ride it), calls FUN_00409270 and bumps obj+0x1312. Allocates an object of param_2 bytes running param_1 and links it into the task ring. It zeroes exactly the first 0xD dwords -- the task header -- and writes eight header fields; everything from obj+0x34 up is left as FUN_004A7400 returned it, and that is a free-list split that does not clear. So a freshly allocated actor's body is the previous occupant's memory, which is why a thrown weapon's tumble rate at obj+0x135C has no authored value: neither SpawnThrownWeapon nor ZombieThrowHandWeapon writes it.

One frame of the task tree, depth first: the +0x24 child list, then this task's own handler through slot 0, then the +0x28 child list -- each walked from the head via +0x1c. ActorAlloc (0x004A6FA0) appends at the tail (+0x2c), so EXECUTION ORDER IS CREATION ORDER. That is what puts EvtInterpreterLoop before EvtRunQueuedActions every frame (created first and third by the scene task list at 0x00460710), and therefore what makes a camera action retired by CamAdvancePathFrame invisible to the script until the next frame.

Zeroes the actor from obj+0x34 to the end of the allocation, taking the size from the heap block header (uVar1 = -*(int *)(obj - 0x10) - 0x44). Run immediately after ActorAlloc by all three spawn allocators, which is what divides the struct: obj+0x00..0x33 is ActorAlloc's own task control block (+0x00 the update function, +0x08 a serial, +0x0C alive, +0x14 the free-list link, +0x18/+0x1C/+0x20 next/prev/list head, +0x30 a u16) and obj+0x34 onward is the game struct. No class may use anything below 0x34.

WalkMeshChainAndDraw(cmd, pass)  The NL1 mesh-chain renderer. cmd is a 0x1D-dword draw command; cmd[3] (+0x0C) is the model pointer and cmd+0x34 is a 4x4 world matrix, installed with SetTransform(D3DTRANSFORMSTATE_WORLD).  Called twice per command: pass 0 draws opaque meshes, pass 1 translucent. The selector is     is_translucent = (tsp_instruction & 0x180000) != 0x80000 i.e. a mesh is opaque only when IgnoreTexAlpha is set and UseAlpha is clear. DAT_007E7940 non-zero collapses both passes into one.  Per mesh: ComputeSphereVisibility on the mesh bounding sphere (dev+0x84); invisible or wrong-pass meshes are skipped with (mesh_data_size >> 2) + 0x14 dwords and only contribute their transformed Z to the sort key.  Per strip, from the strip control word (NOT parameter_control):     & 0x80  reuse previous global parameters -- skips the state change             entirely, so the strip's own bits 0-1 and 6 are IGNORED and the             previous strip's culling / shade mode stand     & 3     CULLMODE via g_CullModeTable = {NONE, NONE, CCW, CW}     & 0x40  SHADEMODE: 1 FLAT / 2 GOURAUD    <- per strip, not per mesh     & 8     triangle list (count is a triangle count) vs triangle strip     & 0x20  super index: records may be back-references, so each is copied             into a scratch buffer; without it the model's vertices are handed             to D3D directly as a contiguous array     & 4     sprite/quad -- NEVER TESTED. 23.5% of strips set it; it has no             effect in this port.  Submission is always     DrawPrimitive(D3DPT_TRIANGLESTRIP|LIST, 0x112, verts, count, 0) FVF 0x112 = XYZ | NORMAL | TEX1: 32 bytes, two f32 UVs at dwords 6-7, taken verbatim from the model file. There is no 16-bit UV path and no texture coordinate generation anywhere in this port.  The `global_flag & 0x10` branch (2-dword back-reference / 14-dword inline) is dead: no model in the game sets that bit.

SetMatrixMode(int mode)  OpenGL-style matrix mode selector over the stack at g_MatrixStackTop. DAT_007E7994 holds the current mode.      mode 3 = PROJECTION     mode 1 = WORLD / model  The commit happens on the 3 -> 1 transition:      if (mode == 1 && current == 3) {         SetTransform(D3DTRANSFORMSTATE_PROJECTION /* 3 */, g_MatrixStackTop);         memcpy(DAT_007E7948, g_MatrixStackTop, 64);   /* cached projection */     }     current = mode;  So the game builds its projection with the same push/identity/translate/ multiply API it uses for object transforms, then installs it by switching back to mode 1. This is the only place D3DTRANSFORMSTATE_PROJECTION is ever set.  The matrix API, all angles in BAMS (65536 = 360 degrees):      MatrixStackPush     0x004A9880   push (duplicates the top; NULL = copy top)     MatrixStackPop      0x004A9840     MatrixLoadIdentity  0x004A9E10   copies the identity at DAT_00571210     MatrixTranslate     0x004A9D80   row 3 += x*row0 + y*row1 + z*row2     MatrixRotateX       0x004A99F0   rows 1,2     MatrixRotateY       0x004A9AE0   rows 0,2     MatrixMultiply      0x004A92A0   top = top * M
